  • Apple is right now beta testing the third major update in the iOS 27 era, and anyone—developer and public tester alike—is free to install it at their leisure.
  • Industry observers note that with the second iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple is introducing face unlock for the iPhone Duo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, apple dropped iOS 27.2.1 last week, patching a handful of security vulnerabilities and bugs—including two iMessage flaws that let people read messages they shouldn't. But while most of us are running this version (or should install it as soon as possible), others are running something different—iOS 27.3.

Apple is right now beta testing the third major update in the iOS 27 era, and anyone—developer and public tester alike—is free to install it at their leisure. With it, comes the return of the Health app, vertical Safari tabs, and Siri AI app actions, among other fresh features. But for consumers of Apple's first foldable, the iPhone Duo, iOS 27.3 brings two rather notable changes—both of which are for the better.

Industry observers note that with the second iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple is introducing face unlock for the iPhone Duo. The foldable famously ships with Touch ID, the first new iPhone since the third-gen iPhone SE to do so. While that isn't a problem per se, many of us are used to unlocking our iPhones with our faces. This update just lets new Duo owners keep up with that muscle memory.

Now, take note: This isn't Face ID. No software patch can introduce new hardware, so the iPhone Duo still doesn't have the camera tech required to power Apple's Face ID system. As such, the Duo's face unlock is likely not as secure as Face ID on other iPhones. Perhaps that's why your iPhone Duo will require Touch ID for Apple Pay and passwords, or after 45 minutes of inactivity. This feature seems to be one of pure convenience: If you want to be able to unlock your Duo with your face (at least, some of the time), you can.

Industry observers note that what's more, this isn't a default setting. If you're running the beta, or if you're reading this after iOS 27.3 drops, you can find the option in Settings > Touch ID & Passcode.

Apple made a big deal about the continuity involved with opening and closing the iPhone Duo. As you do, your content moves with you seamlessly—a very Apple thing to do. That said, you might expect folding the Duo to lock it, but it doesn't. You need to hit the side button to actually put the phone to sleep.

In a recent development, iOS 27.3 changes that. If you so choose, you can enable a setting to lock your Duo whenever you close it. That won't work for everyone, of course—some consumers may still want to move between modes without worrying about locking their Duos. But for those who would rather lock their devices whenever they fold them up, the new option is under Settings > Display & Brightness.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I can't imagine Home Alone fans expected this much Kevin McCallister news ahead of Thanksgiving. Macaulay Culkin is reportedly returning to act in the franchise that made him a household name. But just minutes before that story hit amid the 2026 movie calendar, Chris Columbus, the director of the first two movies, was explaining why he didn't think another sequel could happen. And Columbus has a pretty heartbreaking reason for that.

In a recent development, per Variety, Columbus had no idea Disney was developing another Home Alone movie when asked about the franchise's future. Shortly afterward, reports surfaced about Culkin working with Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg on a new installment. The project is in its early stages, with Rogen and Goldberg shaping the script and producing through their Point Grey banner. Columbus, however, kept coming back to one person who helped make the original movie such a Christmas staple:.

Sources indicate that catherine, as I’ve always mentioned, is 50% of ‘Home Alone.’ There’s the yin and yang of ‘Home Alone’: Catherine O’Hara and Macaulay Culkin. Without those two in the film, there is no film, because they create the emotional epicenter of that film.

He's got a point. We all remember Kevin setting traps for Harry and Marv, screaming after putting on aftershave and eating a ridiculous amount of ice cream. But the first film also follows a frantic mother trying to get back to the child she accidentally left behind. That film's final reunion is still one of my favorite parts, and the late Catherine O'Hara, who played Kevin's mother, Kate McCallister, is at least 50% of why it works so well. O'Hara died in January at 71, and Columbus believes her absence would be impossible to overcome. As he explained:.

I think you potentially could still entertain the idea of doing another ‘Home Alone’ with the cast. Not any of these ridiculous follow-ups to the first. And I only say ridiculous because it’s weird with filmmakers. They don’t understand why that cast works so well. It’s always about the cast. It’s like ‘The Goonies.’ It’s about the cast.

Unfortunately, the reunion he pictured is no longer possible. That makes the timing of his interview particularly surreal. He continued:.

It was really about Catherine and Macaulay, if anyone ever wanted to do a sequel, and unfortunately that can’t happen now.

According to recent reports, as essential as O’Hara was to the success of the first two movies, the bumbling baddies also made the film unforgettable. I'm, of course, talking about the Wet Bandits, played by Daniel Stern and Joe Pesci. Columbus also wanted to make sure those two other actors got their due, adding:.

Let’s not downsize Harry and Marv. Daniel Stern and Joe Pesci are the ultimate comic duo for that particular film. Everyone has tried in subsequent sequels to be as funny or as interesting as Dan and Joe, and they just had a chemistry that is undefinable. So you can’t do that.

I can’t argue with the longtime filmmaker. The subsequent installments have struggled to reproduce the burglars' chemistry. Persci and Stern are hilarious in these iconic roles and not one single actor in any of the follow-up movies holds a candle to their performances in both of the first two movies. Getting hit in the face with a paint can is only funny so many times, but those two made it an art form.

Industry observers note that after Columbus directed 1990's Home Alone and 1992's Home Alone 2: Lost in New York, the series continued without Culkin in Home Alone 3, Home Alone 4, Home Alone: The Holiday Heist and 2021's Home Sweet Home Alone. None brought back the core pairing that Columbus considers essential, and you can feel their absence.

Reports suggest the film could follow Kevin's perspective as a dad, although no final story or additional casting has been confirmed.

Variety also noted that Columbus enjoyed Culkin's recent Home Alone-themed McDonald's commercial and would love to work with him again. When the outlet contacted him after the sequel news broke, though, he declined to comment further.

In a recent development, I'm curious to see what an adult Kevin McCallister looks like in a upcoming movie, especially with Culkin (who now watches the OG film with his own kids) involved creatively. I also understand why Columbus can't picture it without O'Hara. Anyone trying to bring Home Alone back has to contend with the fact that one of the people who made us care about Kevin is gone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After days of rumors circulating about Kate Middleton’s possible participation in the trip to India, confirmation came only at the last minute. This news came as a surprise in many ways, even though the princess’s presence was expected. Her involvement in this tour of India deserves attention, especially in light of the increasingly crucial role she plays alongside Prince William, who will be king. The trip to India, significant in its own right, also included an important meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, aimed at strengthening relations between the United Kingdom and India. This high-profile diplomatic meeting was added after it was confirmed that Modi would return in time from his trip to the Philippines.

The Prince and Princess of Wales arrive at the Earthshot ceremony.

Kate’s participation in the royal tour was made official by Kensington Palace only the day before departure to allow the princess to assess her condition right up until the last minute and determine whether she could handle such a demanding trip, following her recovery. But once she arrived in Mumbai, Catherine proved she was ready to do more than initially planned. The princess appeared, as always, impeccable and smiling—perhaps even more so than usual—in her customary understated and polished style. She greeted the crowd and met with people who had come to see her, participating in events alongside her husband.

It has been revealed that from the first day of this three-day tour—which began on the anniversary of their official engagement— Kate immediately displayed her characteristic good-natured spirit, evident in past tours as well, by joining Prince William in a game of gully cricket—a street version of the sport—alongside local children and teenagers. Serving as host was Sachin Tendulkar, an Indian sports legend whom the couple had already met during their previous visit to the country in 2016. The two princes put their skills to the test with little formality. They then took a ride on the Mumbai metro—a scene we’d already seen in London in candid photos when the Princess of Wales traveled on a bus in celebration of London Poppy Day.

The Princess of Wales at the awards ceremony.

The highlight was the awards ceremony in Mumbai on the evening of the second day, when the Princess of Wales unexpectedly took the stage to deliver a speech dedicated to the power of nature, health, and healing. Her speech was kept secret until the last moment, so much so that not even the celebrities and other guests in attendance knew the Princess of Wales would be speaking. “Nature is precious,” the princess stated. “We are not separate from it. We are part of it, deeply connected in ways both visible and unseen…the health of the planet and our natural world is inseparable from our own, and when it thrives, so do we,” she continued. “I have seen firsthand how nature has the power to heal and enrich our daily lives, but so much remains under threat.” “There will be good days and bad days, that it will take time.".

Industry observers note that catherine then presented the award in the “Protect and Restore Nature” category, dedicated to the protection and restoration of ecosystems. “The people we’re celebrating tonight are a huge part of that story. Their work will inspire and create seismic change that will improve lives for generations to come,” she stated.

The Prince and Princess of Wales at the awards ceremony.

Over the past three days, William and Kate have been busy meeting about sustainability, innovation, transportation, culture, and relations between the two countries. William is, in fact, assuming an increasingly prominent role on the international stage, supporting the United Kingdom’s diplomatic relations through his travels, which Middleton’s presence reinforced. This time, however, it was not simply a princess accompanying her husband on an official visit, but a woman who, after her illness and a long hiatus from major trips abroad, chose to return to her rightful role—and one the public has long expected her to fill.

The Prince and Princess of Wales with some Earthshot Prize winners.

It’s worth noting that this is the first time in four years—since her illness—that Kate has accompanied Prince William on an official overseas mission. The last such occasion was in December 2022, when the couple traveled to Boston, Massachusetts, for the Earthshot Prize ceremony. Her participation in the trip to India thus reflects her desire to gradually resume her international role, as well as her awareness of just how key her presence is to the monarchy.

It has been revealed that after her cancer diagnosis in 2024, Catherine prioritized her health and family, returning to public engagements without rushing things. However, her trip to Reggio Emilia, Italy, last May marked an important first step. On that occasion, she appeared visibly engaged and enthusiastic, and in subsequent statements, she hinted at her desire to travel more and gradually resume international engagements. “So I’m so glad it went well for her. I think she came back buzzing.” William said, describing his wife’s mood after that trip. Court circles had also hinted that Catherine wished to gradually resume a more active schedule.

The Prince and Princess of Wales at the 2026 Earthshot Prize ceremony.

Sources indicate that her return to work, however, was approached gradually, respecting the time needed for her recovery. It’s a journey that Kate herself described with great sincerity in a recent interview published last week in Country Life, a magazine for which Prince William served as guest editor. “I was told in hospital that my recovery would not be linear. There will be good days and bad days, that it will take time,” the princess stated, emphasizing that recovery does not necessarily proceed in a steady and predictable manner. India, therefore, did not come as a complete surprise. Rather, it was the realization of a desire that Middleton had already begun to express, and that the princess agreed to undertake such a demanding trip shows she felt ready to take the next step.

The Prince and Princess of Wales in India.

Before the trip, Kensington Palace issued a statement emphasizing how much the princess cares about her husband’s environmental initiative and how meaningful it was for her to return to participate in the ceremony in person. “She’s enormously proud of what he’s achieved, and it has been particularly special for them to experience this moment together. They are very much a team.”.

This refers to the project’s growth; since her last participation in Boston in 2022, it has significantly expanded its international reach and the impact of the initiatives it supports. “This year’s program in Mumbai promises to be the biggest and most ambitious yet, and she’s excited to see first-hand just how far some of it has come and meet some of the extraordinary people behind that success.” The spokesperson then recalled the couple’s previous trip to India in 2016, explaining that both have particularly fond memories of that visit. “The prince and princess are both really looking forward to what promises to be a fantastic week in India. They have such fond memories of their last visit together in 2016, and are excited to be returning a decade later.”.

In a recent development, as mentioned, the most key diplomatic event of the tour took place on November 18 in Fresh Delhi, where Prince William and Kate met with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. This was the only occasion during the visit when the royal couple left Mumbai, the city that hosted most of their scheduled engagements. Modi returned to the Indian capital specifically for this occasion after attending a major international summit in Manila, Philippines, to take part in the bilateral talks.

A spokesperson for Kensington Palace had emphasized the strategic importance of relations between the two countries, characterized by deep and ever-growing ties in numerous sectors, which include trade, investment, defense, security, technology, education, and culture. Kate’s presence alongside William during the meeting was considered particularly significant. “This meeting reflects the importance of that relationship, as well as the role their royal highnesses can play in celebrating and strengthening the ties between our two countries.”.

“For the prince, it also represents another significant engagement as he continues to take on a growing role on the international stage. We’ve seen him increasingly support the UK’s diplomatic relationships through his overseas engagements, and this meeting will provide an opportunity to build on those connections at the highest level.”.

The Prince of Wales on the Mumbai Metro.

Recent findings suggest that india, after all, holds a special place in the history of relations between the British monarchy and the Commonwealth. King Charles has visited the country numerous times, on both official and private occasions, strengthening a personal and institutional relationship over the years. For William and Catherine, however, this trip represented an opportunity to build a direct relationship with a nation destined to play an increasingly crucial role in the international balance of power.

A close-up of the Prince and Princess of Wales.

Recent findings suggest that with a population of over 1.4 billion people, India is now the world’s most populous country and one of the fastest-growing economies. Hosting the Earthshot Prize meant engaging a potentially massive audience on issues of environmental sustainability, resource conservation, and innovative solutions to combat climate change.

A beautiful image of the Prince and Princess of Wales.

For William and Kate, returning to India also meant revisiting a country to which they are bound by personal memories. As mentioned, their last visit was in April 2016, when the Prince and Princess of Wales—then the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge—undertook an official tour of India and Bhutan at the request of the British government. During that trip, they visited Mumbai, met with representatives from India’s cultural and sports communities, and traveled to Agra, where they admired the Taj Mahal.

Right in front of the famous mausoleum—a symbol of eternal love—William and Kate sat on the same white marble bench where, 24 years earlier, Lady Diana, Princess of Wales, posed during a visit to India. That photograph of Diana, portrayed alone in front of the monument, became one of the most iconic images of her public life. Taken in 1992, when her marriage to Charles was going through a deep crisis, many interpreted it as a visual representation of her loneliness. In 2016, William and Kate’s decision to recreate that shot inevitably brought Diana to mind, adding a personal and symbolic dimension to their visit.

It has been revealed that for Catherine, therefore, this trip is above all a new step on her journey back to public life following her illness. Not a demonstration of recovery to be celebrated as a race against time, but an opportunity to resume playing an important role while moving at her own pace. And to stand once again alongside William on a mission that concerns not only the future of the monarchy, but also that of the planet.

The Prince and Princess of Wales in 2016.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rachael Leigh Cook’s Laney Boggs got her happily ever after in She’s All That — but which of her former castmates does she want to cross over to Hallmark as her next leading man?

It has been revealed that “Dulé Hill is an incredible romantic lead,” Cook, 47, exclusively told Us while promoting her latest Hallmark rom-com, Double Booked for the Holidays. “Oh my God! Him in the movie Holes, I cry every time.”.

Recent findings suggest that she gushed over Hill, 51, and his leading man energy in 2003’s Holes, adding, “I cannot. So handsome,” telling Us she’s “probably” pick him to be her opposite on a Hallmark project.

While Hill portrayed Sam in Holes — who is not the lead, but does have a starcrossed romance — it was his role as cool kid Preston in 1999’s She’s All That where he first crossed paths with Cook, who played leading lady Laney.

Hill and Cook later shared the small screen on Psych when she guest starred as Abigail Lytar in several episodes from 2008 to 2010. Abigail was one of psychic detective Shawn Spencer’s (James Roday Rodriguez) girlfriends on the hit USA Network series, while Hill played Shawn’s BFF and sidekick Burton “Gus” Guster.

Sources indicate that in She’s All That, meanwhile, Laney falls for the boy next door, Zack Siler (Freddie Prinze Jr.). While trying to turn the quiet, art nerd into the next prom queen to win a bet, Zack catches feelings for his neighbor, and the pair spark a real romance.

In addition to working with Hill again, Cook said she’d tap Tamara Mello, who played one of her “tormentors” Chandler in the rom-com, to play opposite her in a Hallmark film.

The actress explained that Mello, 50, “Is actually a really good friend of mine, and she’s one of the funniest people I’ve ever met.”.

While fans might’ve guessed Cook would pick Prinze Jr., 50, to join the Hallmark family since they had such great chemistry in the ‘90s film, she told Us they already have something else on the books.

“Freddie and I are definitely gonna, we’ve already talked about doing something together again,” she teased. “So of course I want to work with him, but we already have something planned that’s not quite for Hallmark, so I don’t think I would drag him in quite on that plan, just to not distract from what we’re trying to do.”.

Fox Entertainment Studio confirmed in May 2025 that Cook and Prinze will reunite for The Christmas Affair, which has yet to receive a release date.

The pair will play “two famous sports broadcasters [who] bond over their cheating spouses during the holiday season,” according to the logline. “As they navigate the media frenzy and Christmas festivities together, unexpected feelings emerge — but timing isn’t always everything.”.

As fans wait for more on Cook and Prinze’s next collaboration, they can watch the actress in Hallmark’s Double Booked for the Holidays.

In the movie, Cook plays twins Abigail and Charlie, who agree to run a bookstore in Hay-on-Wye in Wales during Christmastime. Along the way, the pair dive into a decades-long mystery about the town’s most famous author and stumble upon not one, but two romances of their own.

Recent findings suggest that “I had a great time. I’m not gonna sit here and tell you that the world needed two more of me in a movie. Let’s be realistic,” Cook told Us with a laugh. “But I do know that no one was ever gonna call me up and say, ‘Do you want to play your own twin again?’”.

Wait, How Many People Left Can Actually Win Survivor 51?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that I’m not sure if you’ve noticed, but Survivor 51 is running out of main characters.
  • In a recent development, jeff Probst has said in the past that there’s no one size fits all winner’s edit on Survivor.
  • According to recent reports, I’m not saying the person who wins every season is the person with the most confessionals or the person with the most sympathetic edit, but one recurring theme is that the winner is always a consistent and active part of the narrative.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that I’m not sure if you’ve noticed, but Survivor 51 is running out of main characters. We’ve somehow lost four of the biggest, loudest and most vibrant personalities in consecutive weeks, and now, we’re suddenly left with a season that has a few main characters, a couple wacky side characters and a bunch of people who have been consistently deprioritized and underedited throughout the season. What is going on? How many of these castaways can actually even win?

In a recent development, jeff Probst has said in the past that there’s no one size fits all winner’s edit on Survivor. That’s both true and misleading. The longtime host and showrunner is correct in that the winner gets a different story based on their personality and what happened out there (the underdog, the challenge beast, the social threat, etc), but there is one very consistent pattern we do see: screentime.

According to recent reports, I’m not saying the person who wins every season is the person with the most confessionals or the person with the most sympathetic edit, but one recurring theme is that the winner is always a consistent and active part of the narrative. The show goes out of their way to give us their perspective on what’s going on because the ultimate payoff needs to feel earned and it needs to make sense. That’s just storytelling 101. If we want to know, for example, why someone on the jury does or doesn’t vote for them at the end, it helps if we’re given context and confessionals about their relationship.

Unfortunately, with nine players left in Survivor 51, there are a ton of players who just aren’t present enough in the edit to seem like viable winners. Seriously, let’s run them down real quick. Cristian has been a little more prominent lately, but he had two confessionals during the first four episodes combined. Despite allegedly being so close to Sharonda that he told her about Carter’s idol, we haven’t seen that relationship developed in the slightest. This season would make no sense if he won.

It also wouldn’t make any sense if Thien An won. She’s in last place in total confessionals amongst the players left by an absolute mile. Why? I have no idea. She seems to have great social relationships and is an engaging and sometimes cutting confessionalist when she does get a chance to speak, but she’s the least present character in many episodes for unclear reasons. Why would they do that if she won?

Sources indicate that mike and Eric have been much more present parts of the edit, but their storylines have both been about how much everyone else is annoyed with them. Eric has been getting a wacky theater kid edit that has included multiple montages of him talking and everyone else being annoyed by it. There have maybe been ten shots of characters literally rolling their eyes after he talks. Mike is a different version of the same situation. He’s been the subject of numerous confessionals from other players about how he’s a “bottom feeder” and impossible to work with. I don’t see why Survivor would portray its winner that way.

That’s four of the remaining nine players who have seemingly no chance, and I’m not sure Maggie is in a good spot either. She seems to be one of the most well-liked and dangerous players on the entire island. No one would vote for Mike during the Duos Challenge because he was paired with her, and Jelly has dropped confessionals about how she can win if she gets to the end. But the edit also gave her very little credit for Linnea, even though it was her strategy, and she has just over half as many confessionals as Jelly does (24 to 46).

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

That leaves literally four players: Jelly, Devin, Sharonda and Carter. I’d normally write Carter off because he has two episodes with zero confessionals and no player since Survivor 41 has won with even a single zero confessional episode, but as you can see, we’re a little short on viable winner possibilities. I’m out here trying to make excuses for people’s edits and see some silver lining showing why they could win. I think Carter can win. He’s at least been pretty present during the majority of the season. We’ve gotten his viewpoint consistently, and we’ve gotten confessionals from other people that speak of him very highly.

It has been revealed that so, yeah, Carter is a maybe, but really, that leaves us with Jelly, Devin and Sharonda. The Helicopter Alliance has been the most consistent narrative throughline of the entire season, which is why it makes sense that these three are at the top of the list. Jelly and Devin have, without question, been the main characters of 52 (at least since Brady left), and they’re dominating in screentime and confessionals at 46 and 45 respectively. That’s twelve more than Eric, who is in third place of those remaining thanks to a bunch of vampire analogies and references to his fiance Gina.

Sharonda is quite a bit behind with 29 confessionals. Like Carter, there are some concerns with her edit, as there have been stretches where she hasn’t been super prominent, but her content has been so overwhelmingly positive that I’m willing to give her a pass. I still consider her a very viable winner at this point, as she should come into further prominence in the edit once the other players find out she’s been secretly working with Devin and Jelly the entire time.

According to recent reports, I don’t know who is going to win Survivor 52. There are three, maybe four viable candidates with Maggie and maybe Mike added in there as wild longshots. That’s a really small number of people in play for there being nine castaways left. In fact, it’s starting to feel a little like Survivor 49 where the entire fanbase was convinced one member of the Tres Leches alliance was going to win because they were the only people who seemed viable for like the entire second half of the game (apart from maybe Steven I guess).

Lack of winning edits aside and a few questionable twist-related decisions aside, Survivor 51 has been an absolute banger so far. Fingers crossed it’s able to stick the landing and fulfill its potential to be an all-time great season, whether one of these obvious contenders wins or not.

The Body is available to stream right now with a Netflix subscription, and when I learned it was about controversy surrounding a Catholic school, I had to check it out. As someone who attended a Catholic grade school and high school, I was eager to see how it was portrayed, and while things were a bit wilder than I remember, the show really nailed two parts.

According to recent reports, for those curious but still want to watch for themselves, I'll keep this spoiler-free. All readers really need to know going in is that this series surrounds a Catholic school dance team, and what happens when an initiation prank goes too far and a student's life is in danger.

Recent findings suggest that project Hail Mary was called "blatant Catholic propaganda," as described by someone who never watched, and similarly, The Body is being vilified by groups of concerned Catholics who have not and likely will not watch it. As someone who did, I'll admit no one should go into this assuming it'll be a family-friendly adventure, but the parts that handle religion are done with lots of care.

According to recent reports, I say this, especially, as a person who went through their teenage years in Catholic school. For many, your teens are going to be one of the most rebellious and potentially dangerous times of your lives. Imagine some of the wildest things you did in high school, and now imagine the feeling that you'll be eternally damned for it days afterward.

"Catholic Guilt," they call it, is shown in full effect in The Body. Obviously, there are people in this who deserve to feel guilty, but there are also cases in which we see characters feel immense guilt or shame for things that would otherwise be quite normal today.

Some of this is due to The Body being set in 2004, when things like LGBTQ+ relationships weren't as prevalent in pop culture and were largely frowned upon in Catholic schools. Pregnant teens at my high school weren't allowed to walk to get their diploma at graduation, and I couldn't imagine what would happen if someone were openly gay back then.

It has been revealed that and yet these things happened, and these people existed. It's one of the things I love about The Body, and the way it navigates what would undoubtedly be a scary time for those individuals. Again, it was more extreme than anything I dealt with, but I know that feeling of guilt quite well.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

I also think The Body does a great job of handling what goes down when something controversial does happen at a Catholic school. I can't get into specifics, but there was a controversy at my school so massive that it received national attention, and the fact that it was a Catholic school only amplified the interest and headlines.

Sources indicate that the Internet Can’t Stop Talking About People’s Mouths In Netflix’s The Christmas Switch. I Can’t Unsee It.

Like the kids in The Body, a number of kids attending were from families of some renown. Families were willing to keep quiet about events occurring to protect their children, and the school was eager to let any controversy fade as quickly as possible.

In a recent development, there's certainly something to the added pressure of a Catholic school striving to be perfect. As The Body points out, any controversy draws the same critics who will immediately point to past incidents highlighted by the movie Spotlight. No one wants to be the person to bring added negative attention to the religion, but at the end of the day it's a high school full of rowdy teens just like any other.

I'm admittedly a lapsed Catholic, but I would say The Body was the best representation in media for the faith since Wake Up, Dead Man. In that, both deal with Catholicism, but not so much that they're openly mocking or blaspheming it. They're stories about the people who practice it, who are imperfect and flawed. I don't think teachers should show it in class, but it is worth a watch for those who are curious.

Recent findings suggest that check out The Body and other upcoming Netflix shows as 2026 winds down. With the holidays right around the corner, there's nothing like watching something controversial to spark some conversation at the family dinner table!

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has finally arrived, and, to the surprise of no one, it's putting up some big numbers that speak to the pent-up demand.
  • Recent findings suggest that for starters, the internet service provider Comcast revealed that November 18--the final day of preloading--was the busiest day in the tech giant's history in terms of demand.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has finally arrived, and, to the surprise of no one, it's putting up some significant numbers that speak to the pent-up demand. GTA 6 sold more than 30 million copies and hit almost $4 billion on day one, but that's just the start of understanding the impact of the game's release. For starters, the internet service provider Comcast revealed that November 18--the final day of preloading--was the busiest day in the organization's history in terms of demand. Peak traffic was 31% higher than an average day and a full 9.6% higher that the previous biggest day ever for traffic to Comcast's network. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ble-JJxBBGA GTA 6 also now holds five of the top 10 busiest days of Comcast's network of all time. Going further, Comcast stated around 24% of all internet traffic on Comcast's network was people downloading or playing GTA 6 on November 18 (no doubt thanks to the Fresh Zealand trick). Additionally, traffic to Twitch on Comcast's network was up by almost 50% and "is still increasing," Comcast said. A spokesperson for Comcast further contextualized the traffic data, telling GameSpot that between when preloading began on November 10 and through November 18, PlayStation and Xbox traffic pushed enough data on the network for one million homes to stream The Odyssey in 4K repeatedly for two days straight. Comcast was among the internet service providers that offered free speed boosts to subscribers to help them download GTA 6 faster. Additionally, Mat Piscatella of Circana shared data that speaks to the enormity of GTA 6's launch on PlayStation and Xbox. For active accounts November 19 in the US, 61% of PS5 accounts "engaged with" GTA 6. On Xbox, 56% of Xbox players globally did. PS5 players averaged 513 minutes of play for GTA 6 on November 19, compared to 494 on Xbox. These daily active user and minutes played figures are "absolutely bonkers," Piscatella said. GTA 6 was No. 1 on November 19, pushing Fortnite down to No. 2 based on these engagement metrics, Circana said. For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first. And if you’re eager for news on GTA 7? Get comfortable, because Rockstar is not going to announce it anytime soon.

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has finally arrived, and, to the surprise of no one, it's putting up some big numbers that speak to the pent-up demand. GTA 6 sold more than 30 million copies and hit almost $4 billion on day one, but that's just the start of understanding the impact of the game's release.

Recent findings suggest that for starters, the internet service provider Comcast revealed that November 18--the final day of preloading--was the busiest day in the tech giant's history in terms of demand. Peak traffic was 31% higher than an average day and a full 9.6% higher that the previous biggest day ever for traffic to Comcast's network.

GTA 6 also now holds five of the top 10 busiest days of Comcast's network of all time. Going further, Comcast stated around 24% of all internet traffic on Comcast's network was people downloading or playing GTA 6 on November 18 (no doubt thanks to the Upcoming Zealand trick). Additionally, traffic to Twitch on Comcast's network was up by almost 50% and "is still increasing," Comcast said.

A spokesperson for Comcast further contextualized the traffic data, telling GameSpot that between when preloading began on November 10 and through November 18, PlayStation and Xbox traffic pushed enough data on the network for one million homes to stream The Odyssey in 4K repeatedly for two days straight.

Comcast was among the internet service providers that offered free speed boosts to subscribers to help them download GTA 6 faster.

In a recent development, additionally, Mat Piscatella of Circana shared data that speaks to the enormity of GTA 6's launch on PlayStation and Xbox. For active accounts November 19 in the US, 61% of PS5 accounts "engaged with" GTA 6. On Xbox, 56% of Xbox players globally did. PS5 players averaged 513 minutes of play for GTA 6 on November 19, compared to 494 on Xbox.

It has been revealed that these daily active user and minutes played figures are "absolutely bonkers," Piscatella stated. GTA 6 was No. 1 on November 19, pushing Fortnite down to No. 2 based on these engagement metrics, Circana said.

For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first. And if you’re eager for news on GTA 7? Get comfortable, because Rockstar is not going to announce it anytime soon.

Bryan Cranston Co-Created One Of Prime Video's Best Crime Shows

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that once upon a time, Bryan Cranston teamed up with "House" creator David Shore to develop the pilot for "Sneaky Pete," a crime comedy series starring Giovanni Ribisi.
  • Masquerading as Pete, Marius moves in with Pete's actual family, who haven't seen Pete in so long that they assume that Marius is the real deal.
  • Industry observers note that including the 2015 pilot, "Sneaky Pete" went on for 30 episodes spanning three seasons and wrapped up in 2019.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that once upon a time, Bryan Cranston teamed up with "House" creator David Shore to develop the pilot for "Sneaky Pete," a crime comedy series starring Giovanni Ribisi. The premise of "Sneaky Pete" is very amusing: Ribisi plays Marius Josipović, a con man who, upon being released from prison, finds that he instantly has to go on the run, as he's being hunted by Vince Lonigan (Cranston), a vicious crime lord whom he stole money from. To avoid detection, Marius assumes the identity of his old cellmate, Pete Murphy (Ethan Embry).

Masquerading as Pete, Marius moves in with Pete's actual family, who haven't seen Pete in so long that they assume that Marius is the real deal. Marius, meanwhile, heard so many of Pete's stories about his loved ones that he reckons he can pull off the switcheroo. Pete's family includes his grandmother and grandfather Audrey (Margo Martingale) and Otto (Peter Gerety), along with his three cousins: Julia (Marin Ireland), Taylor (Shane McRae), and Carly (Libe Barer). One of those cousins proves to be very attractive to Marius, too, which, obviously, is something he can't act upon, lest the show get awkward very promptly.

Industry observers note that including the 2015 pilot, "Sneaky Pete" went on for 30 episodes spanning three seasons and wrapped up in 2019. The show follows Marius on his various misadventures, whether that means helping Pete's messy family or reconnecting with people from his own past. The late and much-missed Malcolm-Jamal Warner plays Marius' parole officer, while Marius' brother Eddie is portrayed by Michael Drayer. On the whole, it's quite well-liked and is generally ranked among Prime Video's best crime series.

A panoply of interesting performers lend their talents to "Sneaky Pete" over the course of its run. The late magician Ricky Jay eventually appears on the series, as do M. Emmet Walsh (one of the true character actor greats) and Rory Culkin. Sharp-eyed video game fans may also recognize Steve Wiebe, one of the central "Donkey Kong" competitors in the celebrated 2007 documentary "The King of Kong: A Fistful of Quarters.".

The show's setup, as one might assume, leaves viewers wondering how long Marius will be able to keep up the charade. Like "Dexter," a series about a secret serial killer, "Sneaky Pete" is predicated on how well the lead character can keep their true identity hidden. Late into the show's first season, cousin Carly becomes suspicious of Marius, forcing him to visit Pete in prison to get some more family info. I failed to mention earlier that Pete's family runs a bail bonds business, which put them into the regular company of unsavory individuals. Thus, there's a lot of drama over Pete's family's finances and how things ought to be run. From there, many episode plots became comedic crime misadventures, with stories involving double-crosses, significant piles of money, kidnappings, and cons.

In 2016, it came to light that "Sneaky Pete" co-creator David Shore had stepped away from the show after the pilot had aired, with Graham Yost taking over as showrunner. At that point, Yost had created the hit Western series "Justified," so it was clear that "Sneaky Pete" was in good hands. Meanwhile, in addition to co-creating the series, Bryan Cranston directed the eighth episode of Season 1, "The Roll Over.".

Taken as a whole, all three seasons of "Sneaky Pete" were well-reviewed by critics. Writing for the Los Angeles Times, Lorraine Ali described the show's first season as "a smart, riveting, and often tense ride through a complicated web of family, crime, and everything that should (but doesn't) separate the two." Reviewing Season 1 for Vulture, Jen Chaney similarly noted that it's fun watching people lie to other people, a wicked conceit that makes "Sneaky Pete" an easy series to watch in a single go. To be sure, there's a good deal of tension driving its plot, Chaney observed, and the show's lead yanks us along in a fun way. As she put it:.

"There's [...] an edginess to Marius/Pete, an awareness that he's one false sleight of hand away from going back to the slammer or, worse, getting killed, that mirrors the ratcheting tension in the series. There are some brilliantly executed scenes in episode three, for example, that go all the way toward the moment when it would seem that the gig is up, then turn another way and allow the audience to exhale before some other calamity presents itself.".

All three seasons of "Sneaky Pete" are waiting to be discovered on Prime Video, and it seems to be something Bryan Cranston feels good about. The "Malcolm in the Middle" and "Breaking Bad" veteran has yet to hang up his hat, of course, so who knows what other tricks he may yet have up his sleeves.

Christmas in July? Why Stop There?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (788 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Why do we let something like the calendar dictate our holidays?
  • Instead of condensing so much effort and so much merriment into such a ludicrously small window at the very end of the year with nothing but the bland hell of winter ahead of us, let’s maximize our time by stretching it out.
  • If the holiday season has wrapped by February 14, the weeks following are the shoulder season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Why do we let something like the calendar dictate our holidays? The fact that Thanksgiving and Christmas are just four weeks apart means by the time you’ve returned from November family visits, unpacked, shopped, decorated, done the party circuit, bought gifts, and maybe—maybe—worked for a few days, you have to turn around and celebrate again. It’s exhausting and expensive and too warp-speed to feel like that much of a good time. I’m not arguing to ban Christmas—which I am using as a catchall for nondenominational winter holidays, however that looks to you—what I am proposing is, in fact, much more exciting. I think we should switch the dates of Christmas and Valentine’s Day.

Consider it! Instead of condensing so much effort and so much merriment into such a ludicrously small window at the very end of the year with nothing but the bland hell of winter ahead of us, let’s maximize our time by stretching it out. Valentine’s Day is for romance, whether that means watching Bridget Jones’s Diary with friends, eating overpriced meals at candlelit restaurants, making cards, or mainlining chocolates. So on December 24, celebrate platonic love with friends—à la Galentine’s Day, except we should think of a better name—and maybe go on a date on the 25th. If that date goes well: bam! You now have a plus-one to a Upcoming Year’s Eve party and a midnight make out partner.

If the holiday season has wrapped by February 14, the weeks following are the shoulder season. Life is slow. But by the time everyone trickles back home from watching Die Hard in their pajamas or shopping post-Christmas sales or going to the gym, you only have to survive one month until the sweet relief of spring in late March. Nothing makes more sense for how to survive the long nights and cold of winter.

In a recent development, so we go all-in on spring. Mid-April is when it likely won’t snow again; around then you no longer need heat—at least in New York City—so let’s make that a national holiday celebrating warm weather with seasonal bouquets (tulips, lilacs, peonies), foraged ramps, and maybe specials on dry-cleaning winter coats or sales on shearling boots.

But why stop there? We in America could take a page from France, where May can have four(!) public holidays as a kind of summer practice run. I’d be more than happy to celebrate VE Day in solidarity: Liberté, égalité, holiday! In our version, maybe botanical gardens will be free to the public for picnics. Maybe amusement parks will be gratis? Maybe lobster rolls and strawberry shortcake will be handed out on the street? Can the first summer blockbuster of May be an annual event with free popcorn? This month of long weekends will culminate in Memorial Day barbecues, which is a perfect bookend to summer with Labor Day—no notes.

Let’s keep summer luxurious, so summer Fridays will not be at the discretion of employers but mandated by the government for those three months. The Fourth of July can stay where it is with the caveat that if it rains, we get to observe it on the next day forecast for hot dog weather. Nothing notable happens in August—phone it in, federal holiday or not. Labor Day stays, of course. The week following it in Upcoming York is Fashion Week, which runs concurrently with the US Open for tennis—very busy but very social. We’re going to adopt that nationwide as a festive season soft launching the country into fall.

And finally, let’s turn our attention to that somber stretch of time between early September and Thanksgiving. We don’t get enough time off, so we will move Presidents’ Day from February to mid-October for another much-needed holiday. Then cook a major turkey dinner on Thanksgiving, see your extended family, watch football, whatever, and delight in the fact that you don’t have to do it again until February. But start figuring out your Valentine’s Day dates now—those prix fixe dinners with chocolate lava cakes really book up fast these days.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it doesn't matter how many movies Pixar makes, the studio's biggest achievement will forever be the "Toy Story" franchise. To be sure, there's a reason several "Toy Story" films rank among Pixar's highest rated movies on Rotten Tomatoes, as the animated property has endured for decades and continues to resonate with audiences. Even now, the very first "Toy Story" flick remains the standard for Pixar films (and not just because it launched a reliable hit-maker at the box office).

In addition to establishing Pixar as an animation studio worth paying attention to, 1995's "Toy Story" marked the arrival of 3D computer animation. It's essentially to animation what "Jurassic Park" was to visual effects, signaling a change from what had come before cinematically. At the same time, "Toy Story" is fairly small in its scale, which is a testament to just how well its story and characters work. It's not about grand adventures with huge set pieces, it's a simple tale about a cowboy toy learning to accept change in his life and a space ranger toy realizing he's not who he believed he was (and that's okay).

Sure, the animation in "Toy Story" shows its age nowadays, yet the film itself feels as groundbreaking as it ever did, serving up lots of fun sequences and clever ideas in a narratively tight package. Then there's its cast, anchored by Tom Hanks and Tim Allen as Woody and Buzz Lightyear, who really make their characters feel alive. It's no wonder the movie became such a monumental success, establishing computer animation as more than just a gimmick in the process.

And let's not forget: It's extremely quotable as well, with one of Buzz's most famous line (besides, of course, "To Infinity and Beyond!") being the best example.

Sources indicate that buzz memorably delivers his line near the end of "Toy Story" as he and Woody desperately try to catch up to their owner Andy (John Morris) before he and his family move away to their fresh home. Problem is, Buzz is strapped to a substantial firework taped to his back. (It's a long story.) So, as a last resort, Woody lights the rocket, which sends the duo straight up the air. Fortunately, just before the rocket blows up, Buzz activates his suit's wings, freeing him and allowing him to hold Woody as the two safely glide through the sky to reach Andy and his family in their car.

It has been revealed that it's in this moment that Woody marvels at Buzz's ability to fly, having previously mocked him for claiming he could do so when he couldn't. But Buzz corrects his partner, declaring, "This isn't flying. It's falling with style!" (itself a callback to one of Woody's quips from earlier in the movie).

Industry observers note that altogether, it's a terrific sequence that solidifies Buzz's character arc and the film's core themes all in one go. Having awakened and gained sentience, Buzz is now embracing the fact that he is actually a toy and not a real spaceman. But again, that's okay, as he's found a latest purpose in being Andy's toy. "It's falling with style" really is the perfect encapsulation of the beating heart of "Toy Story" and why the characters of Woody and Buzz have endured for so long. They go from being bitter enemies to the best of friends as they embrace what makes toys special.

"The word I'm searching for — I can't say, because there's preschool toys present." — Woody.

"One minute you're defending the whole galaxy, and, suddenly, you find yourself sucking down darjeeling with Marie Antoinette ... and her little sister." — Buzz Lightyear.

In a recent development, "You are a sad, strange little man, and you have my pity. Farewell." — Buzz Lightyear.

It has been revealed that "Look, over there in that house is a kid who thinks you are the greatest, and it's not because you're a Space Ranger, pal, it's because you're a toy. You are his toy!" — Woody.

"I'm from Mattel. Well, I'm not really from Mattel. I'm actually from a smaller tech giant that was purchased in a leveraged buyout." — Rex.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that east Asia--and particularly Japan--has been suffering a rash of cybersecurity incidents as of late, affecting everything from major banks and cellphone service providers to city governments and small businesses.
  • Industry observers note that east Asia--and particularly Japan--has been suffering a rash of cybersecurity incidents as of late, affecting everything from major banks and cellphone service providers to city governments and small businesses.
  • One recent incident involved the PC launcher for the popular gacha action shooter NIKKE: Goddess of Victory, where malicious code would install a trojan called k2f that would compromise an individual's PC, taking screenshots, logging inputs, and installing/executing programs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that east Asia--and particularly Japan--has been suffering a rash of cybersecurity incidents as of late, affecting everything from major banks and cellphone service providers to city governments and small businesses. Gaming has been one of many areas targeted: between arcade games on Sega's network going offline, 11 million Capcom IDs being compromised, and a high-schooler hacking Bandai-Namco, some major publishers have been suffering a string of embarrassments. One recent incident involved the PC launcher for the popular gacha action shooter NIKKE: Goddess of Victory, where malicious code would install a trojan called k2f that would compromise an individual's PC, taking screenshots, logging inputs, and installing/executing programs. Unfortunately for one Japanese municipality, someone's gacha habits may have lead to a much bigger incident. Iwamizawa is a city of about 75,000 located in Hokkaido, Japan's northernmost island. It's not a place that makes a lot of news, but it recently went viral on the Japanese-speaking side of social media. As reported by Automaton, the city issued a notice that an IT sub-sub-contractor handling the city's fixed asset records suffered a security breach--specifically, a k2f hijack. Observers soon surmised that the most likely source of k2f would be someone playing a certain sexy gacha game on a work PC. The subcontractor in question, IT services tech giant GIS Hokkaido, would then confirm to Japanese tech news site ITMedia that, yes, NIKKE's compromised PC launcher was the source of the problem. When asked if an employee or subcontractor had debuted the game on a work PC, GIS politely replied that "they would prefer not to comment." Moral of the story? While there's nothing wrong with playing a suggestive gacha game on your own time, you probably shouldn't do it on the clock, and definitely not on a company PC, lest you become internet meme fodder.

Lesley Manville, Pierce Brosnan, and More Celebrate Violinist Joshua Bell at the Langham London

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that at the age of four, Joshua Bell was given his first violin, and he hasn’t put it down since.
  • It has been revealed that today, the Grammy Award–winning musician is one of the most celebrated classical violinists of his era.
  • That kinship was solidified over coupes of Champagne and hand-dived Orkney scallops, with the hotel celebrating Bell, a “Langham Luminary,” in its London ballroom packed with writers, artists, designers, and musicians.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that at the age of four, Joshua Bell was given his first violin, and he hasn’t put it down since. “I don’t remember falling in love with music,” states Bell. “Music has just been my life. I used to string rubber bands on my dresser drawers and make pitches by pulling the drawers out. I was fascinated with strings. It’s the closest instrument to the human voice. And I find it the most expressive instrument.”.

It has been revealed that today, the Grammy Award–winning musician is one of the most celebrated classical violinists of his era. By 14, Bell was performing with the Philadelphia Orchestra, and would soon be touring the world. “I live in hotels 250 days a year,” claims Bell of the nonstop schedule he has maintained since his teens. Specifically, Bell has been “staying at the Langham for decades now,” he says, referring to the regal central London hotel that first opened in 1865. “I chose it on my own because it was near one of my favorite halls in London, which is the Wigmore Hall. And now I stay with them whenever I’m traveling.”.

That kinship was solidified over coupes of Champagne and hand-dived Orkney scallops, with the hotel celebrating Bell, a “Langham Luminary,” in its London ballroom packed with writers, artists, designers, and musicians.

Attendees included actor Simon Callow, House of Dragon actor Emily Carey, former British culture minister Ed Vaizey, Saturday Night Live UK cast producer Susie Hall, stage and television actor Indira Varma, and Verity actor Ismael Cruz Córdova.

Industry observers note that held in partnership with Vanity Fair, the evening marked the latest iteration of the Langham’s Luminaries in Residence program. The event series is continuation of the hotel’s legacy that brings together a diverse, influential community—an evocative reminder of prominent guests from its storied past, including Charles Dickens, Winston Churchill, George Orwell, Oscar Wilde, and Mark Twain.

“I’m not going to put my name in the same sentence as Toscanini or Mark Twain—who has stayed here, or Churchill, who has stayed here. But it’s cool to be part of the history,” notes Bell. “So maybe someday, in a hundred years, there will be a violinist who might say that—that I stayed here. I don’t know, maybe that would mean something.”.

It certainly does mean something. Pierce Brosnan and his wife, Keely Shaye Brosnan, “have been huge fans of Joshua for many, many years,” Brosnan tells me. “Keely went to go see him…I don’t know how many years back. Unfortunately, due to the LA traffic, she got there late, five minutes late, and they wouldn’t let her into the concert. So tonight is one of those nights.”.

It has been revealed that bell, who performed mid-dinner with members of the Academy of St. Martin in the Fields—with a surprise appearance from his wife, soprano Larisa Martínez—brought about a collective catharsis.

Dazzling, fiery, and flamboyant, the experience of watching Bell up close is impossible to replicate. “I just think he’s incredibly soulful, and there’s something really elegant,” actor Russell Tovey tells me, before explaining how he actually discovered Bell via his Instagram algorithm.

According to recent reports, for actor Lesley Manville, the event marked her introduction to Bell’s music. “I’m a bit embarrassed that he was not on my radar. But isn’t that nice to have a surprise like that?” says Manville. “Schubert’s String Quintet is one of my favorite pieces of music. It’s unbelievably beautiful. You think of a violin, you think of those strings. And it’s instant emotion. They just make you cry.”.

There is a great power in being able to access the emotions of others, as Bell does.

“I think it is the ultimate gift to be able to make people happy,” states Brosnan. “My job is being an entertainer—to take the words of great writing and try to transform it into something that is meaningful and memorable.”.

Speaking of entertaining, the week’s announcement that Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond was front of mind. “I wish him every joy and every success. He and I made a movie a number of years ago called Remember Me. I played his father. So I was very, very pleased and joyful for his nomination and now his success, and I believe he will be magnificent.”.

Sources indicate that and that creative full circle is exactly what the night was advocating. “Our own Luminaries in Residence program reflects our belief that meaningful hospitality creates genuine connection with extraordinary talents with one another, and with arts,” Bob van den Oord, CEO of Langham Hospitality Group, explained as he took the stage. “The Langham isn’t simply a place to stay, but a place to gather, exchange ideas, and indeed celebrate.”.

Kim Kardashian’s paddock style is already unmatched.

Kardashian, 46, rocked a plunging, fitted black leather long-sleeved blouse with coordinating skintight pants to the F1 Academy finale on Saturday, November 21.

F1 Academy is Formula One’s all-women racing series, introduced in 2023 to help prepare aspiring female drivers to move up the ranks in the high-speed sport. Kardashian attended alongside managing director Susie Wolff and special guest Venus Williams, who had the honor of waving the checkered flag at the race’s starting line.

One day earlier, the Kardashians star attended the F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix qualifying session on Friday, November 20, in a fitted red leather bodysuit in support of her boyfriend, Lewis Hamilton.

Kardashian has been a fixture in the Ferrari garage since she started dating longtime friend Hamilton, 41, earlier this year.

Sources indicate that “I was really single for five years, and that felt great,” she told The Times of London in an October profile, making a rare comment about her dating status before finding love with Hamilton. “I could focus on my kids and projects that I really wanted to be involved with. I really felt no rush. Like, I really didn’t feel empty.”.

Industry observers note that kardashian, who shares four kids with ex-husband Kanye West, explained how she wanted to “completely heal” before diving into a latest relationship. (Following her divorce, the Skims mogul was briefly romantically linked to Pete Davidson and Odell Beckham Jr., respectively.).

According to recent reports, “I felt like I needed my time,” she noted to The Times. “I wasn’t ready to open up. I really wasn’t even thinking about it. The universe works in your favor when you just allow it to.”.

Kardashian, however, has declined to speak about her romance with the British racer at length.

“In the most respectful way, I’d probably rather not,” she quipped to the outlet when pressed for further details about her blossoming romance.

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

Well, here we are: the end of the year. The days are shorter, the nights are longer, and our bank accounts are getting smaller. You know why: the holidays are upon us, which means we all have to spend money like the good little consumers we are. The official unofficial launch of the holiday season always begins on Black Friday, that day after Thanksgiving where we wake up hungover from eating too much and start looking for substantial beautiful deals.

If you're a horror movie fan, I've thrown together a little list of five great Black Friday deals on horror movies, all of which are under $20! That's not bad, especially these days, when everything is outrageously expensive. So if you're a physical media collector and looking for something spooky to drop a few bucks on, keep reading.

In a recent development, danny Boyle's "28 Years Later" returned to the post-apocalyptic franchise he began with "28 Days Later," and he scored a major box office hit in the process. Unfortunately, "28 Years Later" was meant to be the first of a new trilogy, and the second movie, this year's "28 Years Later: The Bone Temple," wasn't a hit at all. As a result, the fate of the third and final movie in this new franchise is right now uncertain.

It has been revealed that which is a damn shame, because "The Bone Temple" absolutely rules. In fact, I think it's better than "28 Years Later." Ralph Fiennes returns as Dr. Ian Kelson, seemingly one of the last good men in a post-apocalyptic landscape overrun by rage-infected zombies and murderous groups of scavengers. This time, Dr. Kelson comes face to face with the deranged Jimmy Crystal (Jack O'Connell), all while trying to find a cure for that pesky rage virus.

"Evil Dead Burn" is the latest entry in the long-running franchise, and it did something no previous "Evil Dead" film did before: it made some fans think the movie was just a little too nasty. The franchise has become known for its over-the-top gore, but Sébastien Vaniček's film is so relentlessly aggressive that it rubbed a lot of fans the wrong way.

Me? I liked it. In fact, I would argue that while the film is definitely unpleasant, Vaniček also tries to inject some humor into the proceedings. It's a very dark and twisted kind of humor, but it's there. In "Evil Dead Burn," recently widowed Alice (Souheila Yacoub) gathers with the family of her dead husband. Unfortunately, the family doesn't really like her, and she doesn't like them either. To make matters worse, the family is soon possessed by those pesky Deadites, and Alice has to fight like hell to survive.

When Tom Cruise was cast as Lestat de Lioncourt, the brat prince at the heart of Anne Rice's "Interview with the Vampire," there was plenty of backlash — including from Rice herself, who thought Cruise was all wrong for the role. Rice eventually admitted she was wrong, however, because you know what? Tom Cruise gives one of the best performances of his career as Lestat, a foppish vampire who just wants to have a good time drinking blood and living his best afterlife.

It has been revealed that if there is a weak link in Neil Jordan's luscious film adaptation, it's Brad Pitt as Lestat's morose vampire companion, Louis. Pitt reportedly didn't have a good time making the movie, and it highlights in his performance. Despite this, "Interview with the Vampire" is a lavish Hollywood horror flick with a lot to offer, including a star-making turn from Kirsten Dunst as Claudia, who is turned into a vampire as a child and is thus trapped in a child's body forever.

Sources indicate that at this point, "Obsession" needs no further introduction. Curry Barker's mega-hit horror flick has a knockout performance from Inde Navarrette as Nikki, the object of affection for her longtime friend Bear (Michael Johnston).

It has been revealed that when Bear gets hold of a magical doodad known as the One Wish Willow, he makes a wish for Nikki to love him more than anyone else in the world. Of course, this wish backfires terribly, and it's made even worse because for all his "nice guy" nonsense, Bear is actually a horrible, selfish creep.

Equal parts funny and scary, "Obsession" got a lot of hype, and I genuinely believe it was worth it: this movie works exceptionally well, and I wouldn't be surprised if Navarrette scores herself an Oscar nom for her work here.

Zach Cregger's "Weapons" is yet another highly-hyped horror movie that lives up to its reputation. Borrowing a page or two from "Magnolia," Cregger's film gives us multiple narratives surrounding the mystery of a mass disappearance of children who were all in the same classroom. Their teacher (Julia Garner) becomes a suspect, and one of the missing kid's fathers (Josh Brolin) starts playing detective to true to solve the mystery himself.

Of course, by now everyone knows one of the biggest and best parts of the film is the malevolent Aunt Gladys, played to perfection by Amy Madigan, who earned herself a Best Supporting Actress Oscar for her now-iconic performance.

Tech Report: 10 Books Like ‘Dungeon Crawler Carl’ You Should Read Next

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There’s nothing quite like Dungeon Crawler Carl, Matt Dinniman’s hilarious, inventive, and surprisingly emotional book series about a man in his underwear forced to fight his way through a livestreamed game show based on dungeon-crawling video games that takes place after an alien takeover of Earth.
  • The premise should not work, but it sure does—and it makes more sense if you know it fits into a popular genre known as "LitRPG," a blend of "literature" and "role-playing game." If you've torn through all eight books released so far and you're looking for more reads that blend surprisingly deep hilarity with tabletop and video game rules (or just similar feels), here are 10 books you should check out.
  • It has been revealed that an isekai story that lands in the sweet spot for DCC fans, He Who Fights with Monsters kicks off with Jason—a completely normal, kind of boring middle manager—waking up in a strange hedge maze, completely nude (even his hair is gone).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There’s nothing quite like Dungeon Crawler Carl, Matt Dinniman’s hilarious, inventive, and surprisingly emotional book series about a man in his underwear forced to fight his way through a livestreamed game show based on dungeon-crawling video games that takes place after an alien takeover of Earth. (Did I mention he's accompanied by his ex-girlfriend’s suddenly talkative cat?).

The premise should not work, but it sure does—and it makes more sense if you know it fits into a popular genre known as "LitRPG," a blend of "literature" and "role-playing game." If you've torn through all eight books released so far and you're looking for more reads that blend surprisingly deep hilarity with tabletop and video game rules (or just similar feels), here are 10 books you should check out.

It has been revealed that an isekai story that lands in the sweet spot for DCC fans, He Who Fights with Monsters kicks off with Jason—a completely normal, kind of boring middle manager—waking up in a strange hedge maze, completely nude (even his hair is gone). He has magic that works like a video game, and has to deal with quests that slowly give him clothes (it’s a relief when he finally acquires some pants), force him to survive cannibals, and hunt down various monsters that definitely need killing. It’s got the same “gaming rules” structure as DCC and a similarly absurdist tone, with just the right spice of darkness.

The Cradle series by Will Wight isn’t a LitRPG, and it doesn’t have Carl’s focus on humor, but it’s another progression fantasy with enough game-like elements to be a great match. Lindon is an “unsouled,” incapable of gaining any of the sacred arts and doomed to a life without a future. His lack of power makes Lindon ferociously determined to find an alternative path to power and success, and that’s what drives this story. He has to find creative ways to move forward, and slowly this leads him to a path that just might make him the most powerful person in his world. DCC fans will love the progression and the tone.

Sources indicate that one of the key elements of any video game is the respawn—you get killed, but you pop back up to try again, sometimes at the beginning, sometimes at a save point. Django Wexler leverages that mechanic to great effect in How to Become the Dark Lord and Die Trying. Davi has been summoned to a fantasy world to be the hero, the person who defeats the Dark Lord and saves the day—but she’s failed (and died) so many times, she’s fed up, and decides that on this run through, she’s going to switch sides and become the Dark Lord, using all her knowledge gained from endless replays to her advantage. The humor is pitch-black the way DCC fans like it, and the progressive structure is a perfect fit.

Is Princess Donut your favorite part of Dungeon Crawler Carl? Of course she is. In that case, check out Andrew Seiple’s Threadbare series. Threadbare is a stuffed bear brought to magical life in a failed experiment. He’s a foot tall, full of stuffing, and extremely dumb when the story begins. But when he’s rescued by a little girl and plunged into a horrible series of dangers, Threadbare has to find a way to level up. Like DCC, Threadbare starts off leaning into the absurdity and humor, then slowly gains emotional gravitas as the story progresses.

If you play tabletop RPGs, you’ve encountered a Murderhobo or two: A character who solves all their problems by killing—even members of their own party. Luke doesn’t aspire to be a Murderhobo—he just wants to take over the family business and hang with his buddies. But when an invasion threatens the kingdom, everyone over the age of 17 is ordered to be tested for Potential. Luke’s friends all test high and join the Ascender Corps, traveling to different planes for training. Luke tests ... very low, and when he steps through a portal to engage in his training, he finds himself without any guidance or training in a strange, deadly world where his only chance of survival is to murder his way through it. It’s dark, darkly funny, and a progression fantasy like no other.

According to recent reports, if you’re looking for a book series that combines the dark, chaotic humor, absurd game mechanics, and surprising emotional depth of Carl, here’s Ryan “Quicksave” Romano, a man who has the unique ability to literally create a save point in his existence that allows him to go back and redo things whenever he dies. Searching for a childhood friend, he becomes embroiled in a violent gang war that lets him make good use of his power—but underneath the snark and the insanity of Ryan’s existence is a surprisingly affecting story of a man who has suffered, and suffered countless tragedies that are definitely taking their toll.

If your fave bit of DCC is Carl himself—a mediocre dude in an extraordinary situation—you should read Dennis E. Taylor’s fantastic Bobiverse books. Bob is a software engineer who hits it massive and promptly dies, waking up to discover a century has passed and he’s been repurposed as an AI controlling a space probe searching for fresh planets for humanity to inhabit. If he fails in his mission (and he’s not the only probe out there), he’ll be turned off for good. Luckily, he can make copies of himself, and he’s pretty smart. The humor here is smart and soaked in pop culture, making it a perfect match for DCC fans.

Want more of Carl’s absurdist humor? Mayor of Noobtown is the LitRPG you’re looking for. Jim dies and wakes up in a video game-esque universe and finds himself stuck in the zone designated for newbies—players with no experience, skill, or hope. The area fell out of the mainline progression mechanic a long time ago, so there doesn’t seem to be a way to gain power, and the monsters are not at all concerned about the unfairness of it all, so Jim has to figure out how to advance in a universe that seems designed to kill him (again).

It has been revealed that if you want to lean into the meta side of things, check out Scathing Reviewer, written by an author who goes by the unusual pen name "BananaDragon." Liu Peijin is the author of a sprawling LitRPG web novel, and she’s used to the bad reviews and complaints from readers—and quite combative about it. When her books’ universe blossoms into a very dangerous new reality, she should be perfectly positioned to survive, having written the story in the first place. But her story becoming real also means her insufferable protagonist is real, and all those nasty critics are now passing judgment on her entire existence. It’s a dark, funny takedown of the entire genre itself, and DCC fans will love it.

According to recent reports, if you want a story that parallels the dungeon crawling aspect of DCC, Andrew Rowe’s Arcane Ascension series is the ticket. The Serpent Spire is a tower of constantly changing traps, puzzles, and dangerous creatures. If you enter and survive, you emerge with magical powers. Corin Cadence’s brother entered the Serpent Spire years ago and never returned—and now Corin is determined not only to survive, but to make it to the top, where legend claims a goddess will grant you whatever you wish. And what Corin wants is his brother back. It’s a literal progression combined with LitRPG rules, game-inspired puzzle-solving, and a complex magic system that fans of Carl will definitely enjoy.
