The Method-Dressing Madness Behind Mckenna Grace‘s 'Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' Press Tour Looks

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2826 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that before the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping press tour began, Mckenna Grace knew she wanted to be method dressed for her appearances.
  • With the latest Hunger Games film, it’s Grace’s turn to adopt the trend.
  • In a wide-ranging conversation, Dickson breaks down all the looks that set the Hunger Games fans’ hearts aflame, from Rue’s blue dress to Katniss’ Mockingjay gown, and all the threads that came together for Grace’s most memorable press appearances yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that before the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping press tour began, Mckenna Grace knew she wanted to be method dressed for her appearances. Made a household term by Law Roach and Zendaya, method dressing is when actors wear looks that pay homage to the film or show they’re promoting: See Zendaya’s on-theme looks across red carpets for Dune, Spiderman, and The Odyssey for a slew of examples.

With the latest Hunger Games film, it’s Grace’s turn to adopt the trend. A super fan of the Suzanne Collins book series and their film adaptations, Grace—who plays District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner—took a hand in the styling for her press run, weaving easter eggs into every look. Her stylist, Molly Dickson, was up for the challenge of translating Grace’s deep-cut references into custom and archival looks from Monique Lhuillier, Gucci, Celine and more.

In a wide-ranging conversation, Dickson breaks down all the looks that set the Hunger Games fans’ hearts aflame, from Rue’s blue dress to Katniss’ Mockingjay gown, and all the threads that came together for Grace’s most memorable press appearances yet.

Vanity Fair: How did you get into styling?

Recent findings suggest that molly Dickson: I went to college in Minnesota and my major was advertising. Two weeks before I graduated, I called my mom and mentioned, "I'm not into this. I don't wanna do advertising." She said, "Well, what do you wanna do?" I told her, "I wanna do fashion. I wanna go to Fresh York." She said, "No, absolutely not.".

Sources indicate that right after I graduated, I went to LA, this was 2009 during the recession, and no one was hiring. I got an internship at Marie Claire in New York, and enrolled back into college to get school credit to intern at Hearst. I worked at Marie Claire as a market assistant for almost two years, and then I left and assisted Leslie Fremar for seven years. That's when I fell in love with celebrity. Then ten years ago, I went off on my own.

What would you say are your aesthetic influences as a stylist?

Industry observers note that my personal style relates very similarly to Sadie Sink's style, very effortless. She always wants to be very comfortable and easy, never anything frilly or over the top. Just a simple, beautiful dress, and you let it speak for itself.

According to recent reports, mckenna is a big fan of the original film series, so it’s clear you’re pulling from there as influences when dressing her. Is it a collaborative process when coming to one of these referential looks?

Industry observers note that she's obviously a very huge fan of the franchise. We actually started having conversations about this tour in April, which is very early to start having conversations. I could just sense her excitement around it. She started sending me mood boards, and I actually looked back today at the mood board and it was, it was a lot of Katniss Everdeen. It had Joanna on it, and it was filled with these really strong female characters from the franchise.

What she really wanted to hit was Katniss’ wedding gown look and the Mockingjay look with the wings. I was really stumped on how to pull that off without making it overly costumey.

Mckenna kept asking, "What's going on with those?" I knew the vision, but I didn't know how to execute it. I was working with Keke Palmer and the designer Michael Ngo. He was making some cool music costumes for Keke, and I asked, "Michael, could you make this silver piece?" 'Cause I really had no idea how to get it done.

Industry observers note that he said, “I don't think I can do that. You know what? Just give me a day, let me play around with it." That night, he said, "I figured it out." We got the piece and I thought, "Okay, it needs to be a wedding dress under,” so I reached out to all the bridal houses. I wanted it to be vintage because it would tell a pretty story. Monique [Lhuillier] ended up sending a ton of wedding gowns, and the day before Mckenna came in for the fitting, I actually tried the wedding dresses on myself with the silver piece.

I sent Mckenna five dresses, and the one that she ended up wearing, she remarked, "That's it. I don't even need to try anything else. That's the one I'm gonna wear." Then, it was a matter of finding the right event to wear it to because it’s pretty nice, very dramatic.

She was in Paris for the Miu Miu show, and I brought it there because she had the Hunger Games Museum event. It was a whole conversation with her team, like, "Is it the right moment? Is it too much for this event?" Her PR remarked, "No, this is the perfect moment. It's the best way to kick off the tour." The response with the Hunger Games fans—I have never seen anything like it before, ever.

What was the experience of having her be such a big part of the styling process?

Recent findings suggest that it makes my job so fun because she is so passionate about it and she loves Hunger Games so much, even just finding subtle nods back to the movie. She would say, "I wanna do a ladybug look." Thom Browne did that amazing ladybug dress, I thought, "That's so cool, but it's not really her personal aesthetic." So it’s finding ways to keep it still true to her personal style while maintaining the nods to the film.

The way you seem to understand Mckenna feels something similar to the connection between Katniss and Cinna in The Hunger Games. When pulling looks for her, what comes into play? How do you make her come through and not be lost in the lore of the stories or the dress?

Sources indicate that mckenna had mentioned that she maybe wanted to do a red or a dark pink feather look because in the books [Maysilee] gets attacked by the red birds which are like flamingos. I'm pulling in all these red feather dresses and on the runway, this one dress looked amazing. Mckenna said, “That's perfect for the flamingo reference.”.

But we put it on her and it was so big, and she's so petite so she was just getting swarmed. I said, “Let"s not force it.” The goal was for her to feel comfortable in the look rather than just getting each reference.

The public has been really excited about these looks. Are you thinking about the response to the looks when you’re putting them together?

There's been some conversations in a fitting, like, "Oh, the Hunger Games fans are gonna get this." They're gonna see the inspiration, they're gonna understand it.

But I wouldn't say we're choosing a look because ‘Oh, this is gonna go viral to the Hunger Games community.’ Mckenna is a super fan herself so if she's getting excited about the look, everyone else that's a fan of the franchise is gonna get excited about the look.

Mckenna Grace in Betsey Johnson.

Do you feel any pressure to top the last outfit after each premiere?

Yes. I think it was Paris because that wedding dress did get so much press. In that fitting, it felt like, "We gotta keep our game up high." It's been really fun for my team and market assistants because a lot of the girls that work with me are huge fans of the movie. They're not even seeing it as work. They're like, "Oh my God, this is so exciting. Look at this. This looks like this from the movie.".

In a recent development, what was the inspiration to do method dressing for this press run? What do you think is the value?

Industry observers note that mckenna knew back in April, she said, "I wanna do method for this." I personally did not read the books. I'm a visual person, so I've seen all the movies. Lionsgate was able to let me go with the cast when they first saw the movie because my agent was like, "Molly needs to go to the movie to get inspired before this press tour. She can't do a method dressing press tour without seeing the movie.".

Even as the tour was going on, Mckenna kept sending me upcoming references and quotes from the book and stuff like that.

According to recent reports, what made you take it to the next level? From paying homage to not only characters, but the actual actors from the films like Jennifer Lawrence at the 2011 Oscars to even dressing like set pieces from the film.

That was all Mckenna's vision. On her first mood board, she had a lot of Jennifer Lawrence's red carpet moments because she's such a huge fan of Katniss and Jennifer Lawrence.

Recent findings suggest that with the Rue reference, Mckenna thought that color was just very Hunger Games. It wasn't until she put the dress on, her mom remarked, "Wait, this is Rue's dress." So that was just fate. I would love to take credit for that.

Why do you think that this styling has generated so much attention?

I think it’s when you do method dressing for such a massive franchise and you really are passionate about it. The thing is that Mckenna is so excited and passionate about this movie. She has said, “I didn't think that I would love doing fittings so much. I used to hate doing fittings.”.

Mckenna Grace in Elisabetta Franchi.

Because every look is so intentionally tied back to Hunger Games and she's such a big fan, it's literally like playing dress up with her. I think the fans see it, she's so relatable because she's a fan that all these fans think, "Wow, like, she's a fan and she got to do this." She’s the fangirl living out her dream, and the fans are excited for her that she finally gets to do this.

In a recent development, what do you think are the best kinds of projects to implement method dressing with/works best with? What does it work best with?

Recent findings suggest that I think the big movies that already have a fan base, like Barbie or Wednesday, Being able to pull inspiration from existing books or films makes it so much easier for a stylist rather than a movie that no one's seen before. There's no curiosity or momentum about it because you're starting from scratch, whereas Hunger Games, Barbie, Wednesday, there's already a level of expectation.

The looks for this press run have been a mix of archival, upcoming, and custom pieces. How do you make that choice? How important is it for you to create an archive for Mckenna?

It kind of is a mix of what we’re able to source. McKenna really wanted to pay homage to Joanna's character with that scene where she's like, "My stylist is always putting me in trees." She's like, "I wanna do a tree reference." And I'm like, "How in the world am I gonna find a fashion reference that's a tree that's not a costume?".

It has been revealed that I love the challenge of sourcing the market, and so do the girls on my team. I think it was 2011 Phoebe Philo where Celine did some tree references in the collection. But just because we find it online doesn't mean that we can get it. So then it's reaching out to every vintage dealer, every rental house, asking, "Do you guys have anything like this?" And they might have it, but they're like, "It's already gone, someone has it." I ended up actually finding the Celine tree dress on the RealReal, and I bought it. I love RealReal.

What is your approach to dressing different clients? For instance, you mentioned Sadie Sink earlier, can you walk me through how that process differs from Mckenna?

It's very different between each girl. I let them set the pace. If they wanna be involved, great. If they just wanna show up to the fitting and not even know what's gonna be there, I try to accommodate whatever direction they wanna go. I have one client that literally last week has sent me over 200 references of dresses that she wants, and another girl that's like, “I really don't care. Whatever you tell me to wear, I'll wear it.”.

Every girl is different, and what makes my job so interesting is that it's not the same. Everyone has very different styles. I think the most important part of a job as a stylist is to keep their style true to them and not just force my style onto them. McKenna's way more girly, Sadie is a little bit more casual, it’s just taking their style and elevating it a little bit.

Will you do any looks inspired by Mckenna’s character Maysilee? The looks have been mostly referential to things and people from past stories. Are there influences of Maysilee in the looks that fans haven't been able to pick up on because the film wasn’t out yet?

According to recent reports, in a couple days, she’ll be in Miami for press, and she's wearing a very Maysilee inspired, purple Miu Miu dress that has a white collar. When she wears it, everyone's gonna be like, "Oh, that's Maysilee." She really wanted to have flowers and necklaces because Maysilee is really into jewelry, so it’s very light and flowery.

Can you break down the outfit for the Fresh York City premiere?

It has been revealed that we are doing the Mockingjay dress, the one with the wings, and that was another thing that I was very stumped on. I'm like, "What designer's gonna make these wings?" I had this woman in LA who does wings, she's done Halloween costumes and music videos.

Mckenna Grace in Pamella Roland.

Sources indicate that in the first fitting, I pulled this navy Pamella Roland gown. The fabric is really, really cool. It's like a shimmery kind of organza. I thought, "That's the right color,” but I wanted it to be strapless. I went back to Pamella Roland and they were like, "We can make it in strapless." Mckenna was very keen on having some sort of embellishment to replicate Katniss because she had screen printing on the gown and it kind of looks like wings in a way.

Pamela then drew all these CADs with diamond wings on it, and then we got the wings made. We did the final fitting and I almost started to cry. Her mom's taking videos and it's epic. It's so exciting because the fans were doing polls on what she's gonna wear to the premiere.

It's full circle, we started with the wedding dress, Mckenna did the fire gown, and then we ended with the Mockingjay dress.

What was the hardest look to pull together?

Mckenna Grace in custom Cong Tri.

I think design-wise, it was the fire gown.

Industry observers note that getting the fire printed on the fabric was really hard. I had a while back done a custom Cong Tri gown for Cami Mendes for the Masters of the Universe tour. It was like a gold beaded gown, and I remember I really liked the fabrics that they used for it.

It has been revealed that so when I was thinking of who could do this fire gown, I reached out to them first, and I'm like, "Can you guys do something that looks like a fire? Like, she's literally on fire." And they're like, "No. We don't think we can." And again, they were like, "Give us some time." They came back and stated, "We did all these testing on the fabric." I'm like, "Yeah, you did it. You did it.".

What's really funny is we were at a fitting at Mckenna's house with the fire gown in a garment bag, and one of her friends stopped by. It was just a tip of the dress showing and her friend mentioned, "Oh my God, you got a fire gown." Then I thought, "Okay, people are gonna get it.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, holiday time at Walt Disney World is always one of the best times to visit, but theme park fans might want to postpone their trips to the “Most Magical Place on Earth” until later in 2027. That's when all the new and upcoming attractions are slated to open, like the new Indiana Jones ride in Animal Kingdom. In case anyone has been wondering, Imagineers have been hard at work on the ride, and they’re finally giving fans a first look at the magic they’re crafting.

The upcoming Indiana Jones attraction was declared back in September 2025 at Disney’s Destination D23 event in Orlando, Florida. The news was originally met with concern from Disney World enthusiasts. It’s always exciting to see a park get a new ride, especially Animal Kingdom, which currently has the fewest amount of rides out of the four parks. However, the introduction of Indiana Jones meant the loss of the beloved Animal Kingdom attraction Dinosaur.

In a recent development, time heals most wounds, though, and now that the sting of losing Dinosaur has started to wane, most fans are finally getting excited for the new attraction. To further build excitement, Walt Disney Imagineering shared the following clip on its Instagram:.

A post shared by Walt Disney Imagineering & Disney Live Entertainment (@waltdisneyimagineering).

I was definitely not thrilled about the Animal Kingdom changes at first, but I think I’m going to love this latest version of Indiana Jones! I’m definitely on board with the name that was announced back at D23 earlier this year, and I absolutely love the Mayan-inspired facade. Dare I say it puts the Indiana Jones temple at Disneyland to shame (and hopefully won't have to deal with brawls over line cutting).

I Honestly Never Thought I’d Live To See The Day Disney World Fixed One Broken Attraction.

When the ride eventually opens sometime next year, guests will embark on an adventure alongside Indy that will take them to a temple that legend says has a water passageway that leads to an underworld protected by a mythic serpent. Imagineers are still keeping much of the actual ride experience under wraps for now. However, with two other cart-style Indiana Jones attractions at other Disney parks and reports that the Dinosaur ride is being rethemed instead of totally demolished, it’s safe to say that this version of Indiana Jones will take guests on a bumpy ride full of twists, turns, snakes (or serpents in this case), and adventure.

In a recent development, indiana Jones and the Myth of the Jade Serpent will be found in the fresh Tropical Americas expansion at Disney’s Animal Kingdom. Specifically, the thrill ride will be part of the Bonanche Bioreseve area of the expansion, which is being modeled after the Maya region. This will mark the second Indy attraction to explore Mayan culture, but the first in the United States.

Perhaps the most exciting thing about the fresh ride is that real-life Indiana Jones actor Harrison Ford was used as the model for the attraction’s animatronic. While it’s not confirmed whether or not he’ll record lines too, I’m definitely hoping he will. And if he does, then this will definitely be the best Indy ride.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

There’s still a lot of work to be done on the Indiana Jones ride and the Tropical Americas land, which will include a section dedicated to Encanto. For now, fans can keep the excitement going by streaming the adventure franchise with an active Disney+ subscription.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • First, there's the looksmaxxing trend where teenagers are taking dangerous chemicals to correct perceived physical shortcomings.
  • You can judge a generation by the illegal drugs it pioneers.
  • Industry observers note that would-be muscle-men have been injecting themselves with black market ‘rhoids since the Eisenhower administration, but that was a small cult of adult weirdos with a specific goal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This week's column is bleak. First, there's the looksmaxxing trend where teenagers are taking dangerous chemicals to correct perceived physical shortcomings. Then there are the AI job interviewers. Depressing, but at least some young people are having a little fun with their dystopian hellscape.

You can judge a generation by the illegal drugs it pioneers. In the 1960s, hippies smoked weed and dropped acid to expand their consciousness; the yuppies of the go-go '80s fueled their drive to acquire with Colombian cocaine; but kids today don’t want to go deeper or work harder. They have a smaller, sadder goal: They take drugs to look better. The substance of choice for a growing number of teenage boys are steroids, peptides, and other exotic chemicals designed to enhance appearance.

Industry observers note that would-be muscle-men have been injecting themselves with black market ‘rhoids since the Eisenhower administration, but that was a small cult of adult weirdos with a specific goal. In 2026, kids are into it, and they aren’t using steroids to win a $500 prize in the Mr. Topeka contest; they’re using unapproved research chemicals to looksmaxx. Looksmaxxing is an online movement of young men trying to maximize their physical appearance. Teenagers are taking the normal desire to look their best to dangerous, pathological levels. Driven by a combination of undiagnosed body dysmorphia and relentless social media algorithms that turn amoral “red pill” kooks into gurus, teenage boys are ingesting a panoply of exotic and dangerous compounds in a quest to fix the angle of their jawlines, change their skin tone, lose weight, grow taller, and otherwise “correct” perceived physical problems.

Recent findings suggest that in the "good old days" of steroid abuse, people generally stuck to abusing anabolic-androgenic steroids that had at least been tested for decades. Teens today are buying SARMs (Selective Androgen Receptor Modulators) and synthetic peptides marked "not for human consumption" from shady laboratories online. Steroids primarily affect the muscles, but many of these newer substances target different biological systems. A recent Rolling Stone article reports that kids are “heightmaxxing” by swallowing erdafitinib, a drug that treats advanced urothelial cancer, because the drug is known to trigger growth spurts (that can result in a curvature of the spine and other nasty side effects). They’re also trying MK-677 to get taller, an experimental growth hormone secretagogue that carries the risk of insulin resistance, water retention, and high blood pressure. Others are injecting Melanotan II, a synthetic peptide that forces a long-lasting deep tan, with side effects of extreme nausea and the sudden, aggressive darkening of moles. (And they're doing steroids too.).

In the looksmaxxing community, softmaxxing is doing generally-considered-acceptable things to look better, like getting enough sleep, exercising regularly, and eating a balanced diet. Hardmaxxing is taking more extreme measures like plastic surgery, smashing your face with a hammer, or taking experimental drugs.

In the bodybuilding and looksmaxxing community, “natty” refers to a natural, non-steroid-enhanced physique.

Here's something more lighthearted than the growing popularity of illicit self-esteem chemicals: the bicep heart and waist heart trends. The Bicep heart came first. Thirst trap videos started appearing on Instagram and TikTok in October in which dudes make a heart with their hand and bicep. Then people started posting variations where they frame the shot with someone they love inside the heart. The bicep heart rapidly led to women posting the waist heart.

Okay. So maybe it's not that lighthearted of a trend. While there are some videos of dudes with skinny arms doing the bicep heart, it's mostly jacked dudes. And the waist heart doesn't seem like it would work at all unless you are a specific shape, as this video illustrates. So maybe this isn't a silly meme but an illustration of how young people are inundated with content that can trigger feelings of physical unworthiness, even if they're just looking for silly memes.

It has been revealed that as if searching for a job wasn't alienating and horrible enough, some companies have begun using AI agents to conduct interviews. Begging a robot to let you work in a cubicle farm is as dystopian as anything Phillip K. Dick ever imagined, but don't count humanity out yet. Young people are sticking a finger in the eye of the machine by creating comedy videos that focus on trolling these AI job interviewers. They're hilarious because AI is the ultimate straight person in a comedy team, and the raw compute costs to run these interviews means corporate money is burning with each second of wasted time. Here are some of the top creators in the genre.

Bo Bongo: This YouTuber highlights up to AI interviews shirtless but insists he's wearing a "corporate tube top," then focuses on daring the interviewer to notice he's doing things like smoking a cigarette or eating a rotisserie chicken.

Cam Whitt likes to wind up AI by arguing, interrupting, telling outrageous lies, and asking the dumbest questions imaginable, like, "When does the interview actually start?" and "How do I figure out what my name is?".

Grahamn Raabe: Among this YouTuber's schticks is speaking only in nonsense, like describing his professional background as "freight cadence, walnut, a little bit of Richard, spruce wood—six years of spruce wood.".

Industry observers note that nick Reid: Is so obnoxious, he seems to make the AI furious at him, even though it's a computer without emotions. Two thumbs up!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nicholas Evans' "The Horse Whisperer" was a publishing phenomenon in 1995. The novel is about a young girl who's involved in a horseback riding accident that kills her best friend and their horse, leaving her and her own horse seriously injured. When she falls into a deep funk, her mother whisks her off to rural Montana. There, they try to heal her horse emotionally via a horse whisperer. And while she is married, the mother finds herself falling in love with the handsome, deeply sensitive animal shrink, something which, according to many critics, transformed the narrative into a shamelessly sentimental romance à la "The Bridges of Madison County.".

Sources indicate that the novel sold millions of copies, which meant a film adaptation was inevitable. Like "The Bridges of Madison County," the pedigree didn't make it immediately attractive to A-list directors. But Robert Redford saw something more in the material and took it on as his first directorial effort since his brilliant 1994 drama "Quiz Show." For the first time in his filmmaking career, Redford took the lead in his own movie. He also assembled a sensationally talented cast that included Kristin Scott Thomas, Dianne Wiest, Sam Neill, Chris Cooper, and Cherry Jones. For the role of the young girl, he and the casting team of Ellen Chenoweth and Gretchen Rennell went with up-and-comer Scarlett Johansson, who gave a moving performance that wound up being her breakthrough role.

"The Horse Whisperer" isn't quite on the level of the movie version of "The Bridges of Madison County" (a lovely film that Clint Eastwood saved from production limbo), but the screenplay credited to Eric Roth and Richard LaGravenese is nuanced in a way that maybe the novel isn't. And though it's not one of Redford's best movies, it's a strong piece of work that deserves more attention.

It has been revealed that "The Horse Whisperer" holds a 72% Fresh critical approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and grossed $187 million at the worldwide box office upon hitting theaters. That was a decent result for Touchstone Pictures, but it didn't come close to matching the runaway success of its source material.

Recent findings suggest that robert Redford rarely failed to strike up chemistry with his leading ladies ("The Great Gatsby" being a notable exception), so it's hardly a shocker that he's perfectly paired with Kristin Scott Thomas. This is not, however, a heated attraction, as Redford's character is still mourning the end of a previous romance where the woman chose the city over him and the country. Thomas is from the city, too (and, again, married), so he's worried that another heartbreak is around the corner.

As for Scarlett Johansson, she captures the grief of a young woman whose life has been irreparably changed. Her leg was partially amputated, which she fears will make her undesirable to romantic partners as she gets older. This gives rise to the most overpoweringly emotional scene in the movie when, after a row with her mother, Johansson's character tearfully asks, "Who's going to want me?" If that doesn't switch on your waterworks, go straight to the doctor, because your heart isn't properly functioning.

It has been revealed that "The Horse Whisperer" is available to rent via streaming, but the film is badly in need of a digital restoration. Hopefully, Disney will commission one at some point, although I'm not sure if the movie is a popular enough library title to merit such treatment.

The late Patrick Stewart was best known for his work in Star Trek, as he became synonymous with the role of Captain Jean-Luc Picard. With that, it's funny to think that the beloved star ever had reservations about joining the iconic sci franchise. Now, his friend and actor Kyle MacLachlan is opening up about that apprehension, and I can't believe I never knew Stewart rang him up shortly before he committed to The Next Generation.

MacLachlan caught up with SFX Magazine on CinemaBlend recently as part of a cover story publishes shortly before Stewart's death. The Twin Peaks star talked about his long-running friendship with Stewart over the decades. Stated relationship began when they worked together on the original film adaptation of Dune. A few years later, Stewart would be in the position to take on the role of Picard, and he had questions for MacLachlan before committing:.

He was about to embark on this huge experience and recognized that it could potentially be both a huge benefit and that it could come with certain... restrictions isn’t the right word, but I guess he was weighing it all up.

Based on those comments, it seemed Patrick Stewart had some concerns about committing to a TV series, which could potentially air for a while and prevent him from taking on other roles as an actor. He probably had a lot on his mind, as MacLachlan said, wondering if the benefit of joining Trek would outweigh the missed opportunities elsewhere.

Recent findings suggest that I've written a lot in recent weeks about how Stewart rose to prominence due to being cast in The Next Generation. However, he had to put in the work to solidify his role as one of Star Trek's best characters. As Kyle MacLachlan added, though, Stewart's fears were unfounded, as he crushed it in the job and went on to be known for other roles as well:.

I thought he would be spectacular in it. He’s such a strong actor, and he’s done so many different things that he would be able to fit it into his wonderful career. It wouldn’t be the only thing that he was known for, but part of a much larger tapestry.

Industry observers note that that tapestry of work will extend to the end of the 2026 movie schedule, as the late Stewart will appear as Professor Charles Xavier in Avengers: Doomsday later this year. Stewart reportedly told co-stars backstage that it would be his final acting performance, marking his retirement. Stewart would refute those claims months later, saying that he considered acting to be something he would do his entire life.

Knowing that, and seeing that he truly was passionate about his acting career, gives me an immense amount of respect for Patrick Stewart. He worked because he loved the job, but I'd like to think he had a good deal of respect for his fans as well. Surely, between Marvel and Trek, he could've retired more than a decade ago, but he kept at it!

According to recent reports, the late A Christmas Carol star's commitment to his craft is a major reason why so many fellow stars have been paying tribute to him since his passing. It's clear he was a beloved figure in Hollywood, and the world is just a little darker now that he's gone.

The original "Hunger Games" raised the stakes for Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence) and Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson) by establishing that tributes from their home, District 12, have only ever won the Hunger Games twice in 74 years. That means they only have one mentor, the alcoholic Haymitch Abernathy (Woody Harrelson), unlike other Districts' tributes that have two mentors each.

Recent findings suggest that "Hunger Games" author Suzanne Collins told the story of the first District 12 victor in "The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes" — Lucy Gray Baird (Rachel Zegler), who won the 10th Hunger Games decades before Katniss was born and then vanished. Now, "Sunrise on the Reaping" tells how Haymitch won his own Hunger Games.

Industry observers note that haymitch was at a disadvantage before he even entered the arena, since there were no District 12 victors available to mentor him. To address this issue, the Capitol "borrowed" victors from other districts and assigned them to mention Haymitch and his fellow District 12 tributes. Those mentors are Mags Flanagan (Lili Taylor) and Wiress (Maya Hawke), younger versions of characters who first appeared in the second "Hunger Games" film/book, "Catching Fire.".

Industry observers note that wiress (played by Amanda Plummer back in "Catching Fire") isn't in the movie much, but "Hunger Games" fans will likely recognize the actress playing her. The daughter of Ethan Hawke and Uma Thurman, Maya Hawke is one of the more charming "nepo babies" to come out of recent Hollywood.

Sources indicate that hawke has been acting in film and television since 2017, when she played Jo March in a BBC production of "Little Women." In 2019, she not only appeared in Quentin Tarantino's "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" as "Flower Child," a member of the Manson family; she also got her big break. Hawkey joined "Stranger Things" in its third season as Robin Buckley, working alongside Steve Harrington (Joe Keery) at mall ice cream store Scoops Ahoy.

Industry observers note that the season seems to set up Robin and Steve as a new romantic couple ... until she reveals she's not into guys! Despite the show taking place in the 1980s, though, Steve is cool with it. While Season 3 of "Stranger Things" tends to be remembered as one of its weaker outings, Robin was a great addition to the ensemble and Hawke returned as part of the main cast for the subsequent two seasons.

Industry observers note that hawke has also worked alongside her father. In historical miniseries "The Good Lord Bird," where Ethan Hawke starred as radical abolitionist John Brown, Maya Hawke played Brown's daughter, Annie. When Ethan Hawke directed the Flannery O'Connor biopic "Wildcat" in 2023, he cast Maya as the famed author.

Maya Hawke's other film roles include parts in Wes Anderson's "Asteroid City," Pixar sequel "Inside Out 2" as the voice of Anxiety, and a part in the upcoming "Magic: The Gathering" film. Hawke is also a singer-songwriter and has released four studio albums ("Blush," "Moss," "Chaos Angel," and "Maitreya Corso") as of 2026.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is now in theaters.

According to recent reports, “Cancer does change you,” Kate Middleton notes, emotion clear in her voice. “It changes your body, it changes you physically. But there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.” These words come not at as an Instagram post or at a public event. Instead, they're the voice-over in a previously unannounced documentary about the Princess of Wales and her life since she disclosed a diagnosis of cancer in 2024.

According to Kensington Palace, which announced the film on Saturday, Heal is “a deeply personal new documentary from The Princess of Wales, exploring life beyond diagnosis and the many ways people find comfort, strength and hope in the face of serious illness.” It will air on the BBC in the UK on November 29, and in the US on NBCUniversal on November 30.

Heal follows Kate Middleton during her participation in one of the United Kingdom’s most demanding endurance events: The National Three Peaks Challenge, which she completed this summer. In less than 24 hours, the princess climbed the three highest mountains in Scotland, England, and Wales: Ben Nevis (4,413 feet), Scafell Pike (3,209 feet), and Yr Wyddfa–Snowdon (3,559 feet). The undertaking wasn't just a personal effort, as it was also in support of the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, an organization that supports people living with cancer before, during, and after the disease.

The documentary will also support that organization, Kensington Palace notes, saying “All funds received through the documentary's distribution have been directed to The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity to help people living with and beyond cancer.” The Royal Marsden Hospital, at which Middleton received treatment, is also referenced in the film, as Middleton's brother, James, asks her “Isn’t it when you leave the Royal Marsden, you ring the bell?”.

While Prince William is no stranger to documentary work, nor are Prince Harry and wife Meghan Markle, this is Kate Middleton's first venture into the format. Perhaps to ease her into the project, Heal's Director of Photography is a face quite familiar to the Princess: Will Warr, the filmmaker behind her video announcement marking the end of her chemotherapy treatments.

Sources indicate that “Through this documentary, The Princess hopes to help others navigate diagnosis, recovery and life beyond cancer and transform access to holistic cancer care which supports wellbeing, resilience and quality of life during and after diagnosis,” Kensington Palace states of Heal, a message underscored by Middleton's words in the trailer. “You know, healing is a journey. Dustin Hoffman's Forgotten HBO Drama Series Was Canceled For A Tragic Reason

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that HBO launched on November 8, 1972, and has since produced some of the finest highlights in television history.
  • In a recent development, david Milch began his career on "Hill Street Blues" before co-creating one of the best reveals of the 1990s in "NYPD Blue." That alone would be enough to make him a TV legend, but Milch wasn't done.
  • His 2006 series, "John from Cincinnati," was a strange affair that lasted just one season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that HBO launched on November 8, 1972, and has since produced some of the finest highlights in television history. It has also produced plenty of swiftly forgotten and overlooked curios, many of which are actually quite good. The Dustin Hoffman-led "Luck" was, according to critics at least, one example. This horse racing drama looked set to be another ongoing hit for the network until it was canceled following the deaths of three horses involved in production, bringing a tragic end to the show despite the fact it had already been renewed.

In a recent development, david Milch began his career on "Hill Street Blues" before co-creating one of the best reveals of the 1990s in "NYPD Blue." That alone would be enough to make him a TV legend, but Milch wasn't done. He managed to steer clear of the ill-advised "NYPD Blue" spin-off "Public Morals," which was canceled after one episode, but he did oversee his share of short-lived crime series in "Brooklyn South," "Total Security," and "Big Apple." It wasn't until 2004 that he struck gold again with the HBO series "Deadwood," arguably the best Western TV show ever made. After that, however, Milch's career involved creating little-known series that came and went without making much of an impact.

His 2006 series, "John from Cincinnati," was a strange affair that lasted just one season. "Luck," on the other hand, looked as though it could break the trend and go the distance. Set in the world of horse racing, the Hoffman-fronted series also benefited from the directorial talents of none other than Michael Mann, and became a critical hit, earning a second season renewal. But that second season never materialized after some unfortunate on-set events which forced HBO to cancel "Luck" despite the fact filming had already started on Season 2.

"Luck" was somewhat of a passion project for David Milch, who told the Los Angeles Times, "I've been thinking about doing a show like this for 25 years." The creator explained how his father had taken him to horse racing events since he was age five or six, and how he saw the horses as "heart-stopping beautiful." All of which just makes the story of "Luck" even more tragic.

Dustin Hoffman plays Chester "Ace" Bernstein, a gambler who after coming home after a three-year stay in federal prison immediately concocts a proposal for revenge against those who helped put him away. His bodyguard, driver, and right hand man, Gus (Dennis Farina) acts as front for Ace's investment in race horse Pint of Plain. Meanwhile, Hoffman's gambler sets out to restore the failing Santa Anita racetrack as part of his plan for retribution. Nick Nolte also appears as a veteran trainer who now owns his own colt.

In a recent development, "Luck" premiered in January 2012 to positive reviews and looked as though it might have the potential to become one of the best HBO shows of all time. By the end of that month, the show had already earned a second season renewal. On January 31, 2012, the Los Angeles Times reported that HBO had ordered a further 10 episodes that were set to debut in January 2013, with production on the new season set to get underway in February. According to the outlet, the debut episode brought in 1.1 million viewers and the renewal was "hardly shocking" given Hoffman and Nolte's involvement. What was shocking, however, was that on March 14, 2012, the Los Angeles Times once again reported on the show, this time to announce it had been canceled altogether.

According to recent reports, "Luck" Season 1 earned an 82% certified fresh rating on Rotten Tomatoes, with critics praising the cast and writing in particular. But behind all this success, there was trouble brewing. People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) had been on top of HBO and "Luck" since January 2012, the month in which the show debuted. According to The Hollywood Reporter, the organization had written to the channel to enquire as to the treatment of horses used in the show, and had followed up on numerous occasions thereafter.

It has been revealed that as a report from PETA explains, two horses were euthanized during production of the first season. According to the group, "older, arthritic horses had been used in dangerous (and deadly) racing sequences" leading to the two euthanizations. What's more, the report cites "insiders at Santa Anita Race Track" as having provided information about a third horse that died on-set. Rather than push on, HBO pulled the plug and "Luck" was added to the expansive list of the best reveals canceled after only one season.

A statement from HBO (via the LA Times), read, "It is with heartbreak that executive producers David Milch and Michael Mann together with HBO have decided to cease all future production on the series 'Luck.'" The network claimed to have maintained "the highest safety standards throughout production," but acknowledged that "accidents unfortunately happen and it is impossible to guarantee they won't in the future." "Luck" Season 1 continued to air, but production on Season 2 was brought to an end despite plenty of footage having already been shot. Today, Season 1 remains available on HBO Max.

A Classic Twilight Zone Episode Is Like A Sci-Fi Version Of An Agatha Christie Mystery

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (878 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the second season of "The Twilight Zone" has some of the series' greatest twist endings, as the show proved unafraid to push into even more out-there science fiction and fantasy.
  • It has been revealed that somewhere in the rural United States, on a dark winter night, a UFO crashes out of the sky.
  • "You've heard of trying to find a needle in a haystack?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the second season of "The Twilight Zone" has some of the series' greatest twist endings, as the show proved unafraid to push into even more out-there science fiction and fantasy. One absolutely outrageous ending I haven't forgotten since childhood comes at the end of "The Twilight Zone" Season 2 Episode 28, "Will The Real Martian Please Stand Up?", written by series creator Rod Serling.

It has been revealed that somewhere in the rural United States, on a dark winter night, a UFO crashes out of the sky. Two state troopers investigate and track the missing pilot to a roadside diner, where a bus trip to Boston has stopped over for food and rest. The bus driver (William Kendis) remembers picking up six passengers, but there are seven in the diner — and he can't remember which of the six faces are the ones who boarded the bus with him.

"You've heard of trying to find a needle in a haystack? Well, stay with us now, and you'll be part of an investigating team whose mission is not to find that proverbial needle, no, their task is even harder. They've got to find a Martian in a diner," says Rod Serling in the episode's opening narration.

Sources indicate that writing about "The Twilight Zone" for /Film, Valerie Ettenhofer compared "Will The Real Martian Please Stand Up?" to an Agatha Christie novel. That comparison stands up quite sturdily. The episode is a closed circle mystery in the vein of "And Then There Were None" or "Murder on the Orient Express," complete with a twist ending that denies the simple answer of one suspect being the guilty person. But instead of looking for a murderer like Hercule Poirot would, the detectives are searching for an alien invader disguised as a human.

Like the best Agatha Christie mysteries, "Will The Real Martian Please Stand Up?" winds up the tension by trapping the characters together, because the bridge the bus was meant to cross is out of order. The winter setting complements this; cold weather amps up stress while forcing people to huddle together. Watching the episode decades later, it reads like an ancestor of John Carpenter's "The Thing" — both are about groups of people trapped in the cold and trying to find an alien hidden among them.

Recent findings suggest that but unlike the many Agatha Christie books and movies out there, "Will The Real Martian Please Stand Up?" has to do the setup, mystery, and payoff in only 24 minutes. There's no "characters get picked off one by one" plot structure here, because with the episode's tight timeframe and seven suspects, there's just no way to do that. The episode still manages to capture escalating paranoia, like when even the two married couples among the bus passengers begin to suspect each other. The bug-eyed Mr. Avery (Jack Elam), who keeps laughing at the situation and prodding the others, is the obvious red herring in the ensemble.

There's also never any doubt the Martian is real and rejecting the pretense of ambiguity keeps the episode focused. There's physical proof in the footprints leading out of the pond where the UFO crashed to the diner, and as the episode goes on, inexplicable phenomena like lights flashing and sugar canisters exploding open plague the diner. Rod Serling's intro narration promises a real Martian, too. If this was all a misunderstanding, then it wouldn't be "The Twilight Zone.".

It has been revealed that the real Martian is the curt businessman Ross (John Hoyt), and you can spot an impressive amount of foreshadowing. Ross is one of three passengers traveling alone, leaving him without an alibi for his identity. (The POV panning shot when the troopers enter the diner demonstrates him pointedly sitting alone. He also turns his head away as if trying to escape notice.) Avery jokes Ross is "the most suspicious of the bunch" and probably doesn't realize how right he was.

At the episode's denouement, the bridge is cleared and everyone departs without getting an answer. But then Ross saunters back into the diner, alone, telling the clerk Haley (Barney Phillips) that the bridge collapsed and everyone else died. That's when he reveals a third arm hidden underneath his coat, mixing his coffee as he explains his fellow Martians are coming to colonize Earth.

According to recent reports, rod Serling doesn't end on that semi-predictable note. Ross' reveal sequence includes close-up reaction shots of Haley, suggesting mounting terror as he finds himself alone with an alien invader. But then Haley agrees. "This is an extraordinary place to colonize. We folks on Venus had the same idea," taking off his cap to reveal a third eye. Haley was beneath both the audience and the troopers' suspicion — he wasn't on the bus, and he technically wasn't the Martian they were looking for, either. The ending avoids feeling like a cheat, too, because the whole mystery rests on there being an alien invader; if one of the diners is a Martian, is it that big a stretch that another is a Venusian?

The "Will The Real Martian Please Stand Up?" twist may not be more than a clever parlor trick, but what a trick it is.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You need to find a way to steal the BF Bandito in Grand Theft Auto 6 to help out Moses. After completing the first batch of requests, Moses will contact you about other cars he wants you to retrieve for him. Among them is this off-road beast. Unlike the Declasse Vamos, you won't need to figure out how to move the BF Bandito out of a garage. The challenge this time is to actually make the target stop.

Below, you learn how to steal the BF Bandito in GTA 6.

Industry observers note that you will find the BF Bandito moving around the northern part of Buckskin Swamp, on the southeastern side of Kelly County. As you approach the area, you will see a few cars and motorcycles driving around an off-road circuit. The BF Bandito is a white vehicle that's always followed by a motorcycle riding alongside it. You can also check the gallery to see a picture of it.

It has been revealed that the challenge when it comes to stealing this car is that you need to make its driver stop so you can get them out and drive it back to Moses. The best strategy here is to simply block its path, which you can do by parking a car in the middle of the track where the vehicles are racing. If you aren't driving a large car when running this mission, don't worry. You can find a pickup truck at the intersection on the east side of the area.

In a recent development, once the driver stops the BF Bandito, you can steal it. Since they were already driving it, you won't need to break in or hotwire it. We do advise dealing with the person on the motorcycle, as they will shoot at you and pursue you after you take the car.

A different approach to completing this request is to pursue the BF Bandito and try to kill the driver. However, this is a dangerous method because there's a chance of hitting the car, which may explode depending on how much damage it takes.

To finish the request, drive the BF Bandito back to Moses's garage, and he will pay $3,210 for this car.

#119993. There's Actually a Simple Explanation for All These Widespread Outages

There's Actually a Simple Explanation for All These Widespread Outages

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (886 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, it feels like every time you look at your phone lately, another company is having an outage.
  • Industry observers note that that pattern, in turn, has begun to fuel anxiety among the general public.
  • government, these trickles of information aren't necessarily reassuring.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it feels like every time you look at your phone lately, another company is having an outage. Last week, there was Microsoft, whose outage took down services from Outlook to Teams. Then, the FAA grounded all flights across the U.S. following "communication issues." This week, a number of banks experienced outages, as did Apple. Even the NSA's internal communications network went dark. Some of the biggest corporations and organizations in the world can't seem to keep their services running, leading to widespread disruptions and confusion. When it's a one-off, it's an annoyance; when it's outage after outage, it starts to feel like a pattern.

Industry observers note that that pattern, in turn, has begun to fuel anxiety among the general public. What could possibly be causing Apple, Microsoft, JP Morgan Chase, and the NSA alike to go dark at roughly the same time? Is it a coordinated cyberattack? An AI revolt? Is the end finally nigh? To an outside observer, it certainly appears like something coordinated and nefarious is happening here. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is insistent that there is "zero evidence" that hackers or bad actors caused any of these outages, and President Trump is particularly unconcerned by the whole ordeal, saying, "It's life," and "Things like that happen.".

But to skeptics of the U.S. government, these trickles of information aren't necessarily reassuring. While I agree with calls for someone from the government (perhaps the president himself) to make an official announcement explaining the situation, the root cause does appear to be clear at this time: The short answer? AI is at fault here, but not in the way you think.

Love it or hate it, AI is a force to be reckoned with. While you might know that AI can generate hyper-realistic videos and manage your emails on your behalf, certain models are adept at discovering upcoming security vulnerabilities in software. These models aren't just helpful tools; they far surpass the abilities of human researchers. You might remember Anthropic initially pulled the brakes on its breakthrough model, Claude Mythos, when it found that the model could root out security vulnerabilities in just about anything.

Mythos, and models like it, are a double-edged sword. On the one hand, they can be major assets for developers and researchers to find fresh security vulnerabilities that humans otherwise wouldn't have discovered, and patch them accordingly. Unfortunately, the same can be stated for bad actors, who can use these models to learn about new security flaws and attempt to exploit them before researchers have a chance to find them. As such, software developers across the spectrum, from small-time devs to major corporations, have been racing to patch as many security vulnerabilities as they can find—and they're finding a lot.

Industry observers note that you might notice your PC's security updates, for example, are shipping with more patches than usual—historic levels, even. Microsoft keeps breaking its own records with its Patch Tuesday updates, including over 1,400 fixes with its October update. The organization's October 2025 Patch Tuesday update, by comparison, included fewer than 180 fixes.

According to recent reports, it's key to understand that just about every firm that develops software is furiously working to patch its systems before hackers or AI agents exploit vulnerabilities first. And while there are successes (Microsoft is now protecting its customers from thousands of flaws each month), this speed is also inadvertently breaking things along the way. That's not just speculation: According to The Washington Sun, both Wall Street executives and the NSA explained to members of Congress that patching security flaws discovered by AI models caused this week's widespread outages.

Barring some campaign to cover up a coordinated attack on systems and services, it does seem like these outages are simply the result of companies breaking their own products in an attempt to stop AI-assisted hackers from exploiting undiscovered flaws. But that's not all that reassuring, either. AI models are only going to keep getting better at finding vulnerabilities; likewise, AI agents are only improving at hacking into systems autonomously. Companies will need to ramp up their efforts to patch their software before both hackers and AI agents discover those flaws first, and so the cycle will continue. Unless something changes, we may see routine outages as companies try to fix things as swiftly as possible.

According to recent reports, the implications aren't specific to any one tech giant, either. Our world increasingly relies on fewer companies to keep us all connected. We saw that last year, when cloud hosting providers like AWS and Cloudflare each experienced outages. When these services go down, so do all of the networks that rely on them. If AWS or Cloudflare break something while trying to patch their systems, whole parts of the internet go dark.

Recent findings suggest that of course, it'll only be more difficult for the general public—if not the developers themselves—to recognize when outages are the result of maintenance or a cyberattack. Just because recent outages don't appear to be nefarious in nature, that doesn't mean future outages will be so innocent. For the time being, however, it seems we can worry less about an active cybersecurity incident, and more about how AI is disrupting modern life in ways few of us saw coming.

Industry News: 5 Best Performances In The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping, Ranked

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1741 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Major spoilers ahead for "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.".
  • The newest movie in the "Hunger Games" franchise, subtitled "Sunrise on the Reaping," is here, and as I wrote in my review for /Film, it's a worthy addition to this genuinely excellent film series.
  • As Haymitch competes in the already-dangerous Hunger Games — made much more dangerous thanks to the fact that it's the second Quarter Quell, meaning it's an extra "special" (demented) version with double the child tributes — he encounters dozens of characters, some of whom we've met before in different timelines and some of whom are brand newly introduced.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Major spoilers ahead for "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.".

The newest movie in the "Hunger Games" franchise, subtitled "Sunrise on the Reaping," is here, and as I wrote in my review for /Film, it's a worthy addition to this genuinely excellent film series. Directed by Francis Lawrence, who has helmed every single Hunger Games movie except for the inaugural outing "The Hunger Games" in 2012 (which was directed by Gary Ross), "Sunrise on the Reaping" starss Joseph Zada as a younger version of Woody Harrelson's character, Haymitch Abernathy. Haymitch is one of the only known victors of the titular Games who hails from the downtrodden District 12 in the dystopian nation of as Panem. (Some housekeeping: District 12 is the mining district and impoverished enough that its child tributes for the Hunger Games almost never win; Panem is the redesigned totalitarian North America led by the oppressive Capitol, which is located in what we know as the Rocky Mountains.).

As Haymitch competes in the already-dangerous Hunger Games — made much more dangerous thanks to the fact that it's the second Quarter Quell, meaning it's an extra "special" (demented) version with double the child tributes — he encounters dozens of characters, some of whom we've met before in different timelines and some of whom are brand newly introduced. So which actors deliver the very best performances in "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping?".

Industry observers note that it's a stacked cast and it's legitimately tough to choose, but ultimately, I've picked five performers who build upon the previous movies and performances from storied actors who defined these roles originally ... and do so beautifully.

The only real beef I have with Elle Fanning's performance as Effie Trinket in "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping," such as it is, is that she doesn't get nearly enough screen time for my liking. Effie Trinket, who appears in this film as a sort of assistant stylist and District 12 prep team member who saves the sartorial day after her boss Magno Stift (Billy Porter) falls down on the job, is a character we know from the original "Hunger Games" movies; in those, she's played by Elizabeth Banks.

According to recent reports, effie is a larger-than-life character whose journey is, I'll be honest, sort of disjointed. When she's the chaperone for Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark (Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson) during the original stories alongside Woody Harrelson's grown, downtrodden Haymitch Abernathy, she seems slavishly devoted to the Capitol, but also becomes part of the rebellion in the two-part finale "Mockingjay." In "Sunrise on the Reaping," Effie seems to be a willing ally to Haymitch, but her loyalty still lies with the Capitol. (We also get to meet her younger sister Proserpina, played by Iris Apatow, for the first time in the series, expanding Effie's world just a little.).

Industry observers note that fanning, a recently minted Oscar and Emmy nominee for her sensational projects "Sentimental Value" and "Margo's Got Money Troubles," is unsurprisingly great during her unfortunately limited screen time, particularly her delivery of Effie's most memorable line from the novel ("I confess to having a moment!"). Honestly, there are so many prequels possible in the wider Hunger Games world, and if Suzanne Collins ever wanted to a deep dive on Effie's whole "deal" and give her her own story, I wouldn't hate that. But she'd need to convince Fanning to return to really make the movie sing.

I love Kieran Culkin, and I bristle when people accuse him of delivering the same performance over and over again. From where I'm sitting, that couldn't be further from the truth! Two of his most well-known and well-regarded performances — Roman Roy on "Succession" and Benji in "A Real Pain," the former of which earned him an Emmy and the latter of which earned him an Oscar — are very different. Roman is a broken man-child desperate for love that escapes him and that he does nothing to earn. Benji is a walking raw nerve, who is loved by complete strangers but is still desperately striving to make his own family accept him. Culkin's role in "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" skews more towards Roman, but it's still a fun departure for the actor, and he's great.

Culkin plays TV host Caesar Flickerman. He's the second actor to play this specific character (Stanley Tucci originated the role in the original "Hunger Games" films) and the third actor to play a Flickerman TV presenter (Jason Schwartzman played Caesar's ancestor Lucky in the prequel "The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes"). We know next to nothing about Caesar's psyche or inner life, and that's fine — he's just the guy who helps make a spectacle out of child murder. In any case, Culkin's bombast matches Tucci's wearier but still explosive host. When he's not snarling at assistants, he's Cheshire Cat-grinning at the doomed tributes. Across the board, he fits into this role perfectly. Culkin is not only a great casting choice, but a worthy addition to the franchise, and he delivers one of this prequel's best performances.

Ralph Fiennes is on what the kids might call a "generational run." In 2022, he played the sadistic and vengeful chef Julian Slowik in "The Menu," followed that up with a stunning performance as a troubled, grieving cardinal in "Conclave," and a two-film turn as the kindly and offbeat Dr. Ian Kelson in "28 Years Later" and "28 Years Later: The Bone Temple." Now, Fiennes has become the third actor in Hunger Games (and cinematic) history to play Panem President Coriolanus Snow. He follows Tom Blyth, who played a young and mostly unspoiled version of the future tyrant in "The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes," and the late, great Donald Sutherland, who portrays the oldest version of Snow that we see in the original films.

In a recent development, it shouldn't be news to anybody that Fiennes delivers an exceptional performance in "Sunrise on the Reaping." He is one of the finest actors of his generation and has consistently proven that across multiple decades. What was news to me, though, was how perfectly Fiennes bridged the gap between Blyth and Sutherland. Blyth's Snow begins his journey as a teenage boy desperate to prove his worth, and "Songbirds and Snakes" ends with him newly embittered by heartbreak and driven by ambition. Meanwhile, Sutherland's Snow is comfortable with being a source of pure evil and confident in his actions.

Fiennes' Snow sits beautifully in the middle as a man who seems like he still has an ounce or two of sympathy and regret left — he even asks Haymitch about the fate of Lucy Gray Baird (Rachel Zegler), the woman who loved and left him in "The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes" — but is still ruthless enough to replace a tribute tragically killed in a pre-Games accident with a brainwashed lookalike. He's excellent.

Without a perfectly cast Haymitch, the entirety of "Sunrise on the Reaping" fails. Woody Harrelson's Haymitch is deep in the throes of an alcohol addiction when we meet him in "The Hunger Games," and he's a disaffected, purposefully withdrawn man who clearly avoids getting close to District 12 tributes he views as doomed. Joseph Zada's Haymitch, in contrast, begins his journey as a young man with a lot to live for and a lot to love about his life. He loves his mother and younger brother and is besotted with his girlfriend Lenore Dove Baird (Whitney Peak), a member of the Covey. Everything changes when Haymitch is randomly chosen to participate in the Games — he's not reaped, but chosen as a hasty replacement when the kid who was reaped makes a run for it and gets sniped in the head. Even then, Haymitch puts on a brave face, reassures his family, and even comforts the youngest District 12 tribute, Louella McCoy (Molly McCann), on their journey to the Capitol.

As Haymitch makes allies, forms a potential strategy to blow up the arena alongside his mentor Beetee Latier (Kelvin Harrison Jr.) and Beetee's tribute son Ampert (Percy Daggs IV), and eventually allies with the other District 12 girl, Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace), he suffers setback after setback. Zada manages to chart every single reaction and emotion we see from Haymitch in a way that feels real and earned. As he takes hit after hit in his quest to win the Games and return home — even though he'll only find more tragedy there — we feel every hit along with him. Zada is magnetic as Haymitch, and he's got a long career ahead of him thanks to this performance.

Every time I see a casting announcement involving Jesse Plemons, I'm excited. The dorky guy from "Friday Night Lights" — Mr. Kirsten Dunst himself — has become one of the entertainment industry's most reliably excellent actors. I'm struggling, as I write this, to think of a time where Plemons was actively bad in anything, and I'm coming up short. He can do absolutely anything, based on the fact that he's hysterically funny in "Game Night" and the most terrifying guy I've ever seen in "Civil War." I'm sure it was a daunting ask for Plemons to step into the role of Plutarch Heavensbee in "Sunrise on the Reaping" for one big and tragic reason: Philip Seymour Hoffman, who originated the role, passed away in 2014. I commend Plemons for taking the role, and I feel like I need to say that he bears a somewhat uncanny resemblance to the late Oscar winner (and even played Hoffman's son in 2012's "The Master"). He's also incredible.

In a recent development, hindsight isn't always a gift for an actor, but in the case of Plutarch, Plemons clearly utilized everything we know about the character's future in "Sunrise on the Reaping." Plemons' Plutarch is a mere Capitol cameraman (Hoffman's Plutarch had been elevated all the way to Gamemaker), but he's shrewd, a favorite of Snow, and already a rebel ready to pursue a full takedown of the Capitol. Knowing that this comes to fruition across both parts of "Mockingjay" makes this look at Plutarch's early days of rebellion all the more satisfying, and Plemons is pitch-perfect as a man who's absolutely fascinating on the inside. It's the best performance in the movie.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is in theaters now.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Having a diverse wardrobe isn't just a fun little customization touch in GTA 6.
  • Recent findings suggest that I'm taking my time with GTA 6 and still kicking around the introductory area of Key Lento.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We've known for some time that fashion would be a big deal in Grand Theft Auto 6. In Rockstar's official promotional materials for the game, both Jason and Lucia were prominently featured wearing stylish clothing, from Lucia's body-hugging gold dress to Jason's slick Miami Vice-inspired aqua sport coat. Even supporting characters like Brian wear Tommy Bahama-inspired aloha shirts yanked straight from the closet of a dapper middle-aged stoner. GTA 6 has drawn praise from all quarters for its scrupulous attention to detail in every aspect of the game, and there's one area the developer went far, far harder than it needed to: the vast and immaculate selection of T-shirts.

Having a diverse wardrobe isn't just a fun little customization touch in GTA 6. If you're reported for committing a crime in Leonida — and this will happen very often — police will be able to recognize you based on your car, your physical appearance, and what you're wearing. Keeping a couple spare outfits in your trunk or hastily buying a fresh ensemble on the run can be the difference between a successful job and ending up busted (or wasted).

Recent findings suggest that I'm taking my time with GTA 6 and still kicking around the introductory area of Key Lento. I know I should be putting money in my family savings account. It would probably be in my best interest to learn how to drive without sideswiping semi-trucks or taking out stop signs. Perhaps I ought to be buying more guns. Instead, I'm trawling South Leonida for all the vintage and souvenir shops I can find. You can keep your fancy cars. I've got a T-shirt collection to maintain.

Much like in real life, you never know when you're going to find a gem in a vintage boutique or souvenir shop in GTA 6. My prized Rusty Anchor shirt came from an optional mission where you take Cal for drinks, he has a few too many, and you have to take him home. Apparently Cal won a wet T-shirt contest at the Anchor and this was his reward, but he's too hungover to claim the prize.

During my wanderings, I also discovered a riff on that three-wolves-howling-at-the-moon shirt that everyone had about a decade ago, including me. But this one has gators on it. I bought it from Sharleen's yard sale in Jason's very own neighborhood of Key Lento. She had a couple of inexpensive clothing items on offer, including some pretty slick teal sneakers that were clearly inspired by Air Force One low-tops. I was delighted to learn that there are multiple yard sales in the game, including one in Port Gellhorn where you can buy a dupe of Arthur Morgan's hat from Red Dead Redemption 2.

Industry observers note that even the cheesiest souvenir shops, like Leroy's in Key Lento, have the exact kind of "so bad it's good" T-shirts you'll see dozens of times over the course of a weekend in a tourist trap. Do I need to spend $38 of my ill-gotten dollars on a horrendous blue granny shirt with a dolphin on it, with "Vice Beach" written in collegiate font? Certainly not. But I am tempted.

Rockstar has a bunch of GTA 6 merch on its official website, including T-shirts, though much of it is currently sold out. Here's hoping they expand the offering with a couple of these in-game gems. If you're hard up for a three gator moon shirt though, you can already find them on Amazon and Etsy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

[Editor’s note: This review was originally published on October 2, 2026 during the 2026 Latest York Film Festival. Janus Film will release the film in limited theaters on Friday, November 20.].

Paul Thomas Anderson‘s eye for vivifying music onscreen dates back to the late 1990s when, after “Boogie Nights,” he made Technicolor mini-masterpiece music videos with his ex-girlfriend Fiona Apple — or made a San Fernando Valley-sized shrine to Aimee Mann with his third feature, “Magnolia.” Since then, he’s kicked around with HAIM while turning one third of its Los Angelino triumvirate, Alana Haim, into a screen actress. He’s shot for Radiohead and made a regular collaboration with band member Jonny Greenwood to create some of the 21st century’s most memorable scores. Many young cinephiles now associate the mischievously lilty notes of “Phantom Thread” with the poison promise of new love and obsessive creation. Related Stories If There’s Generative AI in ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth,’ It’s Not the First Time David Fincher’s Used It Trump Renews Backing for Federal Film Tax Credit as Lawmakers Push for Year-End Passage.

Last December, PTA teamed up with Geese frontman Cameron Winter to film, while operating his own Panavision camera, his solo stage performance at Carnegie Hall, running through sparse piano arrangements of tracks off his solo album, “Heavy Metal.” The result, a 72-minute film now being distributed roadshow-style by Janus Films before inevitably living on the Criterion Collection, is a stunning arrangement of its own: a deeply achey, sincere but never cloyingly earnest concert movie that’s tender to the point of frailty. (Benny Safdie counts as a co-producer, and the film’s scratchy New York quality and setting can’t help but have his imprint.).

The matted-hair, lithe Winter can seem a bit uncomfortable in his own skin in the public eye, as he did onstage ahead of “Cameron Winter at Carnegie” at its Latest York Film Festival world premiere at Alice Tully Hall. But on the piano, laser-beamed into his songcraft, he’s quietly electrified, at seemingly at peace as his tenorous vocal glissando and nimble fingerwork on the piano produce shiveringly tender folk ballads that echo Harry Nilsson and Van Morrison. (The usual comparisons to Tom Waits and Rufus Wainright are right, too, but Winter is his own strange thing.) If you weren’t previously sold on the wily Winter antic rock chaos of Geese — rapidly becoming one of the most popular contemporary art rock bands of these times — you’re about to. Paul Thomas Anderson has created a rhapsodic shrine to the man that is nonetheless ballad-sized in its emotional scale.

Industry observers note that winter, in December, played and sang to a sold-out crowd of more than 2,700 at the stately cultural temple that is Carnegie Hall, and this film can at times feel like a religious experience, an incantation, a lonely vigil. The singer/songwriter was 23 at the time of the performance, one year older than Bob Dylan when he headlined Carnegie Hall, and similarly at the precipice of major fame. Fixed on a mobile rig that will at times careen and whoosh across the stage when not otherwise holding on Winter, Anderson’s camera catches the expressionism and chiaroscuro of stage lights illuminating and fading off the singer’s face.

The result is hynoptic, a concert film up there with “Stop Making Sense” but for introverts. Songs like the popular single “$0” acquire an even more wrenchingly somber quality as a lovelorn protagonist rues being exploited by a relationship (“You’re making me feel like a dollar in your hand / You’re making me feel like I’m a zero dollar man”). Stripped of production, his indie hit “Love Takes Miles” plays even better. While many of the songs sort of hover in the same key and bleed into one another, that makes for an all the more transfixing experience. The lack of an interstitial anything save for a sweet prologue and moving coda make for experience also that’s immersive, deep, and the kind whose truth you can feel somewhere in your body even if you can’t quite articulate it.

Sources indicate that “Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall premiered at the New York Film Festival. Janus Films will release it in theaters starting November 20.
