If you do count yourself among the many fans of House of the Dragon, there's a new release that celebrates one of its coolest winged beasts, Caraxes.

According to recent reports, over on the Iron Studios website, the manufacturer of physical memorabilia has confirmed that pre-orders are now open for Caraxes - House of the Dragon - Icons, a new highly-detailed polystone rendition of Daemon's dragon. The figure clocks in at 14" (H) x 10.9" (W) x 13.3" (D), making it the perfect size for display area at home, without taking up too much space.

The official description for the statue reads as follows:.

"Inspired by the acclaimed HBO series House of the Dragon, Caraxes joins the Icons line from Iron Studios. Known as the Blood Wyrm, Caraxes is one of the most fearsome dragons in the world of Westeros and serves as the mount of Daemon Targaryen.

"This collectible faithfully recreates the dragon's distinctive appearance, featuring his elongated neck, powerful wings, menacing expression, and unique serpentine physique. The detailed sculpt captures the creature's imposing presence, while the themed display base enhances the dramatic presentation inspired by the Targaryen legacy. Expertly crafted and hand-painted, this statue is a must-have for fans of the series and collectors of fantasy-themed collectibles.".

Recent findings suggest that if you aren't familiar with Caraxes' story, he's widely known as the Blood Wyrm thanks to his blood-red scales, serpentine build, and immense ferocity. First claimed by Prince Aemon Targaryen, he spent many years without a rider after his death before being claimed by Daemon, and playing a crucial role throughout the events of House of the Dragon.

By the time of the events of Game of Thrones, some 170 to 200 years later, dragons are seemingly entirely a thing of the past, until Daenerys hatches her three eggs and rules the skies (until she doesn't).

In a recent development, as mentioned earlier, the statue is currently available for pre-order, with an expected release date of April—June 2027. It's also worth noting that the images included in the listing are of the current design, which is still awaiting approval from the licensor. It's also not cheap, coming in at a considerable $399.99, though in this case you are paying for the quality.

As for the final season of House of the Dragon, there's a bit of a wait for that as well, with the final season not expected to debut until 2028 (though we don't have anything more specific than that just yet).

Taking place about 172 years before the events of Game of Thrones, House of the Dragon tells the tale of the rise of the Targaryens, the only family of dragonlords to survive the Doom of Valyria.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” made quick work of the competition, debuting to an impressive $120 million and easily capturing the top spot on the domestic box office chart.

Recent findings suggest that the sequel represents a massive improvement on the opening of its predecessor, 2023’s “The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes,” which bowed with $44 million, a franchise low. However, “Sunrise on the Reaping” didn’t match the highs of the series. Its opening pales in comparison to 2013’s “Catching Fire” ($158 million debut), 2012’s OG “Hunger Games” ($152.5 million), and 2014’s “Mockingjay Part 1” ($121.8 million debut). Deadline trumpeted the fact that the film has the second highest-grossing opening for a prequel behind “Rogue One,” which seems like a milestone no one really ever thought or cared about before. So extra credit to some enterprising studio publicist or Google for unearthing that gem. Related Stories Box Office: A24’s ‘You Can See Everything’ Crosses $100 Million Globally If There’s Generative AI in ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth,’ It’s Not the First Time David Fincher’s Used It.

According to recent reports, but whatever records it holds, “Sunrise on the Reaping” has revived a series that was looking a little long in the tooth. Why did this “Hunger Games” outpace “The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes”? It probably helped that franchise icons Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson, and Woody Harrelson were coaxed back for brief appearances. There was also a top-shelf cast that included Oscar winner Kieran Culkin, Oscar nominees Glenn Close, Elle Fanning, Ralph Fiennes, and Jesse Plemons, and rising stars like Iris Apatow, Mckenna Grace, Ben Wang, and Joseph Zada. Internationally, “Sunrise on the Reaping” earned $105 million from 84 territories, pushing its worldwide box office gross to $225 million.

Lionsgate is distributing the $150 million production, as it has the previous films. The studio recently mounted something of a comeback under Adam Fogelson, who replaced Joe Drake as the motion picture chief in 2024. Lionsgate was on its back foot at the time, having released flops like “Borderlands” and the reboot of “The Crow.” In recent months, its fortunes have shifted thanks to blockbusters like “Michael” and hits such as “The Housemaid” and “The Long Walk.” A revived “Hunger Games” franchise is critical, as it gives Lionsgate another pillar for its slate.

But “The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes” success threatened to overshadow “I Play Rocky.” The Amazon MGM Studios release earned $9.3 million after expanding from 29 locations to 2,477 theaters. It’s playing like gangbusters, earning an A+ CinemaScore, a rare distinction that puts it in the company of “Top Gun: Maverick” and “The Avengers.” The word-of-mouth is clearly excellent, which could help it build momentum over the holidays. It’s also worth noting that “I Play Rocky” is catering to older moviegoers who take their time getting around to seeing things. Even if it starts to fade, “I Play Rocky” is a relatively economical bet. It cost in the $30 million range to produce and has earned $10.4 million since it debuted.

Then there’s “Ebenezer.” The Johnny Depp revival isn’t as glorious as his most diehard fans may have hoped. The Christmas story fell roughly 60 percent in its second weekend, earning $7.7 million to bring its domestic total to $32.5 million. But Paramount didn’t spend lavishly to make the film. It only cost $38 million to remind Depp’s Scrooge of the Christmas spirit. “Ebenezer” has also earned $45.9 million internationally, bringing its global total to a respectable $78.4 million.

Among the newcomers, Sumerian Pictures released “Josephine,” a family drama with Gemma Chan and Channing Tatum,” on four screens in New York and Los Angeles this weekend, grossing an estimated $84,200 for a per-screen average of $21,050. The film earned raves at Sundance where it premiered and Sumerian bought it. “Elsinore,” a drama about Ian Charleson’s final stage performance, opened with $240,000 from six locations in New York and Los Angeles for a per-theater average of $40,000. Focus Features is distributing the film, which has earned Oscar buzz for Andrew Scott. Lastly, Janus Films and Criterion debuted Paul Thomas Anderson’s concert film “Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall” in three locations, where it earned $162,000 for $54,000 per-screen average. The film is only showing in 35mm, which limits the number of screenings available to cinephiles and PTA completists.

In a recent development, nearly a month into its release, DC's Clayface has slowed down considerably. The comic book film has delivered a modest performance at the box office so far, and will soon enter the next phase of its journey when it lands on the PVOD market. The movie's box-office run was marred by the sudden announcement that DC Studios co-CEOs James Gunn and Peter Safran, who shepherded the project from its standalone origins and integrated it into the DC Universe franchise, were departing from their positions after four years. Clayface, which revolves around the iconic Batman villain, is the last film of their tenure.

Recent findings suggest that the movie is only the third theatrical release of the one-year-old DC Universe, which began with Gunn's Superman reboot and continued with this summer's Supergirl. Starring David Corenswet, Superman grossed nearly $620 million worldwide against a reported budget of $225 million, which was deemed successful enough for a follow-up to be greenlit. The movie in question, Man of Tomorrow, will be released in 2027.

In a recent development, earlier this year, audiences roundly rejected the Supergirl spin-off feature, starring Milly Alcock and directed by Craig Gillespie. The movie grossed $126 million worldwide against a reported budget of around $180 million. By comparison, Clayface cost around $40 million to produce, and should be able to surpass Supergirl globally this week. However, the movie has lost a significant number of theaters over the last couple of weeks and is about to lose even more.

It'll enter its fifth week of release in 1,147 theaters, down from its opening-week theater count of 3,458. Starring Tom Rhys Harries, Naomi Ackie, and Max Minghella, the movie received mostly positive reviews. It's now sitting at a "Certified Fresh" 78% score on the aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes, where the consensus reads, "Carving out a unique identity for itself in the DCU while closely resembling a litany of body horror classics, Clayface takes time to get going until it eventually morphs into an icky and satisfying revenge thriller.".

Industry observers note that rather unusually for a horror movie, Clayface holds an exceptionally high "Verified Hot" 94% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes. This indicates a bright future on digital, where it's expected to land on December 8. Although the movie didn't break out like many would've liked, it has now tripled its reported budget theatrically. This may be enough for the movie to break even, but it's a fraction of what major superhero movies are able to generate these days. Stay tuned to Collider for more updates.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that one of the various Strangers & Freaks side quests in Grand Theft Auto 6 deals with the legendary Skunk Ape, an elusive sort of Bigfoot-esque creature that's stalking around the swamps in Pelican Valley. Early on, you'll be able to trigger a quest by viewing the signs posted around the starting area and contacting Kirk, eventually tracking down a series of effigies in the swamp.

!!! WARNING: THIS GUIDE HAS SPOILERS FOR THE SKUNK APE MISSION IN GTA 6 !!!After you've found each of these effigies and waited a few days, Kirk will get in contact with you for a meetup in the swamps again, this time with a partner and a helicopter. Jason will have to shoot the Swamp Ape, aka Mr. Mangrove, with a tranquilizer gun from the helicopter, which will cause the creature to run into a shed and collapse. Once Jason tries to pick it up, some very strange things happen.

Sources indicate that first, players will turn into a frog and be required to hop around the docks and eat several flies, and then will be transferred into a fly and be asked to find Kirk, listening in on the Swamp Ape hunter's nefarious plans to use the QR code tattooed on Mr. Mangrove for a large sum of money. When Jason wakes back up, you'll have to choose whether to save Kirk from the Swamp Ape.

Killing Mr. Mangrove the Skunk Ape is the most straightforward option of the bunch, and has the clearest and most immediate reward. First, if you're planning to kill the Swamp Ape, be sure to question Kirk about who Harry Sherrick is by both threatening and questioning him. You'll have found out by now that Kirk was planning on leaving you for dead anyway, so putting a little fear into him isn't all that big of a deal.

Afterward, you can kill Mr. Mangrove and choose to save Kirk. This will result in a monetary reward of anywhere between $10,000 and $12,500 depending on if you questioned/threatened Kirk, and he'll then promise to give you a cut of the QR code payout, but that doesn't end up happening, seeing as the helicopter will explode and Kirk and Noah will die.

It has been revealed that there are actually two different ways to spare the Skunk Ape in this mission, the first being to shoot Kirk with the rifle, which will knock him unconscious. The Skunk Ape will then pick him up and carry him off into the swamp. The second option is to just let the Skunk Ape go ham on Kirk and squeeze his head until it pops. Mr. Mangrove will then carry Kirk's corpse off into the swamp as well.

Seeing as Mr. Mangrove will still be alive, it's very likely he can be found later in the game or even after you've completed the main story and return to Leonida for the Post-Game experience. As of this writing, it isn't clear specifically what this entails, but based on my experience with another Strangers & Freaks mission involving the mutant form of Kyle, there are likely benefits to leaving the Swamp Ape alive.

Recent findings suggest that if sparing Mr. Mangrove is anything like the Hulk-Kyle "Buddy?" quest, my guess is that the Swamp Ape will clear out the Kingfisher drug dens in the swamp area, though this has yet to be confirmed.

Despite not knowing the exact benefits of sparing Mr. Mangrove, it's likely that all the Strangers & Freaks missions have benefits that are immediately clear. While the $12,000 or so seems like a good chunk of change, assuming Mr. Mangrove helps clear out the Kingfisher operations, you'll be able to go into these encampments with zero resistance and arguably benefit more than you would from the cash.

In a recent development, that said, this is only really worth it if you're completing the mission in Chapter 2, as going back to these areas when you're in the later chapters isn't all that much of a challenge anymore. Further, since I haven't been able to confirm the specific results of the Skunk Ape surviving and taking Kirk into the swamp, it'd be understandable if you want to take the cash reward instead.

It's also entirely possible that you can find the Skunk Ape in the endgame and claim the QR code prize that Kirk and Noah were after, though this is purely speculation as of this writing. This GTA 6 guide will be updated as soon as more details become available.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Responding to a question from IndieWire during an in-conversation event at the 23rd Marrakech International Film Festival, the writer/director of “Star Wars: The Last Jedi” was clear that his next project lies elsewhere: “I’m already writing the next thing I’m going to do, and it’s not a Star Wars thing, or in that genre,” he said.
  • Sources indicate that “I’m very much enjoying just making my own stuff, but I mean, if the opportunity presented itself,” Johnson said, nodding.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rian Johnson isn’t writing a Star Wars movie, but he isn’t ruling one out, either.

Responding to a question from IndieWire during an in-conversation event at the 23rd Marrakech International Film Festival, the writer/director of “Star Wars: The Last Jedi” was clear that his next project lies elsewhere: “I’m already writing the next thing I’m going to do, and it’s not a Star Wars thing, or in that genre,” he said.

Sources indicate that “I’m very much enjoying just making my own stuff, but I mean, if the opportunity presented itself,” Johnson said, nodding. “It’s a world I deeply love. It’s also a group of people I love.”.

“I love Star Wars more now than I ever have,” he added. “And it’s exciting to me that there are a lot of different voices now taking cracks at it.” The timing is hard to ignore. Related Stories Box Office: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Debuts to Mighty $120 Million, Reviving Lionsgate’s Most Notable Franchise Box Office: A24’s ‘You Can See Everything’ Crosses $100 Million Globally.

Johnson’s remarks land just as Lucasfilm appears to be turning back toward the corner of the saga he helped shape. Polygon reported that two long-gestating features, “Star Wars: New Jedi Order” and an untitled film from Dave Filoni, are still listed as in development by Production Weekly, despite months of silence and the soft box office performance of “The Mandalorian & Grogu.”.

Recent findings suggest that “New Jedi Order” would theoretically bring back actress Daisy Ridley as Rey roughly 15 years after “The Rise of Skywalker,” rebuilding the Jedi Order that “The Last Jedi” so memorably called into question. Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy is attached to direct, with George Nolfi now writing after earlier drafts from Damon Lindelof and Justin Britt-Gibson, and a stint by Bond 26 screenwriter Steven Knight. The film was pulled from its December 17, 2027 release date in May 2025. Meanwhile, “Star Wars: Starfighter,” the Shawn Levy-directed film starring Ryan Gosling and set five years after “The Rise of Skywalker,” remains the only Star Wars feature with a firm date: May 28, 2027.

Recent findings suggest that in 2017, the year “The Last Jedi” hit theaters, Lucasfilm unveiled that Johnson would create a fresh Star Wars trilogy. Those films have yet to materialize, but Johnson had warm words for Filoni, who took on the role of Lucasfilm’s president and chief creative officer in January: “Dave Filoni I got to know while making ‘The Last Jedi’, and he’s a wonderful guy who really has the spirit of Star Wars in him,” he mentioned. “All the Lucasfilm folks are awesome.”.

Later, answering questions from the audience, Johnson described “The Last Jedi” as “the most joyful process of any movie I’ve ever made”, despite the challenge of stepping from his own original films into what he called a contested mythology.

In a recent development, “I’m a huge, huge fan of George Lucas, and I’ve read a lot about when he was writing the original Star Wars, how personal it was for him,” Johnson continued. “I think especially with something that has a deep cultural impact, and that belongs to everybody, that makes it even more important… to make sure it’s coming from a personal perspective and something that’s deeply on fire inside you, as opposed to thinking, ‘what’s gonna please this person and this person and this person’. That leads to homogeneity, to repeating yourself and to something that feels dead on screen.”.

Recent findings suggest that as a middle chapter, “The Last Jedi” drew directly on Johnson’s childhood experience of “The Empire Strikes Back,” though not as something to copy. “I didn’t want to imitate ‘The Empire Strikes Back’,” Johnson stated. “What I wanted to get to was the heart of what that movie has, which is this center part of life where your job is to fail, and your job is to learn from that and to get up and keep moving forward.”.

He drew a distinction between a film having a moral compass and having a moral. The compass, he stated, “comes from the entire mass of every single creative decision made by the writer, or director, or whole team.”.

Johnson also reflected on the only two composers he has worked with. His cousin Nathan Johnson has scored his films since the pair started making movies together at age ten: “Nathan is the first person to read the script; he’s on set for the entire shoot so it’s very much a collaboration.”.

Recent findings suggest that john Williams, he said, is also “a miracle of a human being”, and working with him was the opposite experience. “You give him the movie and then the first time I hear any music is when we’re on the scoring stage, and there are 200 musicians playing it.”.

Industry observers note that if Johnson does return to Star Wars, it seems he won’t be thinking about franchise strategy. “For me it’s not about thinking about IP, it’s about stories,” he said. “I deeply believe the only way to actually make a movie that matters and is worth something is to have your eyes nowhere else except on making that movie. What is the story we’re telling? Why are we telling it? Why do we care about it?”.

“Outside of that bubble,” Johnson added, “I’ll leave it to the executives.”.

With those executives now steering Star Wars back toward Rey and the post-“Rise of Skywalker” era, the bubble may be closer to his than it has been in years.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that britBox has cemented itself as the place to be for fans of the Queen of Crime, Agatha Christie. One of the freshest and most exciting Christie adaptations is on the way to the platform, as My Lady Jane's Edward Bluemel takes on the role of Hercule Poirot in the upcoming Hercule, written by Benji Walters. The series has been described as an "intimate study" of Poirot himself, with the moustache-twirling crime-solver joined by the likes of Henry Ashton, James D'Arcy, Guy Remmers, and Rivals star Katherine Parkinson.

For Hercule to become BritBox's best Christie series, it will have to take down the brilliant 2026 arrival Tommy & Tuppence, based on the two fictional detectives that recur throughout Christie's work, first appearing in her second novel, 1922's The Secret Adversary. Josh Dylan and Antonia Thomas star in the series, which brings the iconic duo to the modern day, as they become entangled in their own relationship and a string of puzzling mysteries. The series also features Harry Potter's Imelda Staunton.

After impressing in the U.S., the series has finally found a British home in time for Christmas. It's been confirmed that 5 have acquired Tommy & Tuppence, with the six-part series expected to air over the festive season. "Agatha Christie's Tommy and Tuppence brings together everything audiences love about a great mystery: clever plotting, intriguing characters and plenty of twists along the way," wrote 5's Acquisitions and Co-Production Director, Cherry Vantreen, in a statement. Vantreen continued:.

"With its charming central duo and blend of suspense, adventure and wit, it's a fantastic addition to 5's drama offering, and we're delighted to be bringing this classic Agatha Christie title to our viewers.".

Four criminal masterminds. One of them was always going to be yours. Here is who comes for you, why they picked you out of everyone available, and what they want from the encounter.

Your nemesis does not want to beat you. He wants to know you completely, and he is patient enough to wait for it. The frightening part is how good the conversation is.

Your nemesis respects you, which sounds flattering until you work out what it means. He chose you because nobody else was worth his time.

Industry observers note that your nemesis has no personal interest in you whatsoever, and that is precisely what makes him unsurvivable. You are not a rival. You are a stop on the way.

In a recent development, the Guardians of the Galaxy are crossing over with a familiar Marvel character who had never met them. Throughout the decades, the Guardians of the Galaxy have always been a gloriously mismatched ragtag crew of cosmic outcasts from radically different backgrounds. While no longer as famous, the original 31st-century Guardians squad that brought together Vance Astro, Martinex, Yondu, Charlie-27, and Starhawk thrived on clashing alien cultures long before the modern Guardians. When Dan Abnett and Andy Lanning assembled the current incarnation in 2008, the new Guardians doubled down on the eclectic formula with half-human outlaw Star-Lord, deadly Zen-Whoberi assassin Gamora, vengeful warrior Drax, cybernetic raccoon Rocket, and gentle tree-monarch Groot.

Industry observers note that an equally varied lineup of Earth-based and galactic icons has crossed paths with, or temporarily joined, the Guardians of the Galaxy roster over the years. Mutant favorites like Peter Quill's temporary Star-Lord replacement Kitty Pryde, Iron Man, the Thing, Captain Marvel, Angela, Ant-Man, Hercules, and Nova have each suited up as official or honorary members. Beyond their own ranks, the Guardians of the Galaxy have teamed up with Thor, Doctor Strange, Beta Ray Bill, Silver Surfer, Deadpool, the brutal Frank Castle variant known as Cosmic Ghost Rider, and most recently with Spider-Man himself.

Years after welcoming a former villain into their ranks, the Guardians of the Galaxy reunite with a different member of his species.

Sources indicate that in Jordan Morris and Luke Ross’s The Amazing Venom #3, former Spider-Man villain Fred Myers a.k.a. Boomerang, now the red-and-blue symbiote hero Comeback, travels through deep space with his symbiote partner Passenger to reach Klyntar. Running low on fuel, Fred and Passenger make an emergency stop at Knowhere, where Fred compares the local bar to the headquarters he used to share with his fellow Spider-Man rogues, the Bar With No Name. To his understated surprise, he finds Rocket Raccoon fighting the bartender inside.

In a recent development, rocket’s solo presence on Knowhere is a direct result of the Guardians of the Galaxy's disbandment after Jonathan Hickman's Imperial event and Dan Abnett’s Imperial Guardians series. While Peter Quill rules Spartax as Emperor of the Galactic Union and Gamora works to rebuild a proper Guardians roster following Maximus's coup, Rocket works largely on his own. Meanwhile, members like Groot, Drax, and Mantis are still scattered after the original team broke apart. After his team-up with Spider-Man, Rocket Raccoon is acquainted with the wall-crawler's villains, which is why he isn't shocked to see the former Boomerang on Knowhere.

The Guardians of the Galaxy share a notable if surprisingly brief history with the symbiotes, highlighted most prominently during Flash Thompson’s celebrated stint aboard the team in the mid-2010s. Appointed as Earth’s official liaison to Star-Lord’s squad in Brian Michael Bendis’s Guardians of the Galaxy run and Robbie Thompson’s Venom: Space Knight, Agent Venom traveled to Klyntar, where his symbiote was temporarily cleansed of its rage. Besides Flash’s tenure as an "Agent of the Cosmos", the Guardians also crossed paths with symbiote chaos during the Venomized event and later fought off Knull’s symbiote dragons during Al Ewing’s Guardians run in the King in Black crossover.

In a recent development, still, considering how close the Guardians of the Galaxy are to the symbiotes' cosmic nature, it's odd that the Guardians haven't been far closer to symbiote lore. Klyntar is an ancient cosmic civilization tied to Celestials, Gorr the God Butcher, and the same areas of space that heroes like Star-Lord, Gamora, and Rocket patrol every day. Yet, symbiote sagas like Absolute Carnage, King in Black, and Queen in Black have largely unfolded on Earth rather than among the stars. Curiously enough, it takes characters like Fred Myers and Passenger a trip from Earth to Knowhere for a Guardian to meet another symbiote.

Would you like Comeback to become a Guardian of the Galaxy?

Six Things You Should Do Now to Optimize Your Setup for GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1146 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that you’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI.
  • Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 is absurdly large.
  • Alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that you’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI. You’ve preloaded the game on your console, you’ve taken the next month off work, and you’ve locked your phone in a Faraday cage and set it adrift at sea. You’re prepared to lock in, and you haven’t forgotten a thing…right? Well, just to make sure, here are the most important tips to optimize your setup before you fire up the most anticipated game of the decade.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 is absurdly large. According to Rockstar, you’ll need up to 212GB of storage space. For high-end consoles like the PS5 Pro, that’s more than 10% of the available storage space, and close to half the space on the more budget-conscious Xbox Series S. There’s a good chance you’ll have to delete something to make room.

Alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it). External SSDs are probably the cheapest route, though you’ll want to make sure to use a high-speed USB cable to connect it. It’s even worth shopping around for alternate models of SSD. For example, at the time of writing, the popular 2TB WD_BLACK external drive was close to $200, but the exact same drive in pink was $132.

You can also directly upgrade the storage of your console with expansion drives. The Xbox Series X|S supports proprietary expansion cards, while the PS5 and PS5 Pro can accept most M.2 internal SSDs. These will generally be faster, since they plug directly into the console via higher-speed connections than a drive hooked up via USB.

Let’s face it: Half the fun of any sandbox game is the weird, unique stuff that happens to only you. So you’re probably going to be hitting that “record recent gameplay” button more often than usual. While you’re cleaning up your storage space (or adding more), make sure to account for all the video clips you might want to save.

Sources indicate that file size of video clips depends on a lot of factors, but 4K recordings can generally take up to 0.5GB per minute of footage. You can cut that down by saving footage in 1080p instead, but either way you’ll want to leave a little extra space.

Game footage is also a pretty good place to look if you need to make room on your console and don’t want to delete any games. Be honest with yourself: You don’t need all those clips from Horizon Forbidden West you saved four years ago. Dive into the settings on your console and find the biggest media files you forgot you even had on there.

According to Rockstar, GTA 6 will be targeting 30fps across consoles at launch, which is pretty low as modern AAA games go. Part of the reason for that is all the processing power going to rendering a complex environment, but it also means you won’t need a fancy high frame rate TV or monitor any time soon to get the most out of it. Still, it couldn’t hurt to check a few settings on your display.

It has been revealed that first, make sure you’re using a higher refresh rate than 30Hz. While the game is targeting 30fps, it is technically capable of more, so if your console can keep up, you don’t want to accidentally bottleneck your frames. This setting will vary by device, so check the manual that came with your screen.

According to recent reports, also, make sure you have HDR enabled on your hardware. There’s a good chance this is already turned on for your TV, but sometimes other devices can switch display modes if they only support SDR. The game will help you calibrate your HDR settings for GTA 6 specifically when you launch it, but only if it detects HDR compatibility in the first place.

If you’re planning to buy a console specifically for GTA 6, this might be one of those rare instances where a PS5 Pro really is worth the upgrade. According to Rockstar, certain features like ray-traced shadows will only be available on the Pro version of Sony’s console.

More importantly, the PS5 Pro version supports PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (or PSSR), which upscales lower-resolution images to get better detail and higher frame rates out of the same hardware. Given that GTA 6 is already starting at a meager target of 30fps on most consoles, anything that can give your frame rate a boost is probably going to feel like a welcome improvement over the baseline.

I’ll tell you a secret as someone who’s spent a lot of time testing different game controllers: Most of the time, you really don’t need an expensive “elite” controller. Most of the time. I don’t buy into the idea that a taller control stick is going to make you an esports athlete. It can be nice to have, but it’s not a game changer. What does matter is customizing your controls, especially for long gaming sessions.

The DualSense Edge wireless controller is a favorite of mine, mainly because of the rear paddles and adjustable triggers. The former lets you map any button to a rear lever that you can access with your fingers underneath the controller, which can often ease some of the wrist strain of awkward button combos. And the adjustable triggers let you activate the buttons with less motion, again reducing repetitive stress.

It has been revealed that the Xbox Elite Series 2 controller has similar features for the Xbox, as well as custom caps for the D-pad. Both consoles’ versions of pro controllers are more expensive than the standard ones, but if you’re planning to game for many hours, it can be worth it to get a controller that’s more comfortable for you.

It has been revealed that if you have an Xbox One, you don’t necessarily have to upgrade your console to play GTA 6, but you might want to take a look at your network. GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on day one, and you’ll be able to stream the game to an Xbox One console (as long as you purchase Cloud playtime as well or get some with your Game Pass subscription). This is the only way to play on a console older than the current generation, so if you don’t want to shell out for new hardware, this might be your best bet.

Recent findings suggest that xbox recommends a minimum of a 20Mbps connection to run cloud gaming, but more is obviously better. If you can connect your console to a wired Ethernet connection, that would be better and provide more stability. If you can’t connect a cable, then at least make sure you’re well within range of your wifi router, and try to limit any other bandwidth-hogging applications on the network while you’re playing.

Recent findings suggest that black Friday is usually a great time to grab a upcoming e-reader, but the ongoing RAM crisis has made that a question mark this year: Amazon recently raised the prices of all its Kindles by around $50 and refreshed the entire lineup, which means your odds of grabbing one at a big discount are low. But you aren't totally out of luck: If you haven't noticed, micro-e-readers—I'm talking credit card-sized, with screens that measure around four inches—are all the rage in 2026, and right now, you can pick up one of them for around $55.

Sources indicate that if you too can see the appeal of carrying all of your books with you on a device so small you'll forget it's even in your pocket, it's a great time to jump in: The recently released Xteink X4 Classic is right now 38% off for Black Friday, bringing it down to $54.87, a record-low price. Meanwhile, the smaller X3 is $55.72, or 19% off. Both are available in either "mist grey" or "space black." The discounts should last through the end of Cyber Monday on Nov. 30.

Xteink is a Chinese startup that shook up the e-reading world last year with the launch of the X4, a super bare-bones device that made up for its lack of features and usability with a cheap sub-$70 price point. Since then, a huge online community of fans has formed, sharing tips on Reddit and even coming together to crowdsource an alternate operating system that fixed a lot of early problems. Xteink quickly followed up the X4 with a slate of other devices, including the 3.7-inch X3 and the X4 Pro, which adds a front light and touchscreen (at the cost of screen clarity and two physical buttons).

In a recent development, the X4 Classic and the X3 improve on the original X4 with quality-of-life upgrades like a larger battery, relocated page-turn buttons, a real-time clock, and a tilt-to-turn-page feature. They're also lighter and thinner than the X4, though there is a trade-off involved: They drop the USB-C charging port in favor of magnetic pogo pins that require a separate adapter (included).

These upgrades also increased the cost: The X4 Classic typically retails for $89, $20 more than the discontinued X4 and only $10 less than the X4 Pro, while the X3 rolled out at $79. But right now, the X4 Classic is just under $55, or around 38% off, and the X3 is about a dollar more. Either is a great option for those who prioritize crisp, readable text above the conveniences of a built-in light or touchscreen, as those add extra layers between the inner screen and outer glass. It's also important to understand what you're getting into: These devices support only e-books without Digital Rights Management (DRM), which means you can't use it to read your existing library of Kindle books. On the plus side, there's no longer a need to worry about flashing newly introduced firmware if you don't want to, as the native version has been totally overhauled and is now one of your best options (though the new firmware, called "Licorice," isn't available on the X3 quite yet).

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Based on the novel by Aldous Huxley, this 1-season sci-fi miniseries explores a world divided into those trying to live in a homogenous society without any privacy, and others trying to maintain the old ways of the world.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Science fiction has advantages that few other genres possess. It can create fascinating worlds completely different from our own and use this removal of real-world contexts to explore fascinating issues surrounding free will and dystopian societies. From Paradise to The Handmaid's Tale, Black Mirror to The Running Man, the genre keeps on producing quality narratives that thoroughly entertain audiences with thought-provoking concepts. If you're looking for your next binge in this realm, there is no better place to look than Peacock's Brave New World miniseries.

Based on the novel by Aldous Huxley, this 1-season sci-fi miniseries explores a world divided into those trying to live in a homogenous society without any privacy, and others trying to maintain the old ways of the world. Brave Fresh World creates an incredible world that feels fully realized and one of the more creative projects in recent memory, most likely greatly assisted by Huxley's original novel, contrasting both dystopian themes and colorful sets. On top of this, Brave New World fills this world with a wide range of characters played by A-listers, giving some of their best performances, communicating the complex reactions people would have to such a world.

It has been revealed that brave New World's central premise is that the world has been divided into New London and the Savage Lands. In New London, as the opening text of the pilot episode explains, there is no privacy, no monogamy, and it claims that everybody is happy. This satisfaction is enforced through drugs and intimidation, and private relationships are seen as selfish, with children being grown in labs rather than being born biologically. In the Savage Lands, there are remnants of what is known as "before." This includes a commitment to monogamy, and people are not on state-sponsored drugs. However, while New London is a paradise, the Savage Lands indeed live up to their name, as a desolate wasteland akin to Mad Max.

Recent findings suggest that the two worlds are separated by a blue barrier that only emphasizes the division in society. Rather than trying to help the Savage Lands, Fresh London citizens view them as a lesser species, not understanding why they commit to monogamy or a more individualistic society. When the Savage Lands begin a rebellion focused on destroying New London, members on both sides of the conflict begin to doubt their own way of life. With sex being a key aspect of Brave New World (there are multiple orgy scenes), it examines whether sexual relations can be purely hedonistic and not lead to love and whether that love truly leads to peace, or just increases the chance of jealousy and strife.

Arguably, the most important measure of a sci-fi show is how impressive the world-building is, and that is something that Brave Upcoming World nails throughout. In New London, almost every aspect of life is given a futuristic lens that also contains dark undertones. With everyone having to wear optical lenses that track and record everything, which actually penetrate the pupil to do so, featuring pop-up menus and digital emojis that wearers can project at each other, Brave New World doesn't just tell its audience that there is no privacy; it shows them.

It has been revealed that on top of this, the societal hierarchy is given a recontextualizing in this world, as not only are children grown in a lab, but from conception, they are designated a status from Beta to Alpha Plus, which their heads-up displays constantly show next to everyone. This makes every interaction a focus on power dynamics, whether it is two alphas talking or a beta being rude to an alpha. Even the Savage Lands are presented through beautiful cinematography. While it is clear that it is desolate, the expansive nature of its desert and bright colors make the world feel full of passion and emotion, contrasting Newly introduced London's overly clean and cold presentation.

In a recent development, the mystery of what is known as an Epsilon, essentially a human worker-bee bred to do whatever they are told, killing themselves, is a fascinating subversion of the typical detective mystery. Bernard (Harry Lloyd) is the first on the scene and uses the technology of the world to see the worker's memories, giving him a personal attachment to the suicide that drives him to search for the truth. It is similar to I, Robot in how Brave Upcoming World can incorporate its sci-fi elements into not just the world-building, but the story and character arcs themselves.

Brave Fresh World populates its incredible world with a wide range of characters who all question whether their society is the correct one. In New London, Lenina (Jessica Brown Findlay) and Bernard struggle with the enforced happiness and refusal of monogamy, yet their patronizing view of the Savage Lands makes them complex characters who know no better than to make fun of a way of life most viewers live themselves. In the Savage Lands, John (Alden Ehrenreich) and his mother, Linda (Demi Moore), feel stuck in the middle of the conflict, trying to better their lives in a world that has little place for good people.

This conflict makes Demi Moore's character particularly fascinating. In an interview with Entertainment Weekly, Moore called her character, who is an Ex-Upcoming London citizen, a "bridge between the two worlds" as she dreams of her son leaving the Savage Lands for a better life in New London. Yet, her cold and even dismissive attitude toward John gives her a layered presentation of motherly love.

In a recent development, in the end, Brave Newly introduced World is certainly worth the binge. With nine episodes and a myriad of twists and turns, Brave New World runs at a high pace that keeps the audience guessing where this terrible conflict will go next. There are few worlds as detailed and well-thought-out as Brave New World's, and the stacked cast keeps the audience engaged even in scenes where characters are merely exploring the world, whether that is listening to music from "before" or watching a pantomime-like performance of a conflict-filled marriage ceremony. While some scenes contain graphic sexual content that may make you want to look away, it's worth noting that every detail in Brave New World is intriguing and deserves your attention.

Warning: Spoilers for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

It has been revealed that the Hunger Games series has never been one to shy away from putting its characters through the most unimaginable horrors. But the latest movie in the franchise, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, just might take the cake. Author Suzanne Collins took the brutality in this one to a whole latest (and devastating) level, putting readers through some of the darkest moments in the franchise's history. From the Capitol's calculated cruelty to the horrifying propaganda they promote, this story is a reminder of just how little control the districts held before Katniss entered the Games.

Set during the Second Quarter Quell, the latest from the Hunger Games franchise centers around one of the most brutal Games yet, with 48 tributes fighting to the death. With twice as many children thrown into the arena, the stakes are that much higher and the losses are seemingly endless. The book itself doesn't hold back from these heart wrenching losses either, going into the nitty-gritty gory details of what really went down in the arena.

While it's totally understandable that the filmmakers need to make adjustments to the story to maintain its PG-13 rating, several of the novel's more disturbing moments unfortunately didn't make the cut. One particularly disturbing moment was missing from Sunrise on the Reaping's ending, which was the grisly death of Wellie.

Industry observers note that one of the most horrifying moments in the Sunrise on the Reaping book is when Wellie meets her demise. While the movie doesn't nearly showcase how gruesome her death is, Suzanne Collins did not hold back. During the Games, Silka, District 1's tribute, kills Wellie by cutting off her head with an axe, making it one of the most memorable and brutal deaths the series has seen so far.

Sources indicate that the violence isn't the only part of Wellie's death that makes this moment so painful. It also reveals how ruthless Silka has become. At this point in the Games, whatever humanity Silka had left has ultimately disappeared. And all that's left is her animalistic instinct to survive, no matter what it takes. She's no longer just a tribute determined to win, she is a savage, willing to commit unimaginable acts of violence in order to win. Her transformation is so important to the story, especially in contrast to Haymitch's much more merciful attitude.

Recent findings suggest that and of course, the broadcast doesn't necessarily see this death play out the way Haymitch does in the book. Wellie's death all points back to Sunrise on the Reaping's theme of how the Capitol uses propaganda to maintain their power. This death, in particular, highlights the devastating consequences on the kids' psyche while they're in the Games, and the movie's choice to leave it out is all the more disappointing.

It's not particularly surprising that Sunrise on the Reaping changed the way Wellie's death is depicted in the film. Despite the already dark subject matter of the series, the films have kept a PG-13 rating, meaning that filmmakers have had to be strategic about how much graphic violence they can actually show.

Sources indicate that these movies certainly aren't lacking in death or violence, but they often rely on quick cuts and character reactions instead of showing every brutal detail. In an interview with Entertainment Weekly, SOTR director Francis Lawrence explained:.

“What’s great about Suzanne’s writing is that she pulls no punches. The only thing we have to do in the movies is make them PG-13. So there's certain things she describes in the book that I could never put in the movies. There’s a character holding the head of a child at one point in the book, and that’s just not something you can do in a PG-13 movie.”.

Wellie's death presents a very difficult challenge because her decapitation is much more graphic than a PG-13 audience would expect to see. Showing that death the way it's written in the book would have pushed the movie into a more restrictive place, with the risk of losing a huge part of its audience. As a result, Silka still murdered Wellie, but it is significantly less graphic.

Recent findings suggest that while it's understandable that Sunrise on the Reaping couldn't recreate every gruesome detail of Wellie's death without potentially jeopardizing its PG-13 rating, that doesn't mean the filmmakers made the right decision by toning down the moment. In fact, leaving out the nature of her death takes away from one of the most disturbing turning points in the story.

Industry observers note that wellie's decapitation isn't just part of the story for shock value, but it's an notable indicator of how high the Second Quarter Quell's stakes have become. It demonstrates how far tributes are willing to go to survive.

Sources indicate that more importantly, the moment says a lot about Silka and the role she has in the Sunrise on the Reaping cast. Wellie was one of the younger tributes and not particularly dangerous, so Silka didn't necessarily need to decapitate her. Wellie was never a true threat to Silka, or anybody, for that matter. But in losing this moment in the film, her transition into true savagery isn't shown.

Industry observers note that now, the filmmakers didn't necessarily need to show the death in every graphic detail to preserve the meaning of the scene. A longer sequence, stronger reactions from Haymitch and Silka, or more attention to the aftermath could have communicated the same horror without pushing the movie past its PG-13 rating.

Beyond changing the circumstances of Wellie's death, Sunrise on the Reaping missed the opportunity to do more with her as a character. With 48 tributes, it naturally has a lot of characters to introduce with stories to balance, but that shouldn't mean the minor characters have to fade into the background.

It has been revealed that in the Sunrise on the Reaping novel, Wellie is a District 6 tribute and a member of Haymitch and Ampert's alliance, The Newcomers. On the last day of the Games, Haymitch sticks with Wellie and hides her under a tree while he goes to locate dry kindling. In his mind, Wellie was to be the victor, and he was going to try his hardest to make that happen.

According to recent reports, in the movie, Wellie is only seen for a couple of seconds when Haymitch offers her his lunch. Had that connection been established earlier, viewers would have had more of a reason to care about her before she died. Her relationship with Haymitch could've reinforced his arc in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping even more.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’ve had the iPhone Duo for nearly two weeks now, and have officially decided to return it.

  • Perhaps over time I’d get used to needing two hands for most iPhone interactions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’ve had the iPhone Duo for nearly two weeks now, and have officially decided to return it. Here are the three main reasons why the Duo didn’t work out for me, but might for you.

In a recent development, I use my iPhone one-handed all the time, and based on my experience, iPhone Duo is clearly intended to be used with two hands. You can use it one-handed, but for me it’s not nearly as comfortable as the iPhone 18 Pro. It’s too wide and too heavy to be used for long.

Perhaps over time I’d get used to needing two hands for most iPhone interactions. But that would be a pretty significant shift for me, as there are so many situations when I don’t have both hands free.

According to recent reports, if you already use two hands with your iPhone regularly—perhaps because you have a Pro Max model—then the Duo’s one-handed experience likely won’t bother you. But the more I used the Duo, the more I found myself missing my iPhone 18 Pro.

The biggest value proposition of a foldable is that it’s a 2-in-1 product, letting you have a standard phone but also a tablet-sized display that fits in your pocket.

I totally get the appeal, and fully expected to love that hybrid design. But after two weeks of trying, I still struggled to find times when I actually wanted to unfold the Duo. And to be clear, that’s a me problem, not an concern with the Duo itself.

Sources indicate that I tried a bunch of apps on the inner display, and struggled to find use cases that—for me—made it worthwhile to open the Duo. But based on the feedback I’ve seen from most Duo owners, I’m very much in the minority.

I know lots of people love the Duo for video, but I don’t watch much video on my iPhone. I almost never watch YouTube, TikTok, or Instagram Reels. And for indicates and movies, I stick with my TV screen and an Apple TV 4K.

Multitasking support on iPhone Duo works really well. But when I found myself needing to multitask, I still reached for my iPad Pro with Magic Keyboard attached. A keyboard-free product can’t replace my main computer (nor would I expect it to), and the Duo screen was too small to comfortably work on it.

Last year I bought an iPhone Air and absolutely loved it. Initially, the Air’s less capable camera system didn’t bother me, it was “good enough.”.

After a few months though, I started missing the Pro camera system more. Then I learned that my wife was pregnant with twins, and I knew I wanted the best possible iPhone cameras to capture their early weeks and months. So I bought an iPhone 18 Pro in September.

Recent findings suggest that I’ve been very impressed by iPhone 18 Pro’s Main camera upgrades, and it’s great having a Telephoto lens again too. Since having the best camera system is so crucial for me right now, I knew iPhone Duo couldn’t be my only iPhone.

According to recent reports, I initially planned to dual-carry the two models, using iPhone 18 Pro solely as a camera. But over and over I found myself wishing it was my only iPhone.

Recent findings suggest that I returned mine as well. Beautiful device, but functionally not very good.

In a recent development, is the iPhone Duo camera good enough for most people? Probably so. But for this year at least, with my twins aging rapidly, it’s not quite right for me. If I loved the Duo for other reasons, I would just use both models. But since I didn’t, I’m happy to stick with the iPhone 18 Pro.

In closing, I want to explicitly state that I don’t think the iPhone Duo is a bad product, and this isn’t a “bad review.”.

The iPhone Duo just isn’t for me. I get the sense, though, that it’s lots of people’s favorite iPhone in years. Apple created its most unique fresh iPhone model since the original, and there’s plenty to love about it. I’m very curious to see how popular foldables become over time compared to slab models, because each clearly offers pros and cons. But for me, at least right now, the iPhone 18 Pro is my model of choice.

What has your iPhone Duo experience been like so far? Love it? Undecided? Let us know in the comments.

The otherwise meticulous plan has one hitch: Noah's girlfriend, Rose, works at the bank as a teller. With time and love on the line, Noah must figure out who he can trust if he hopes to make it out of the heist alive.

The Take streams on Netflix on Friday, January 15, 2027.

The streamer has started unveiling next year's releases, and The Take is one of two films releasing early in 2027. The other is Danny Boyle's INK, which debuts in theaters on December 11, 2026, before streaming on January 8, 2027. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that david Pepose is one of the most versatile writers in comics.
  • began its push on Kickstarter, but was recently picked up by Boom!
  • is one of the most creative changes to the classic book and movie.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that david Pepose is one of the most versatile writers in comics. Readers can see him bringing Layla El-Faouly from the MCU's Moon Knight to Marvel Comics and writing the amazing Cable: Love and Chrome. Then, he’ll turn around and give horror fans an amazing comic book like Mad Cave Studios' The Devil That Wears My Face. Among the amazing comics David Pepose has written is a bold reimagining of the classic book and movie, The Wizard of Oz, The O.Z.

Sources indicate that the O.Z. began its push on Kickstarter, but was recently picked up by Boom! Studios. In a recent interview ScreenRant was fortunate enough to have with Pepose, he talks about what the story is about, the way it came to be, and more.

Sources indicate that the O.Z. is one of the most creative changes to the classic book and movie. When asked about what the story is about, Pepose goes into great detail about it and why it's different from other Wizard of Oz tales.

It has been revealed that david Pepose: THE O.Z. is like Mad Max meets The Wizard of Oz — it’s the story of Dorothy Gale’s granddaughter and namesake, who is an Iraq war veteran grappling with PTSD and disillusionment. But when our upcoming Dorothy is caught up in a tornado, she finds herself stranded in the land of Oz — where she learns her grandmother’s adventures plunged the country into a brutal civil war. Now Dorothy must team up with the Tin Soldier, the Prince of Lions, and Jack Pumpkinhead in order to find the Silver Slippers and bring peace to the Occupied Zone… or as the locals call it, The O.Z.

Many people have brought different versions of The Wizard of Oz to various genres, but Pepose's has been the most adventurous. Considering the source material, that says a lot. When asked about that, he said, "I’ve always been a fan of mashing up different genres, so doing a fantasy war story was something I’d wanted to do early in my career." However, how he landed on The Wizard of Oz is a funny story.

Pepose: Landing on The Wizard of Oz came across as kind of a happy accident — I was typing different fantasy staples to see if anything could serve as inspiration, and my cursor froze in the middle of the word “Oz.” That had me thinking about the word Oz as an acronym, which turned into “Occupied Zone” — and that moment instantly crystallized the entire narrative for me.

When asked why he went this particular route with Dorothy, Pepose gives an interesting reason.

Pepose: Back in my days as a newspaper reporter, I’d interviewed a ton of returning veterans about their experiences coming back home, and those stories had always stuck with me — and that became the basis for Dorothy’s story in THE O.Z.

Industry observers note that now that The O.Z. has been picked up by Boom! Studios, the next question is whether or not the series will continue. Pepose seems hopeful that this won’t be the last comic book fans will see of the characters and this alternate reality Wizard of Oz story. However, there are some factors to consider.

According to recent reports, pepose: Never say never! Whether we do a sequel storyline will ultimately be determined by demand and me and Ruben Rojas’ respective schedules, but I do have a few ideas in my back pocket, which I’d actually pitched to BOOM!’s Editor-in-Chief Andy Schmidt and our O.Z. editor Gregory Hopkins. So there’s definitely room to return to the Occupied Zone if enough people demand it.

The O.Z. #1 is scheduled to be released in February 2027 by Boom! Studios.

Industry observers note that 15 years ago, there weren’t many movie fans that had heard of Denis Villeneuve, but flash forward to today, and he’s one of the most prominent directors/writers in all of Hollywood. Villeneuve is a sci-fi savant who is widely known and celebrated for his work on Dune and Dune: Part Two, but his work with the sci-fi genre extends well beyond Arrakis’ reach.

According to recent reports, four years before the first Dune movie, Villeneuve took the reins from Ridley Scott for Blade Runner 2049, which is one of the most beloved sci-fi films of the 2000s despite its underwhelming box office performance. Villeneuve was already red-hot off the back of directing Arrival, the critically acclaimed sci-fi epic starring Amy Adams and Jeremy Renner. The year before Arrival, he directed Sicario, which was written by Taylor Sheridan.

Next up for Denis Villeneuve after Dune: Part Three releases in less than one month is the next James Bond movie, which is now confirmed to star Robert Pattinson as 007. Villeneuve will have to rely on his years of experience as a director to helm the best Bond film possible, calling on elements from all of his past movies, even Prisoners, the 2013 crime epic starring Hugh Jackman and Jake Gyllenhaal.

Villeneuve spent $46 million on the making of Prisoners, but the film proved to be a worthy investment by grossing $122 million at the global box office — an impressive run for a director’s first American movie. 13 years after Prisoners left theaters, the film has finally found a streaming home on Apple TV, where it surged into the top 10 during the last week.

Recent findings suggest that in addition to Hugh Jackman and Jake Gyllenhaal, Prisoners also features other stars you’ll likely recognize, such as Viola Davis and Paul Dano. Aaron Guzikowski, who also wrote the Ridley Scott HBO Max sci-fi series, Raised by Wolves, penned the script for Prisoners. The official synopsis for Prisoners, which earned strong scores of 82% from critics and 87% from audiences on Rotten Tomatoes, reads as follows:.

Recent findings suggest that “Keller Dover (Hugh Jackman) faces a parent's worst nightmare when his 6-year-old daughter, Anna, and her friend go missing. The only lead is an old motorhome that had been parked on their street. The head of the investigation, Detective Loki (Jake Gyllenhaal), arrests the driver (Paul Dano), but a lack of evidence forces Loki to release his only suspect. Dover, knowing that his daughter's life is at stake, decides that he has no choice but to take matters into his own hands.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AirPods got a variety of new features this fall in iOS 27, several of which are exclusive to AirPods Pro 3 (now only $179). Here’s everything new.

Custom EQ is a feature that some AirPods consumers thought Apple would never ship, but iOS 27 adds it.

According to recent reports, with Custom EQ, Apple now lets you set your own sound profile for AirPods. Per Apple:.

AirPods are designed and engineered by Apple to faithfully represent music, TV highlights and movies, and calls. If you prefer a different sound profile, you can customize how AirPods represent any audio played.

You can change the EQ by going to your AirPods’ settings ⇾ Audio & Routing ⇾ Equalizer ⇾ Custom. From here, you can adjust the sound profile for low, mid, and high frequencies.

Custom EQ is available on AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Max 2, AirPods 5, and AirPods 4.

According to recent reports, apple GymKit has been available for years, but only for Apple Watch. It lets you pair and sync workout data with compatible cardio equipment, like treadmills, ellipticals, indoor bikes, and more.

In a recent development, in iOS 27, GymKit expands to support iPhone using AirPods Pro 3’s heart rate sensor. My colleague Zac gave it a try:.

Sources indicate that the setup is simple. I tapped my iPhone to the treadmill, picked Indoor Walk (Indoor Run is also offered), and started the workout from the treadmill. With GymKit, workout data is stored privately on iPhone and removed from the equipment.

Once the workout started, the treadmill received heart-rate data from AirPods Pro 3. Meanwhile, the Fitness app on iPhone received the treadmill’s distance, pace, incline, and calorie data. Treadmills know details that an iPhone and AirPods can’t know on their own, especially incline and precise belt distance.

For more details on iOS 27’s GymKit feature for AirPods Pro 3, check out Zac’s full hands-on below.

Read more: iOS 27 basically turns your iPhone and AirPods into an Apple Watch at the gym.

For most AirPods people, the single biggest upgrade in iOS 27 is Siri AI.

Siri AI is available on compatible iPhone hardware in iOS 27, and Apple made sure to expand full support for the AI assistant to AirPods too.

AirPods are essentially becoming an AI wearable thanks to the new Siri. It will let owners do a lot more than the current Siri. Here are some key features via Apple’s website:.

Sources indicate that earlier this year when AirTag 2 launched, Apple brought Precision Finding support to Apple Watch for the first time. Until now though, it’s been limited to AirTag 2.

But with iOS 27 and watchOS 27, Apple expands Precision Finding on the Watch to AirPods Pro 3.

AirPods Pro 3’s case includes the latest second-generation Ultra Wideband (UWB) chip, letting you find it with greater precision and step-by-step guidance right from your wrist.

With every batch of new AirPods features that debuts, the AirPods settings screen in the Settings app gets more cluttered.

But in iOS 27, Apple has a welcome fix: it’s redesigned and reorganized all AirPods settings.

In a recent development, now, you’ll find AirPods settings organized into more categories and submenus, accompanied by colorful icons. It makes finding the right setting way easier and more intuitive than before.

Read more: iOS 27 revamps AirPods settings in a big way, here’s the newly introduced design.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • There have been all sorts of brilliant Pokémon games over the years, and while everyone has their own favorites, it's widely agreed upon that Black and White are some of the best releases in the series to date.
  • That movement has only been furthered by the rise of PC emulation, which has become easier and considerably more competent in recent years thanks to rapid advances in technology.
  • Happily, it seems as though those concerns are about to entirely be a thing of the past, as a latest and ingenious piece of tech finally solves the matter with aplomb.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There have been all sorts of brilliant Pokémon games over the years, and while everyone has their own favorites, it's widely agreed upon that Black and White are some of the best releases in the series to date. In fact, the DS/3DS era as a whole was just a magical time for franchise releases more generally, and they remain popular games for fans to play in 2026.

That movement has only been furthered by the rise of PC emulation, which has become easier and considerably more competent in recent years thanks to rapid advances in technology. One of the main issues with emulating DS games is the dual screens they were originally designed for, which don't lend themselves particularly well to modern, single-monitor setups.

Happily, it seems as though those concerns are about to entirely be a thing of the past, as a latest and ingenious piece of tech finally solves the matter with aplomb.

As first reported by Retro Dodo, newly introduced software has been made publically available that converts dual-screen Pokémon games into a single-screen 60FPS output. Known as Pokémon FullDex, it's available as a free download from creator mamesj's GitHub, and it already works for a ton of iconic games from the DS era.

The description for the project reads as follows:.

In a recent development, "All your favourite Pokémon games on a PC (Windows and Linux), a Mac, a Steam Deck or other handheld PC, an Android phone, an iPhone or iPad, or a modded Nintendo Switch: one screen, widescreen, 60 fps, up to 4K on a PC and 720p on the Switch. No more squinting at two tiny stacked DS screens.".

The videos posted to the page are also hugely impressive, and you'd never really know that the games weren't designed to run like that in the first place. It works far beyond Pokémon Black and White as well, with more titles on the way all the time. The full list as it stands includes:.

DS: Black 2, White 2, Black, White, HeartGold, SoulSilver, Platinum, Diamond and Pearl.

GBA: Emerald, Ruby, Sapphire, FireRed, LeafGreen and Ultra Violet.

3DS (beta): Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire on Windows, Android and Switch; X, Y, Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon coming soon.

Recent findings suggest that it's a hugely impressive, lightweight piece of tech, and it comes with a bunch of mod-cons like support for RetroAchievements and cheats. The only potential drawback here is that it seems as though the project was heavily assisted by Claude AI, and that comes with its own set of risks, as well as potential moral quandaries for those of us who want to push back against the increased use of AI in gaming.

As for Pokémon fans more generally, the 30th anniversary of the franchise has now largely drawn to a close, and things are expected to go a little quiet for the time being. The first games of the tenth generation (Winds and Waves) are set to be the next significant stopping point on that journey, with more news expected on that in the first half of next year.

  • Because of this, the prices aren't nearly as low as they were last year, but now is still the time to get a decent discount on a Kindle Paperwhite or Colorsoft—but if you'd rather read differently, you can also save significant on a few worthy Kindle alternatives.
  • According to recent reports, the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best e-reader for most people.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, amazon's Black Friday sale kicked off today, which means it's a good time to score some of the year's best prices on e-readers. Timing your purchase is now a bigger deal than ever (so to speak), as Amazon recently raised the price of basically every Kindle by $50 or more due to the ongoing RAM crisis.

Because of this, the prices aren't nearly as low as they were last year, but now is still the time to get a decent discount on a Kindle Paperwhite or Colorsoft—but if you'd rather read differently, you can also save significant on a few worthy Kindle alternatives. Here are your e-reader best bets in the lead-up to Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

According to recent reports, the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best e-reader for most people. An upgraded version of the basic Kindle, the Paperwhite adds a larger screen, temperature-adjustable lighting, water resistance, and better battery life—and if you opt for the Signature Edition, you also get double the storage and no lock screen ads. Earlier this year, it jumped in price to $250, even before the firm introduced a fresh model—but you can get the 2024 model for $179.99, 28% off the new list price.

If you want a great Kindle but you don't care about paying extra for more storage or getting rid of lock screen ads, the non-Signature Edition of the Kindle Paperwhite is also a great buy right now. The 2024 model has been discounted to $129.99 from the list price of $199.99. It's available in standard black, Jade, or Raspberry colors.

Recent findings suggest that if you don't need the bells and whistles of the Paperwhite, you can also pick up the standard Kindle. It's still a very capable device, with good lighting, 16GB of onboard storage, and the ability to hook up your Bluetooth speakers to listen to Audible audiobooks. The standard Kindle, which now retails for $150, is marked down to $119.99, making it the cheapest Kindle option. Though I think it makes more sense to spend $10 more on the Signature Edition, this is the way to go if you want the cute Matcha color.

Recent findings suggest that if you like to read comics or you just appreciate looking at your book covers in full color, the 2024 Kindle Colorsoft is also at a strong 41% discount for Black Friday, bringing it down to around $170. For $10 less than the Paperwhite Signature edition, you get all the same perks (including an ad-free experience) and a color e-ink screen that's great for reading magazines, graphic novels, and manga. Color e-ink isn't for everyone, but if it's for you, the Colorsoft has the best color screen on the market. For an extra $10, the Colorsoft Kids Edition adds a case, a yearlong subscription to Kindle Kids+, and an extended warranty.

In a recent development, if you're looking for a combination e-reader and e-notebook, the Kindle Scribe is a great option. With a larger screen than Amazon's other e-readers, it offers all the benefits of the Paperwhite but adds support for the excellent Premium Pen stylus, allowing you to take notes in your Amazon e-books or create handwritten documents that you can later convert to text using the onboard AI tools. The 32GB black-and-white version of the Kindle Scribe is right now $349.99, while the Colorsoft version will run you $449.99. Both of these are the newest models, released in 2025.

The new Kindle Scribe Colorsoft has all the same great features of the black-and-white version discussed above, but adds a full-color e-ink display. Combined with the large 11-inch screen, this makes it a great device for reading comics or magazine articles as they were meant to be read, or marking up PDFs using the included Premium Pen. This device usually costs a hefty $630, but the current Black Friday sale cuts $180 off of that price.

Recent findings suggest that if you want to step outside of the Amazon ecosystem, the Kobo Libra Colour is a good bet. Discounted $30 to $229.99 at Best Buy, it's currently pricier than the Kindle Colorsoft, but you get a bit more for your money. While most of the specs are similar (they both use the same Kaleido 3 screen and offer 32GB of storage), the Kobo supports a stylus, so you can jot down notes in your books or keep a digital journal. It also has physical page-turn buttons, which the Colorsoft lacks.

In a recent development, if you don't want to be tied to the Amazon ecosystem and/or you're looking for a device that's a bit more portable, consider the Viwoods AiPaper Reader, presently marked down to $200, its lowest price ever. It's got a 6.13-inch screen, so it's the same size and shape as your phone, and it has a crisp e-ink screen with a strong (if not temperature-adjustable) front light and 128GB of onboard storage. The best part is, it runs on an open Android system, so you can install multiple reading apps, including Kindle, Nook, Kobo, and Libby, and keep all of your books in one place. (Check out my review of the Viwoods AiPaper Reader for more—it's a nifty little device.).

If you don't have a large Kindle library, you're moderately tech-savvy, and you praise portability above all else, I can't recommend Xteink's line of e-readers more highly. The 4.3-inch Xteink X4 Classic is at its lowest price ever, coming in at just under $55, around $34 off the list price. Meanwhile, the smaller 3.7-inch Xteink X3 is about a dollar more; that's a less-generous 19% discount. I own both, and while the Classic is definitely worth the current sale price, I actually prefer the form factor of the smaller X3 (presently $55.72), which is about the size of a library card.

If you're feeling tentative about trusting a seemingly no-name Chinese tech brand, read more about the devices in my review, or listen to the collected wisdom of the tens of thousands of people in the bustling r/xteink Reddit group.

Sources indicate that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Industry observers note that follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

According to recent reports, no. If you find the product you're looking for with a major discount right now, get it. It's not likely to drop any lower, but it could always run out of stock. Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.
