Tech Report: Epic accuses Apple of withholding 122,000 documents, seeks daily fines

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (940 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, in a fresh filing, Epic Games accuses Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions and asks the court to impose daily fines until the manufacturer complies.
  • As a result of the lawsuit Epic Games brought against Apple in 2020, Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers ruled in 2021 that Apple would have to, among other things, allow developers to direct customers to alternative payment methods outside the App Store.
  • In a recent development, apple responded by allowing external payment links, but imposed a commission of up to 27% on purchases made through them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in a fresh filing, Epic Games accuses Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions and asks the court to impose daily fines until the manufacturer complies. Here are the details.

As a result of the lawsuit Epic Games brought against Apple in 2020, Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers ruled in 2021 that Apple would have to, among other things, allow developers to direct customers to alternative payment methods outside the App Store.

In a recent development, apple responded by allowing external payment links, but imposed a commission of up to 27% on purchases made through them. This, in turn, led the court to find Apple in civil contempt for violating its injunction. Since then, Apple has been trying to overturn that ruling, a dispute that has now reached the Supreme Court.

At the same time, district court proceedings will determine what, if any, commission Apple may charge on purchases made through external payment links. Apple submitted its proposal on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, and Epic is expected to respond after Apple completes its document production.

In a newly introduced filing, however, Epic is accusing Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to how it arrived at its proposed commission rates.

One of the many aspects of the ever-sprawling battle between Epic Games and Apple centers on document production.

In its newly introduced filing, Epic notes Apple has repeatedly failed to produce documents detailing how it arrived at its proposed commission rates, accusing the organization of withholding materials it deems irrelevant to the proceedings.

Epic argues that Apple previously used questionable claims of attorney-client privilege to withhold documents during the contempt proceedings, but has now changed tactics.

Apple does introduce one tactical change from its prior campaign of delay. Whereas during the contempt proceeding Apple used bogus claims of privilege to evade its discovery obligations, this time Apple withholds thousands of documents on bogus claims of irrelevance. For example, Apple is withholding well over 99% of the documents returned by running the agreed-to search terms on the files of the four custodians Apple notes decided on the proposed fee (Tim Cook, Eddy Cue, Carson Oliver, and Kevan Parekh (Apple’s fresh CFO)) and three other key individuals (Nate Barton, Alex Roman, and Phil Schiller). Apple claims these withheld documents are not relevant to this proceeding-even though they hit on case-specific terms such as “proffer,” “contempt,” “injunction,” and “link-out.” To put this into context, while Apple produced 632 custodial documents returned by these search terms (including families), Apple is withholding over 122,000 based on a claim of non-responsiveness. Moreover, Apple claims that it completed its production from the files of these custodians, yet its production does not include a single substantive email discussing the rates Apple ultimately proposed; any notes or communications reflecting what occurred at any meeting where these rates were discussed or decided; any internal analysis of the financial or business impact of the proposed commissions; any App Store profit and loss statements; or any support for Apple’s assertion that its incremental link-out costs are “essentially zero.”.

Epic goes on to state that “Apple cannot be trusted to fix this problem on its own,” proposing instead that the court order Apple to produce all non-privileged documents matching the search terms agreed upon by both parties, regardless of whether Apple considers them relevant.

Under this proposal, Apple would still be allowed to review documents for attorney-client privilege, but it would be up to Epic to determine which of the remaining documents are relevant to the case. Epic argues that existing confidentiality protections would prevent it from using any of the information for purposes unrelated to the litigation.

Industry observers note that given Apple’s position, Epic respectfully submits that the Court should order Apple to produce to Epic all non-privileged documents that hit on the Parties’ agreed-upon search terms, so that Epic itself can sift the wheat from the chaff. Doing so will avoid further delays and place no burden on Apple. Moreover, doing so would not raise any of the concerns that required Special Master involvement in the prior proceeding, namely concerns around the production of privileged Apple information to Epic. Under Epic’s proposed remedy, Apple would be allowed to continue its review for privilege. For these reasons, Epic asks this Court to order Apple to produce all non-privileged documents that hit on any of the Parties’ agreed-upon search terms by December 2, 2026 (one week after Apple’s deadline to substantially complete production), irrespective of any relevance or responsiveness assessment.

Finally, though Epic does not propose a specific dollar amount, it “asks that the Court impose on Apple a daily monetary sanction for each day Apple fails to comply after December 2, 2026.”.

Sources indicate that according to the court docket, a hearing on Epic’s motion was initially scheduled for November 24 before Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers. However, a upcoming order filed today, which has yet to be made public, refers the discovery dispute to a magistrate judge and includes a notice terminating deadlines and hearings.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple has three main Apple Watch "lines." There's the flagship, right now the Series 12, which represents Apple's mainstream wearable. For athletes and users who think they'll put their watches through some extreme scenarios, there's the Ultra line, currently the Apple Watch Ultra 4. And while both the Series 12 and Ultra 4 are excellent devices in their own right, they can be pretty pricey (particularly the Ultra). That's why the third category, the SE, is actually best for most people, and Lifehacker's choice for best smartwatch gift of the year. Better yet, the third-generation SE is currently $50 off ahead of Black Friday, perfect for most people asking for an Apple Watch this year.

Recent findings suggest that the SE 3 does just about everything you'd expect an Apple Watch to do. It, of course, has a heart rate sensor to keep tabs on your pulse, including high and low heart rate alerts; the ability to track dozens of different workouts and exercise types (including swimming, thanks to the device's water resistance); a sleep tracker with daily analyses available in the Health app; notification forwarding to check in on your alerts without opening your iPhone; and the ability to send and receive text messages.

Industry observers note that it comes in two sizes (40mm and 44mm) depending on how large or small you prefer your watch. No matter which model you get, the watch comes with the S10 chip, Apple's last-generation watch processor. While it isn't as fast as the current S11 chip, the S10 is more than capable of running watchOS 27. Apple says the SE 3 can run for up to 18 hours on a single charge, and up to 32 hours in Low Power Mode, with fast charging from 0% to 80% in 45 minutes.

The majority of the features missing from the SE 3 aren't essential. Apple's other watches have things like bigger, brighter displays, additional health tracking tools like hypertension alerts and an ECG sensor, longer battery life, and Audio Intelligence—the latter of which might be a benefit to miss, depending on who you are.

It has been revealed that if your giftee wants or needs any of those additional features, Series 12 or Ultra 4 might be a better choice. But for anyone who wants the essential Apple Watch experience, the SE 3 is simply the best-value watch Apple sells right now—especially at this discount. Right now, the watch starts at $199 for the 40mm watch, or $229 for the 44mm. You can also save on the cellular versions of these watches: $249 for the cellular 40mm watch, and $279 for the cellular 44mm model.

Recent findings suggest that yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Industry observers note that black Friday sales officially begin Friday, Nov. 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, Nov. 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by Dec. 2, 2026.

Report: iPhone set to gain market share in 2027 amid industry-wide slump

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (558 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple could see iPhone shipments rise 7% next year, giving it a 26% share of global smartphone shipments, according to a new report.
  • As detailed by AppleInsider, a new Morgan Stanley research report says Apple is poised to ship approximately 270 million iPhones in 2027, a 7% bump from 2026.
  • The forecast comes amid a change of pace for Apple, which released only the iPhone 18 Pro models and iPhone Duo this fall, with the rest of its iPhone lineup reportedly set to arrive early next year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple could see iPhone shipments rise 7% next year, giving it a 26% share of global smartphone shipments, according to a new report. Here are the details.

As detailed by AppleInsider, a new Morgan Stanley research report says Apple is poised to ship approximately 270 million iPhones in 2027, a 7% bump from 2026.

The forecast comes amid a change of pace for Apple, which released only the iPhone 18 Pro models and iPhone Duo this fall, with the rest of its iPhone lineup reportedly set to arrive early next year.

Morgan Stanley notes that this could push some purchases from late 2026 into 2027, contributing to the projected shipment growth without necessarily reflecting an increase in underlying demand.

The report also comes as Apple and the rest of the smartphone industry continue to grapple with rising memory and storage prices, though previous reports have suggested that Apple is better positioned than many of its competitors to absorb those costs.

Sources indicate that apple raised iPhone prices in September, after keeping them stable for much of the year while competitors had already introduced price hikes. In some cases, they raised prices more than once within a matter of months.

Back to the report, it notes that global smartphone shipments are expected to drop 5% next year, compared with a previous forecast of 3.6% growth. That stated, it’s still an improvement over the estimated 13.8% decline in 2026.

Recent findings suggest that when it comes to Apple and the iPhone specifically, Morgan Stanley notes that consumer interest in upgrading has remained largely unchanged year over year, with 37% of iPhone owners saying they are extremely likely to upgrade within the next 12 months. That’s compared with 41% of smartphone owners overall, a figure that dropped by 2 percentage points year over year.

As for the market’s reaction to the iPhone Duo, Morgan Stanley found that 22% of non-iPhone customers surveyed expressed interest in switching to Apple’s foldable device, with that figure reaching 34% in China.

Importantly, Morgan Stanley’s survey was conducted after the iPhone Duo was confirmed, but before it launched, so these figures reflect consumer interest rather than actual purchasing behavior.

Apple Intelligence was another factor examined in the survey, with Morgan Stanley concluding that AI features are becoming less important in driving iPhone upgrades, while factors such as battery life and upgrade eligibility are gaining importance.

Finally, Morgan Stanley found that Apple’s customer retention rate increased three percentage points to a record 93%, while its net switching rate improved to 12%.

Huawei was the only other major smartphone brand to show a positive and improving net switching rate, while Samsung and Google remained relatively neutral, and Xiaomi, Motorola, Honor, Oppo, and Vivo recorded negative rates.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that like other streaming services nowadays, Netflix has started to warm up to releasing its films in theaters — at least some of them. The streaming service strongly considered leaning into this route when it tried to acquire Warner Bros., despite having the streaming-at-home line for the longest time. Some of its films this year have received limited theatrical runs in anticipation of Academy Award nominations, and the service has one strong contender so far: La Bola Negra. The Spanish epic has received acclaim from fans and critics, putting it in a strong position for awards in various categories.

In a recent development, apart from La Bola Negra, Netflix has also given limited releases to The Further Misadventures of Cliff Booth, INK, Ray Gunn, and more. However, one of these films hasn't performed well critically, a telltale sign that its Oscar campaign has reached a natural end. That movie is a World War II epic that made its theatrical debut last month and has grossed $815813 across 349 theaters. Now, The Mosquito Bowl is coming to Netflix this week, and it could be a streaming hit.

Directed by Peter Berg and based on a script he co-wrote with Mark L. Smith, the action thriller is set in the 1940s and follows four American college football stars in the aftermath of the attack on Pearl Harbor. These young men abandon their promising careers to enlist as Marines in America's war with Japan. "As they prepare for the brutal invasion of Okinawa, they'll play in a legendary game featuring some of the greatest players in history — a game that, for many, will be the last they ever play," reads the film's description. Cast members include Nicholas Galitzine (John McLughry), Bill Skarsgård (Bob Bauman), Ray Nicholson (Tony Butkovich), and Tom Francis (Dave Schreiner). The Mosquito Bowl streams on Netflix on November 25.

Recent findings suggest that with a current 41% critics' score on Rotten Tomatoes, the film has not received the best reviews. Critics noted that The Mosquito Bowl feels quite hollow in more ways than one. Collider's Maggie Lovitt said that it is a bit pedestrian and "adds very little newly introduced to the canon of war epics," while ScreenRant's Lizzie Declan did not appreciate the violence used to shield the lack of an engaging story. RogerEbert's Robert Daniels said it is "lacking in humanity." However, critic reviews don't always reflect viewer consensus, and those who saw it in theaters gave it a favorable 91% rating. Netflix could be vindicated when The Mosquito Bowl finally enters friendlier territory.

Stream the film on Wednesday, November 25, and stay tuned to Collider for more updates.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that select WhatsApp beta testers on iOS are now seeing an option to use the app’s own backup service as an alternative to iCloud. Here are the details.

A few months ago, WABetaInfo reported that WhatsApp was working on its own backup service as an alternative to the current method of backing up chats, which relies on Apple’s iCloud.

At the time, the feature wasn’t available even to beta testers, but WABetaInfo’s report provided details on how it would work, including 2GB of free storage, optional paid looks for larger backups, and mandatory end-to-end encryption for backups stored on WhatsApp’s servers.

Now, the site reports that some WhatsApp users running the latest TestFlight build are seeing the option to switch from iCloud to WhatsApp’s own backup service, suggesting that a wider rollout may not be too far off.

Recent findings suggest that users can switch to WhatsApp cloud storage from the Chat backup screen. Here, users will have to choose the backup provider they want to use. If they choose WhatsApp, they will have to secure their backups using end-to-end encryption. Since encryption is mandatory, users cannot skip this step. However, they can choose a different method to encrypt their backups. For example, users can secure their backups using a 64-digit encryption key. Users who do not know what to choose can opt for the passkey, which is the default method WhatsApp recommends. After users complete the setup, they can back up their chat history on WhatsApp’s servers. WhatsApp keeps the backup on its servers for four months after a subscription expires. If users do not renew their subscription, WhatsApp deletes the backup permanently.

Importantly, the site notes that backups stored on WhatsApp’s servers cannot at the moment be used to restore chats across platforms, meaning owners switching from iPhone to Android, or vice versa, will still need to rely on WhatsApp’s built-in chat transfer feature.

Although the feature appears to be rolling out to beta testers first, the report notes that “the latest version available on the App Store is also compatible with this functionality,” meaning WhatsApp could theoretically enable it for users running the public version without requiring another app revision.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the weakest episode of one of HBO’s best Mystery Box shows arrived early in the three-season run of the series, but even this outing still had plenty to praise, which highlights the overall quality of the show as a whole. Mystery Box shows are somewhat infamous for their inconsistency. While early seasons of Lost include some of the most enthralling and engaging network TV moments of the 2000s, the show’s filler episodes can feel truly pointless.

Industry observers note that even the earliest Mystery Box shows weren’t immune to this. The best episodes of Twin Peaks were funny, scary, heartbreaking, disturbing, and beautiful, often at the same time, but anyone who has sat through the latter half of season 2 can attest to the show’s plentiful padding. Similarly, while there were mytharc episodes of the ‘90s classic The X-Files that were truly unmissable, there were plenty of other outings that made the central conspiracy more confusing, but not more interesting.

Recent findings suggest that the fact that almost every Mystery Box show has at least a few duds among its great episodes makes HBO’s The Leftovers all the more impressive. Based on the novel of the same name by author Tom Perrotta, HBO’s dark mystery drama takes place after an unexplained disaster sees 2% of the global human population seemingly vanish without a trace. The show follows the stories of the devastated people left behind, from Justin Theroux’s troubled police officer Kevin to Christopher Eccleston’s unhinged religious zealot Reverend Matt Jamison.

Although the characters of The Leftovers gradually crossed paths throughout the HBO show’s story, the series wasn’t in a rush to reveal the links between its sprawling ensemble. With a starry cast that included Liv Tyler, Regina Hall, and Carrie Coon, The Leftovers wasn’t short on talent, but the show’s most divisive outing did leave viewers wondering whether its diffuse storytelling style would ever pay off.

The Leftovers season 1, episode 4, “BJ and the AC,” is often singled out as a rare miss for the show, and one of the only skippable episodes of the series as a whole. At the time of its release, some reviewers noted that episode 4 was left out of screeners for the HBO series, which can sometimes indicate that an episode isn’t likely to be particularly notable or memorable in the long run.

According to recent reports, compared to the preceding episode’s fascinating, focused character study, the plot of “BJ and the AC” felt shapeless and saggy. The subplot involving Jill and her friends didn’t capture believable teen dialogue particularly well, while The Leftovers was a little too on-the-nose in its religious symbolism when it came to the Nativity scene’s missing Baby Jesus doll. Even the very concept of the police assigning Kevin to search for a toy doll stretched credulity for some viewers.

Industry observers note that however, especially when compared to controversial creator Damon Lindelof’s later Watchmen re-imagining from 2019, “BJ and the AC” is far from terrible. In fact, despite how heavy-handed its unsubtle symbolism is at times, the episode still finds time to make The Guilty Remnant a more authentically unsettling presence, while Kevin’s character flaws get more airtime in an outing that complicates his initial introduction.

Industry observers note that as The Leftovers continued, characters like Jill were fleshed out further and the show outdid itself so many times that “BJ and the AC” started to look like a comparably messy, weak early effort. However, in comparison to many of the show’s competitors, this episode of The Leftovers is still an immersive, intriguing entry into the show’s larger story.

Sources indicate that it is arguably unfortunate for the legacy of The Leftovers that HBO’s far shorter, dystopian, character-driven literary adaptation, Station Eleven, never released a single bad episode. However, The Leftovers lasted a lot longer and had many more episodes, so it is easy to forgive a few missteps from the typically stellar Mystery Box series.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that iFixit’s teardown of the upcoming Apple HomeView is now up, revealing a device that seems nearly impossible to take apart and repair.
  • Following last week’s launch of the Apple HomeView, iFixit today published its teardown of the device.
  • Contrary to recent teardowns, which found significant repairability improvements with greater component modularity and easier access to internal components, the HomeView put up a fight nearly all the way through.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that iFixit’s teardown of the upcoming Apple HomeView is now up, revealing a device that seems nearly impossible to take apart and repair. Watch it below.

Following last week’s launch of the Apple HomeView, iFixit today published its teardown of the device.

Contrary to recent teardowns, which found significant repairability improvements with greater component modularity and easier access to internal components, the HomeView put up a fight nearly all the way through.

With heavily glued or adhesive-bonded components, including the display, speakers, antennas, and logic board, the teardown proved particularly challenging, even after the adhesive securing the display’s speakers was soaked in isopropyl alcohol.

At one point, one of them broke apart during removal, while the logic board required considerable force to separate from the chassis due to the thermal adhesive holding it in place.

iFixit’s teardown covered the two HomeView variants: the tabletop model and the wall-mounted version. Interestingly, there are some internal differences between them, as the wall-mounted model has a slightly wider logic board to accommodate capacitors that are housed in the base of the tabletop version.

As a result, the wall-mounted HomeView also has smaller internal speakers, which helps explain the differences in their audio systems that Apple had already acknowledged at launch.

Back to the tabletop model, iFixit’s teardown also showed that separating the display from the base requires either specialized tools or extensive, potentially destructive disassembly of the display assembly, thanks to the way Apple routed the connecting cables through the pivot mechanism.

Once iFixit was in the base, however, there was some good news: the USB-C port is modular and relatively easy to access, as are the passive radiators and the board powering the lower assembly.

Still, an extremely short cable connecting the woofer to the board underneath made disassembly difficult, with iFixit questioning how anyone would be able to reconnect it during reassembly.

Percentage of Apple owners who are interested in repairing their device. 0.000001%.

According to recent reports, percentage of Apple owners who will actually try and repair their device. 0.00000001%.

Given all these repairability challenges, Shahram Mokhtari joked that while iFixit doesn’t have an official repairability scorecard for this category of device, he would give the Apple HomeView a “BEEP this thing” out of 10.

7 Masterpiece Fantasy Book Series, Ranked

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2038 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Collider

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that starting a fantasy series is a major commitment.
  • Sources indicate that by the time the story actually gets going, most people have already put the book down.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, feel free to connect with him or check out his work. He's everywhere — Upwork, YouTube, Spotify, SoundCloud, Collider, LinkedIn, Instagram.

Sources indicate that starting a fantasy series is a major commitment. Some of the genre’s most beloved sagas run for thousands of pages, with maps, family trees, and made-up languages that can feel overwhelming before the story even begins. So many fantasy series get lost in endless exposition and keep bombarding readers with information before giving them a single reason to care.

Sources indicate that by the time the story actually gets going, most people have already put the book down. However, a good fantasy series knows exactly how to strike the balance between building a rich world and telling a compelling story with characters that the readers instantly fall in love with. Here are the seven greatest fantasy book series of all time that can turn even the most casual of readers into lifelong enthusiasts of the genre.

Industry observers note that robert Jordan’s The Wheel of Time is one of the most expansive fantasy series ever written — one that rewards its readers’ commitment every step of the way. The story begins in a quiet farming village called the Two Rivers, where a mysterious woman named Moiraine arrives searching for someone. She belongs to the Aes Sedai, a powerful order of women who can channel magic. Moiraine believes that one of the village’s young men, possibly a humble shepherd named Rand al’Thor, is the Dragon Reborn: a legendary figure destined to face the Dark One. The problem is that the same prophecy notes the Dragon could also break the world all over again.

Industry observers note that the series spans 14 main novels, and its world is magnificent in scope, with dozens of nations and cultures that all feel distinct instead of ever blurring together. The story doesn’t leave a single loose thread and handles its big question of destiny with immense responsibility. Rand al’Thor has to carry the weight of a fate he never asked for, and since male magic-users in this world slowly go mad, his power is as much a curse as a gift. The middle books are famously slow, but the payoff is worth it in the end. Jordan passed away before he could finish the series, and author Brandon Sanderson completed the final three books using his notes. The Wheel of Time remains a towering achievement, with an ending that ties together 14 books’ worth of prophecies in a way that left longtime fans completely satisfied.

Brandon Sanderson is one of the most popular fantasy authors still writing today, and The Stormlight Archive is his magnum opus. The series is set on Roshar, a harsh world battered by massive storms so powerful that the plants and animals have evolved to survive them. Its heroes are a group of broken people. Kaladin is a former soldier sold into slavery, while Shallan is a young scholar hiding a dangerous secret. Dalinar is a battle-hardened warlord trying to make up for the terrible things he’s done. As an ancient threat returns, each of them is drawn toward the long-lost order of warrior-magicians known as the Knights Radiant.

It has been revealed that for a plot so grand, The Stormlight Archive makes sure that it never takes away from the characters’ struggles. Kaladin’s fight with depression is one of the most honest portrayals of mental health in fantasy, and it grounds the world’s fantastical elements in something that plenty of readers can relate to. Sanderson is also famous for his carefully designed magic systems, which follow clear rules and make every battle feel like a clever puzzle. The books are complex, but they move fast, and each one builds to a huge climax that fans call a “Sanderlanche.” Five books in the series are out so far, with five more planned, which means the best may still be yet to come. The Stormlight Archive is the series modern fantasy fans can’t stop recommending, and for good reason.

Sources indicate that discworld proves that fantasy doesn’t have to take itself seriously to be brilliant. Terry Pratchett’s series is set on a flat world that rests on the backs of four elephants, which in turn stand on a giant turtle swimming through space. Over 41 novels, Pratchett fills this ridiculous world with unforgettable characters, including the bumbling wizard Rincewind and Commander Sam Vimes of the city watch. Death himself is a recurring character in the story, who speaks entirely in capital letters.

It has been revealed that the genius of Discworld is that it starts as a fantasy parody and slowly turns into something much more meaningful. Pratchett uses his silly world to poke fun at politics, religion, and human nature, and his jokes often sneak up on readers with surprisingly moving ideas. The series also has a unique structure, since it is made up of several smaller storylines that can be read in almost any order, which makes it easy for newcomers to jump in at any given time. Pratchett was diagnosed with Alzheimer’s later in life but kept writing until he died in 2015. Discworld is funny and wise in equal measure, and it’s the most comforting series on this list.

Four worlds and four completely different ideas of what a good life looks like. This is where you belong, what it would ask of you, and what you would get back in return.

According to recent reports, you belong somewhere old enough that the mountains have names and somebody can still tell you who gave them. Middle-earth is for people who think the right thing is worth doing even when it will not be finished in their lifetime.

You want the sea, a crew, and absolutely nobody telling you where you are allowed to go. The Grand Line is the world for people whose main ambition in life is finding out what is over there.

Industry observers note that you would rather be feared and useful than liked and useless. The Continent is a world where the monsters are the straightforward part of the job and the people are where it all gets complicated.

You want the myths to be real and loose in the actual world, and you want to find out at about thirteen that you were never anywhere near as ordinary as everybody kept telling you.

Long before Game of Thrones took over TV, George R.R. Martin’s A Song of Ice and Fire had already started reshaping the fantasy genre. The story is set in Westeros, where powerful noble families fight a brutal war for control of the Iron Throne. The Starks and Lannisters scheme and battle, while the exiled princess named Daenerys Targaryen is building an army across the sea. All of that is threatened by an ancient danger that is stirring in the frozen north. Of course, that is only half the story, and A Song of Ice and Fire covers a lot more ground, with storylines that converge and diverge all the time. Every chapter is told from a different character’s point of view, so readers see the war and power struggle from all sides.

It has been revealed that the biggest shock of the series is how willing Martin is to break the rules. Characters who seem like the hero can die at any moment, and good people often make terrible choices. That realism made the books feel unpredictable in a way fantasy rarely had before. Martin also writes morally gray characters better than almost anyone, and some of the most hated figures in the early books slowly become fan favorites, which is a testament to the author’s brilliant storytelling. The big catch is that the series is still unfinished, with fans waiting more than a decade for the next book, The Winds of Winter. Even so, A Song of Ice and Fire is the series that made fantasy feel dangerous, and its influence is everywhere.

According to recent reports, decades before Hogwarts, Ursula K. Le Guin sent a young boy to wizard school. A Wizard of Earthsea follows Ged, a goatherd with a natural gift for magic who grows up on an island in a vast world made almost entirely of oceans and small archipelagos. The only problem is that Ged knows how good he is, and his pride often leads him right into dangerous situations. While he is still a student, Ged tries to prove himself by performing a forbidden spell and accidentally unleashes a terrifying shadow creature into the world. He spends the rest of the novel being hunted by it, until he finally has to turn around and face it.

What makes Earthsea special is how thoughtful yet simple it is compared to most fantasy books. In this world, magic works by knowing the true name of things, and every spell comes with a cost, so even the most powerful wizards are careful with their gifts. Le Guin was also ahead of her time in deliberately making most of her characters, including Ged, people of color. All the books in the series are short and beautifully written, and they explore major ideas like balance and death in a way that’s easy to follow. Earthsea has inspired countless writers, and it’s a must-read for anyone who wants to understand where modern fantasy came from.

Sources indicate that everyone knows about Harry Potter at this point, because it has become a permanent part of modern pop culture. J.K. Rowling’s seven-book series follows Harry, an orphan who discovers on his 11th birthday that he’s a wizard and has a place at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. There, he makes lifelong friends in Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger, and he slowly learns the truth about the dark wizard Lord Voldemort, who killed his parents and has never stopped trying to kill him.

The reason why the Harry Potter series still resonates with the entire world is that it grows up with its readers. The first books are full of wonder and whimsy, but the series gets darker and more mature with every installment, until the final chapters cover a full-blown war. Rowling also had a gift for mystery, and each book is built around a central mystery that keeps readers guessing until the last chapter. The friendship between Harry, Ron, and Hermione is the heart of this fantastical story that readers just can’t get enough of. The series turned an entire generation into readers, and with a new HBO series on the way in December 2026, Harry Potter is not losing its magic anytime soon.

The Lord of the Rings is the series that has defined practically every other book on this list. J.R.R. Tolkien’s epic is often published as three volumes, but the author actually wrote it as a single story. Now, he obviously didn’t invent elves, dwarves, or epic quests, but he turned them into the blueprint the entire genre still follows. The story picks up years after The Hobbit, when a young hobbit named Frodo Baggins learns that the plain gold ring his uncle Bilbo left him is actually the One Ring, forged by the Dark Lord Sauron to control the world. The only way to stop Sauron is to carry the Ring into his kingdom of Mordor and throw it into the volcano where it was made. Frodo then sets out with a fellowship of companions, including the wizard Gandalf and his loyal friend Samwise Gamgee, as war spreads across Middle-earth.

It has been revealed that what makes the series so powerful is that its real villain isn’t just Sauron, but the Ring itself, which slowly tempts and corrupts anyone who holds it. Tolkien fought in World War I, and his experience highlights in the way the books treat war as something that leaves lasting scars. The world Tolkien creates feels extremely real. Middle-earth comes with its own languages and thousands of years of history. That depth gives The Lord of the Rings a sense of age and meaning like no other. Peter Jackson’s films brought the franchise to a upcoming generation, but nothing comes close to the brilliance of the source material.
